# Authentication

* API Key (clientId)
    - Parameter Name: **PLAID-CLIENT-ID**, in: header.

* API Key (plaidVersion)
    - Parameter Name: **Plaid-Version**, in: header.

* API Key (secret)
    - Parameter Name: **PLAID-SECRET**, in: header.

<h1 id="the-plaid-api-plaid">plaid</h1>

The Plaid API

## Retrieve real-time balance data

<a id="opIdaccountsBalanceGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/accounts/balance/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "account_ids": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/balance/get`

The `/accounts/balance/get` endpoint returns the real-time balance for each of an Item's accounts. While other endpoints may return a balance object, only `/accounts/balance/get` forces the available and current balance fields to be refreshed rather than cached. This endpoint can be used for existing Items that were added via any of Plaid’s other products. This endpoint can be used as long as Link has been initialized with any other product, `balance` itself is not a product that can be used to initialize Link. As this endpoint triggers a synchronous request for fresh data, latency may be higher than for other Plaid endpoints; if you encounter errors, you may find it necessary to adjust your timeout period when making requests.

<a href="/api/products/balance/#accountsbalanceget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-real-time-balance-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AccountsBalanceGetRequest](#schemaaccountsbalancegetrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[AccountsBalanceGetRequestOptions](#schemaaccountsbalancegetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/accounts/balance/get` results.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Retrieve accounts

<a id="opIdaccountsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/accounts/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "account_ids": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/get`

The `/accounts/get` endpoint can be used to retrieve a list of accounts associated with any linked Item. Plaid will only return active bank accounts — that is, accounts that are not closed and are capable of carrying a balance.
For items that went through the updated account selection pane, this endpoint only returns accounts that were permissioned by the user when they initially created the Item. If a user creates a new account after the initial link, you can capture this event through the [`NEW_ACCOUNTS_AVAILABLE`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/items/#new_accounts_available) webhook and then use Link's [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode/) to request that the user share this new account with you.

This endpoint retrieves cached information, rather than extracting fresh information from the institution. As a result, balances returned may not be up-to-date; for realtime balance information, use `/accounts/balance/get` instead. Note that some information is nullable.

<a href="/api/accounts/#accountsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AccountsGetRequest](#schemaaccountsgetrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[AccountsGetRequestOptions](#schemaaccountsgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/accounts/get` results.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

`POST /application/get`

Allows financial institutions to retrieve information about Plaid clients for the purpose of building control-tower experiences

## Create Asset Report Audit Copy

<a id="opIdassetReportAuditCopyCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/audit_copy/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "auditor_id": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/audit_copy/create`

Plaid can provide an Audit Copy of any Asset Report directly to a participating third party on your behalf. For example, Plaid can supply an Audit Copy directly to Fannie Mae on your behalf if you participate in the Day 1 Certainty™ program. An Audit Copy contains the same underlying data as the Asset Report.

To grant access to an Audit Copy, use the `/asset_report/audit_copy/create` endpoint to create an `audit_copy_token` and then pass that token to the third party who needs access. Each third party has its own `auditor_id`, for example `fannie_mae`. You’ll need to create a separate Audit Copy for each third party to whom you want to grant access to the Report.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportaudit_copycreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "auditor_id": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-asset-report-audit-copy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportAuditCopyCreateRequest](#schemaassetreportauditcopycreaterequest)|true|none|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)|true|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|
|» auditor_id|body|string|false|The `auditor_id` of the third party with whom you would like to share the Asset Report.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "audit_copy_token": "a-sandbox-3TAU2CWVYBDVRHUCAAAI27ULU4",
  "request_id": "Iam3b"
}
```

<h3 id="create-asset-report-audit-copy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AssetReportAuditCopyCreateResponse](#schemaassetreportauditcopycreateresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Retrieve an Asset Report Audit Copy

<a id="opIdassetReportAuditCopyGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/audit_copy/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "audit_copy_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/audit_copy/get`

`/asset_report/audit_copy/get` allows auditors to get a copy of an Asset Report that was previously shared via the `/asset_report/audit_copy/create` endpoint.  The caller of `/asset_report/audit_copy/create` must provide the `audit_copy_token` to the auditor.  This token can then be used to call `/asset_report/audit_copy/create`.

<a href="/none/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audit_copy_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-an-asset-report-audit-copy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportAuditCopyGetRequest](#schemaassetreportauditcopygetrequest)|true|none|
|» audit_copy_token|body|string|true|The `audit_copy_token` granting access to the Audit Copy you would like to get.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Remove Asset Report Audit Copy

<a id="opIdassetReportAuditCopyRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/audit_copy/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "audit_copy_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/audit_copy/remove`

The `/asset_report/audit_copy/remove` endpoint allows you to remove an Audit Copy. Removing an Audit Copy invalidates the `audit_copy_token` associated with it, meaning both you and any third parties holding the token will no longer be able to use it to access Report data. Items associated with the Asset Report, the Asset Report itself and other Audit Copies of it are not affected and will remain accessible after removing the given Audit Copy.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportaudit_copyremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audit_copy_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-asset-report-audit-copy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportAuditCopyRemoveRequest](#schemaassetreportauditcopyremoverequest)|true|none|
|» audit_copy_token|body|string|true|The `audit_copy_token` granting access to the Audit Copy you would like to revoke.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "removed": true,
  "request_id": "m8MDnv9okwxFNBV"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-asset-report-audit-copy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AssetReportAuditCopyRemoveResponse](#schemaassetreportauditcopyremoveresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Create an Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_tokens": [
      "string"
    ],
    "client_id": "string",
    "days_requested": 0,
    "options": {
      "add_ons": [
        "investments"
      ],
      "client_report_id": "string",
      "include_fast_report": true,
      "products": [
        "string"
      ],
      "user": {
        "client_user_id": "string",
        "email": "string",
        "first_name": "string",
        "last_name": "string",
        "middle_name": "string",
        "phone_number": "string",
        "ssn": "string"
      },
      "webhook": "string"
    },
    "report_type": "VERIFICATION_OF_EMPLOYMENT",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/create`

The `/asset_report/create` endpoint initiates the process of creating an Asset Report, which can then be retrieved by passing the `asset_report_token` return value to the `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` endpoints.

The Asset Report takes some time to be created and is not available immediately after calling `/asset_report/create`. When the Asset Report is ready to be retrieved using `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get`, Plaid will fire a `PRODUCT_READY` webhook. For full details of the webhook schema, see [Asset Report webhooks](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/assets/#webhooks).

The `/asset_report/create` endpoint creates an Asset Report at a moment in time. Asset Reports are immutable. To get an updated Asset Report, use the `/asset_report/refresh` endpoint.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "client_id": "string",
  "days_requested": 0,
  "options": {
    "add_ons": [
      "investments"
    ],
    "client_report_id": "string",
    "include_fast_report": true,
    "products": [
      "string"
    ],
    "user": {
      "client_user_id": "string",
      "email": "string",
      "first_name": "string",
      "last_name": "string",
      "middle_name": "string",
      "phone_number": "string",
      "ssn": "string"
    },
    "webhook": "string"
  },
  "report_type": "VERIFICATION_OF_EMPLOYMENT",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportCreateRequest](#schemaassetreportcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_tokens|body|[[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)]|true|An array of access tokens corresponding to the Items that will be included in the report. The `assets` product must have been initialized for the Items during link; the Assets product cannot be added after initialization.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» days_requested|body|integer|true|The maximum integer number of days of history to include in the Asset Report. If using Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty, `days_requested` must be at least 61 for new originations or at least 31 for refinancings.<br><br>An Asset Report requested with "Additional History" (that is, with more than 61 days of transaction history) will incur an Additional History fee.|
|» options|body|[AssetReportCreateRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportcreaterequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/asset_report/create` results. If provided, must be non-`null`. The optional `user` object is required for the report to be eligible for Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty program.|
|» report_type|body|[FreddieReportType](#schemafreddiereporttype)|false|When set to `VERIFICATION_OF_EMPLOYMENT` and the Asset Report is added to an Audit Copy Token, the Asset Report will be retrieved by Freddie Mac in the Verification Of Employment (VOE) version instead of the default Verification Of Assets (VOA) version.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» report_type|VERIFICATION_OF_EMPLOYMENT|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "asset_report_id": "1f414183-220c-44f5-b0c8-bc0e6d4053bb",
  "asset_report_token": "assets-sandbox-6f12f5bb-22dd-4855-b918-f47ec439198a",
  "request_id": "Iam3b"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-asset-report-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AssetReportCreateResponse](#schemaassetreportcreateresponse)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Filter Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportFilter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/filter \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "account_ids_to_exclude": [
      "string"
    ],
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/filter`

By default, an Asset Report will contain all of the accounts on a given Item. In some cases, you may not want the Asset Report to contain all accounts. For example, you might have the end user choose which accounts are relevant in Link using the Account Select view, which you can enable in the dashboard. Or, you might always exclude certain account types or subtypes, which you can identify by using the `/accounts/get` endpoint. To narrow an Asset Report to only a subset of accounts, use the `/asset_report/filter` endpoint.

To exclude certain Accounts from an Asset Report, first use the `/asset_report/create` endpoint to create the report, then send the `asset_report_token` along with a list of `account_ids` to exclude to the `/asset_report/filter` endpoint, to create a new Asset Report which contains only a subset of the original Asset Report's data.

Because Asset Reports are immutable, calling `/asset_report/filter` does not alter the original Asset Report in any way; rather, `/asset_report/filter` creates a new Asset Report with a new token and id. Asset Reports created via `/asset_report/filter` do not contain new Asset data, and are not billed.

Plaid will fire a [`PRODUCT_READY`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/assets/#product_ready) webhook once generation of the filtered Asset Report has completed.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportfilter">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_ids_to_exclude": [
    "string"
  ],
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="filter-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportFilterRequest](#schemaassetreportfilterrequest)|true|none|
|» account_ids_to_exclude|body|[string]|true|The accounts to exclude from the Asset Report, identified by `account_id`.|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)|true|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "asset_report_id": "fdc09207-0cef-4d88-b5eb-0d970758ebd9",
  "asset_report_token": "assets-sandbox-bc410c6a-4653-4c75-985c-e757c3497c5c",
  "request_id": "qEg07"
}
```

<h3 id="filter-asset-report-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AssetReportFilterResponse](#schemaassetreportfilterresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Retrieve an Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "fast_report": false,
    "include_insights": false,
    "options": {
      "days_to_include": 0
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/get`

The `/asset_report/get` endpoint retrieves the Asset Report in JSON format. Before calling `/asset_report/get`, you must first create the Asset Report using `/asset_report/create` (or filter an Asset Report using `/asset_report/filter`) and then wait for the [`PRODUCT_READY`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/assets/#product_ready) webhook to fire, indicating that the Report is ready to be retrieved.

By default, an Asset Report includes transaction descriptions as returned by the bank, as opposed to parsed and categorized by Plaid. You can also receive cleaned and categorized transactions, as well as additional insights like merchant name or location information. We call this an Asset Report with Insights. An Asset Report with Insights provides transaction category, location, and merchant information in addition to the transaction strings provided in a standard Asset Report.

To retrieve an Asset Report with Insights, call the `/asset_report/get` endpoint with `include_insights` set to `true`.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "fast_report": false,
  "include_insights": false,
  "options": {
    "days_to_include": 0
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-an-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportGetRequest](#schemaassetreportgetrequest)|true|none|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)|true|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» fast_report|body|boolean|false|`true` to fetch "fast" version of asset report. Defaults to false if omitted.|
|» include_insights|body|boolean|false|`true` if you would like to retrieve the Asset Report with Insights, `false` otherwise. This field defaults to `false` if omitted.|
|» options|body|[AssetReportGetRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter or add data to `/asset_report/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Retrieve a PDF Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportPdfGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/pdf/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "days_to_include": 0
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/pdf/get`

The `/asset_report/pdf/get` endpoint retrieves the Asset Report in PDF format. Before calling `/asset_report/pdf/get`, you must first create the Asset Report using `/asset_report/create` (or filter an Asset Report using `/asset_report/filter`) and then wait for the [`PRODUCT_READY`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/assets/#product_ready) webhook to fire, indicating that the Report is ready to be retrieved.

The response to `/asset_report/pdf/get` is the PDF binary data. The `request_id`  is returned in the `Plaid-Request-ID` header.

[View a sample PDF Asset Report](https://plaid.com/documents/sample-asset-report.pdf).

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportpdfget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "days_to_include": 0
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-pdf-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportPDFGetRequest](#schemaassetreportpdfgetrequest)|true|none|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)|true|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[AssetReportPDFGetRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportpdfgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter or add data to `/asset_report/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

<h3 id="retrieve-a-pdf-asset-report-responses">Responses</h3>

## Refresh an Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportRefresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/refresh \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "days_requested": 0,
    "options": {
      "client_report_id": "string",
      "user": {
        "client_user_id": "string",
        "email": "string",
        "first_name": "string",
        "last_name": "string",
        "middle_name": "string",
        "phone_number": "string",
        "ssn": "string"
      },
      "webhook": "string"
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/refresh`

An Asset Report is an immutable snapshot of a user's assets. In order to "refresh" an Asset Report you created previously, you can use the `/asset_report/refresh` endpoint to create a new Asset Report based on the old one, but with the most recent data available.

The new Asset Report will contain the same Items as the original Report, as well as the same filters applied by any call to `/asset_report/filter`. By default, the new Asset Report will also use the same parameters you submitted with your original `/asset_report/create` request, but the original `days_requested` value and the values of any parameters in the `options` object can be overridden with new values. To change these arguments, simply supply new values for them in your request to `/asset_report/refresh`. Submit an empty string ("") for any previously-populated fields you would like set as empty.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportrefresh">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "days_requested": 0,
  "options": {
    "client_report_id": "string",
    "user": {
      "client_user_id": "string",
      "email": "string",
      "first_name": "string",
      "last_name": "string",
      "middle_name": "string",
      "phone_number": "string",
      "ssn": "string"
    },
    "webhook": "string"
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="refresh-an-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportRefreshRequest](#schemaassetreportrefreshrequest)|true|none|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportRefreshAssetReportToken](#schemaassetreportrefreshassetreporttoken)|true|The `asset_report_token` returned by the original call to `/asset_report/create`|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» days_requested|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of days of history to include in the Asset Report. Must be an integer. If not specified, the value from the original call to `/asset_report/create` will be used.|
|» options|body|[AssetReportRefreshRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportrefreshrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/asset_report/refresh` results. If provided, cannot be `null`. If not specified, the `options` from the original call to `/asset_report/create` will be used.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "asset_report_id": "c33ebe8b-6a63-4d74-a83d-d39791231ac0",
  "asset_report_token": "assets-sandbox-8218d5f8-6d6d-403d-92f5-13a9afaa4398",
  "request_id": "NBZaq"
}
```

## Delete an Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/remove`

The `/item/remove` endpoint allows you to invalidate an `access_token`, meaning you will not be able to create new Asset Reports with it. Removing an Item does not affect any Asset Reports or Audit Copies you have already created, which will remain accessible until you remove them specifically.

The `/asset_report/remove` endpoint allows you to remove an Asset Report. Removing an Asset Report invalidates its `asset_report_token`, meaning you will no longer be able to use it to access Report data or create new Audit Copies. Removing an Asset Report does not affect the underlying Items, but does invalidate any `audit_copy_tokens` associated with the Asset Report.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportRemoveRequest](#schemaassetreportremoverequest)|true|none|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)|true|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "removed": true,
  "request_id": "I6zHN"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AssetReportRemoveResponse](#schemaassetreportremoveresponse)|

</aside>

## Retrieve auth data

<a id="opIdauthGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/auth/get \
  -X POST \

      ]
    },

  }'
```

`POST /auth/get`

The `/auth/get` endpoint returns the bank account and bank identification numbers (such as routing numbers, for US accounts) associated with an Item's checking and savings accounts, along with high-level account data and balances when available.

Note: This request may take some time to complete if `auth` was not specified as an initial product when creating the Item. This is because Plaid must communicate directly with the institution to retrieve the data.

Versioning note: In API version 2017-03-08, the schema of the `numbers` object returned by this endpoint is substantially different. For details, see [Plaid API versioning](https://plaid.com/docs/api/versioning/#version-2018-05-22).

<a href="/api/products/auth/#authget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

|body|body|[AuthGetRequest](#schemaauthgetrequest)|true|none|

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Get balance of your Bank Transfer account

<a id="opIdbankTransferBalanceGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bank_transfer/balance/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "origination_account_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /bank_transfer/balance/get`

Use the `/bank_transfer/balance/get` endpoint to see the available balance in your bank transfer account. Debit transfers increase this balance once their status is posted. Credit transfers decrease this balance when they are created.

The transactable balance shows the amount in your account that you are able to use for transfers, and is essentially your available balance minus your minimum balance.

Note that this endpoint can only be used with FBO accounts, when using Bank Transfers in the Full Service configuration. It cannot be used on your own account when using Bank Transfers in the BTS Platform configuration.

<a href="/bank-transfers/reference#bank_transferbalanceget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "origination_account_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|If multiple origination accounts are available, `origination_account_id` must be used to specify the account for which balance will be returned.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

```json
  },
```

<h3 id="create-a-bank-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BankTransferCreateRequest](#schemabanktransfercreaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[BankTransferAccessToken](#schemabanktransferaccesstoken)|true|The Plaid `access_token` for the account that will be debited or credited.|
|» account_id|body|string|true|The Plaid `account_id` for the account that will be debited or credited.|
|» ach_class|body|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|» amount|body|[BankTransferAmount](#schemabanktransferamount)|true|The amount of the bank transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» custom_tag|body|string \| null|false|An arbitrary string provided by the client for storage with the bank transfer. May be up to 100 characters.|
|» description|body|string|true|The transfer description. Maximum of 10 characters.|
|» idempotency_key|body|[BankTransferIdempotencyKey](#schemabanktransferidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique bank transfer. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a bank transfer fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single bank transfer is created.|
|» iso_currency_code|body|string|true|The currency of the transfer amount – should be set to "USD".|
|» metadata|body|[BankTransferMetadata](#schemabanktransfermetadata)|false|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|» network|body|[BankTransferNetwork](#schemabanktransfernetwork)|true|The network or rails used for the transfer. Valid options are `ach`, `same-day-ach`, or `wire`.|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|Plaid’s unique identifier for the origination account for this transfer. If you have more than one origination account, this value must be specified. Otherwise, this field should be left blank.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» type|body|[BankTransferType](#schemabanktransfertype)|true|The type of bank transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|
|» user|body|[BankTransferUser](#schemabanktransferuser)|true|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|

|» network|wire|

## List bank transfer events

<a id="opIdbankTransferEventList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bank_transfer/event/list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "account_id": "string",
    "bank_transfer_id": "string",
    "bank_transfer_type": "debit",
    "client_id": "string",
    "count": 25,
    "direction": "inbound",
    "end_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "event_types": [
      "pending"
    ],
    "offset": 0,
    "origination_account_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "start_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /bank_transfer/event/list`

Use the `/bank_transfer/event/list` endpoint to get a list of Plaid-initiated ACH or bank transfer events based on specified filter criteria. When using Auth with micro-deposit verification enabled, this endpoint can be used to fetch status updates on ACH micro-deposits. For more details, see [micro-deposit events](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/microdeposit-events/).

<a href="/api/products/auth#bank_transfereventlist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_id": "string",
  "bank_transfer_id": "string",
  "bank_transfer_type": "debit",
  "client_id": "string",
  "count": 25,
  "direction": "inbound",
  "end_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "event_types": [
    "pending"
  ],
  "offset": 0,
  "origination_account_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "start_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="list-bank-transfer-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BankTransferEventListRequest](#schemabanktransfereventlistrequest)|true|none|
|» account_id|body|string \| null|false|The account ID to get events for all transactions to/from an account.|
|» bank_transfer_id|body|string \| null|false|Plaid’s unique identifier for a bank transfer.|
|» bank_transfer_type|body|[BankTransferEventListBankTransferType](#schemabanktransfereventlistbanktransfertype)|false|The type of bank transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into your origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of your origination account.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of bank transfer events to return. If the number of events matching the above parameters is greater than `count`, the most recent events will be returned.|
|» direction|body|[BankTransferEventListDirection](#schemabanktransfereventlistdirection)|false|Indicates the direction of the transfer: `outbound`: for API-initiated transfers<br>`inbound`: for payments received by the FBO account.|
|» end_date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The end datetime of bank transfers to list. This should be in RFC 3339 format (i.e. `2019-12-06T22:35:49Z`)|
|» event_types|body|[[BankTransferEventType](#schemabanktransfereventtype)]|false|Filter events by event type.|
|» offset|body|integer \| null|false|The offset into the list of bank transfer events. When `count`=25 and `offset`=0, the first 25 events will be returned. When `count`=25 and `offset`=25, the next 25 bank transfer events will be returned.|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|The origination account ID to get events for transfers from a specific origination account.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» start_date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The start datetime of bank transfers to list. This should be in RFC 3339 format (i.e. `2019-12-06T22:35:49Z`)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» bank_transfer_type|debit|
|» bank_transfer_type|credit|
|» bank_transfer_type|null|
|» direction|inbound|
|» direction|outbound|
|» direction|null|
|» event_types|pending|
|» event_types|cancelled|
|» event_types|failed|
|» event_types|posted|
|» event_types|reversed|

## Sync bank transfer events

<a id="opIdbankTransferEventSync"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bank_transfer/event/sync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "after_id": 0,
    "client_id": "string",
    "count": 25,
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /bank_transfer/event/sync`

`/bank_transfer/event/sync` allows you to request up to the next 25 Plaid-initiated bank transfer events that happened after a specific `event_id`. When using Auth with micro-deposit verification enabled, this endpoint can be used to fetch status updates on ACH micro-deposits. For more details, see [micro-deposit events](https://www.plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/microdeposit-events/).

<a href="/api/products/auth/#bank_transfereventsync">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "after_id": 0,
  "client_id": "string",
  "count": 25,
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="sync-bank-transfer-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BankTransferEventSyncRequest](#schemabanktransfereventsyncrequest)|true|none|
|» after_id|body|integer|true|The latest (largest) `event_id` fetched via the sync endpoint, or 0 initially.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of bank transfer events to return.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

`POST /bank_transfer/list`

## Migrate account into Bank Transfers

<a id="opIdbankTransferMigrateAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bank_transfer/migrate_account \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "account_number": "string",
    "account_type": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "routing_number": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "wire_routing_number": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /bank_transfer/migrate_account`

As an alternative to adding Items via Link, you can also use the `/bank_transfer/migrate_account` endpoint to migrate known account and routing numbers to Plaid Items.  Note that Items created in this way are not compatible with endpoints for other products, such as `/accounts/balance/get`, and can only be used with Bank Transfer endpoints.  If you require access to other endpoints, create the Item through Link instead.  Access to `/bank_transfer/migrate_account` is not enabled by default; to obtain access, contact your Plaid Account Manager.

<a href="/bank-transfers/reference#bank_transfermigrate_account">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_number": "string",
  "account_type": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "routing_number": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "wire_routing_number": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="migrate-account-into-bank-transfers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BankTransferMigrateAccountRequest](#schemabanktransfermigrateaccountrequest)|true|none|
|» account_number|body|string|true|The user's account number.|
|» account_type|body|string|true|The type of the bank account (`checking` or `savings`).|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» routing_number|body|string|true|The user's routing number.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» wire_routing_number|body|string|false|The user's wire transfer routing number. This is the ABA number; for some institutions, this may differ from the ACH number used in `routing_number`.|

```bash
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "count": 25,
    "end_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "origination_account_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",

  }'
```

`POST /bank_transfer/sweep/list`

The `/bank_transfer/sweep/list` endpoint fetches information about the sweeps matching the given filters.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/#bank_transfersweeplist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "count": 25,
  "end_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "origination_account_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "start_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="list-sweeps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BankTransferSweepListRequest](#schemabanktransfersweeplistrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of sweeps to return.|
|» end_time|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The end datetime of sweeps to return (RFC 3339 format).|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|If multiple origination accounts are available, `origination_account_id` must be used to specify the account that the sweeps belong to.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» start_time|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The start datetime of sweeps to return (RFC 3339 format).|

## Create transaction category rule

<a id="opIdtransactionsRulesCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/beta/transactions/rules/v1/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

    "personal_finance_category": "FOOD_AND_DRINK_FAST_FOOD",
    "rule_details": {
      "field": "NAME",
      "query": "Burger Shack",
      "type": "SUBSTRING_MATCH"
    },
    "secret": "79g03eoofwl8240v776r2h667442119"
  }'
```

`POST /beta/transactions/rules/v1/create`

The `/transactions/rules/v1/create` endpoint creates transaction categorization rules.

Rules will be applied on the Item's transactions returned in `/transactions/get` response.

The product is currently in beta. To request access, contact transactions-feedback@plaid.com.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "access-sandbox-71e02f71-0960-4a27-abd2-5631e04f2175",
  "client_id": "7f57eb3d2a9j6480121fx361",
  "personal_finance_category": "FOOD_AND_DRINK_FAST_FOOD",
  "rule_details": {
    "field": "NAME",
    "query": "Burger Shack",
    "type": "SUBSTRING_MATCH"
  },
  "secret": "79g03eoofwl8240v776r2h667442119"
}
```

<h3 id="create-transaction-category-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransactionsRulesCreateRequest](#schematransactionsrulescreaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» personal_finance_category|body|string|true|Personal finance detailed category.<br><br>See the [`taxonomy csv file`](https://plaid.com/documents/transactions-personal-finance-category-taxonomy.csv) for a full list of personal finance categories.<br>|
|» rule_details|body|[TransactionsRuleDetails](#schematransactionsruledetails)|true|A representation of transactions rule details.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Create Asset or Income Report Audit Copy Token

<a id="opIdcreditAuditCopyTokenCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/audit_copy_token/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "report_tokens": [
      "string"
    ],
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/audit_copy_token/create`

Plaid can create an Audit Copy token of an Asset Report and/or Income Report to share with participating Government Sponsored Entity (GSE). If you participate in the Day 1 Certainty™ program, Plaid can supply an Audit Copy token directly to Fannie Mae on your behalf. An Audit Copy token contains the same underlying data as the Asset Report and/or Income Report (result of /credit/payroll_income/get).

Use the `/credit/audit_copy_token/create` endpoint to create an `audit_copy_token` and then pass that token to the GSE who needs access.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditaudit_copy_tokencreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "report_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-asset-or-income-report-audit-copy-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditAuditCopyTokenCreateRequest](#schemacreditauditcopytokencreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» report_tokens|body|[string]|true|List of report tokens; can include both Asset Report tokens and Income Report tokens.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "audit_copy_token": "a-production-3tau2cwvybdvrhucaaai27ulu4",
  "request_id": "Iam3b"
}
```

<h3 id="create-asset-or-income-report-audit-copy-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[CreditAuditCopyTokenCreateResponse](#schemacreditauditcopytokencreateresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Remove an Audit Copy token

<a id="opIdcreditReportAuditCopyRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/audit_copy_token/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "audit_copy_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/audit_copy_token/remove`

The `/credit/audit_copy_token/remove` endpoint allows you to remove an Audit Copy. Removing an Audit Copy invalidates the `audit_copy_token` associated with it, meaning both you and any third parties holding the token will no longer be able to use it to access Report data. Items associated with the Report data and other Audit Copies of it are not affected and will remain accessible after removing the given Audit Copy.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditaudit_copy_tokenremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audit_copy_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-an-audit-copy-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditAuditCopyTokenRemoveRequest](#schemacreditauditcopytokenremoverequest)|true|none|
|» audit_copy_token|body|string|true|The `audit_copy_token` granting access to the Audit Copy you would like to revoke.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "removed": true,
  "request_id": "m8MDnv9okwxFNBV"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-an-audit-copy-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[CreditAuditCopyTokenRemoveResponse](#schemacreditauditcopytokenremoveresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Update an Audit Copy Token

<a id="opIdcreditAuditCopyTokenUpdate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/audit_copy_token/update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "audit_copy_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "report_tokens": [
      "string"
    ],
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/audit_copy_token/update`

The `/credit/audit_copy_token/update` endpoint updates the Audit Copy Token by adding the report tokens in the `report_tokens` field to the `audit_copy_token`. If the Audit Copy Token already contains a report of a certain type, it will be replaced with the token provided in the `report_tokens` field.

<a href="/none/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audit_copy_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "report_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-audit-copy-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditAuditCopyTokenUpdateRequest](#schemacreditauditcopytokenupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» audit_copy_token|body|string|true|The `audit_copy_token` you would like to update.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» report_tokens|body|[[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)]|true|Array of tokens which the specified Audit Copy Token will be updated with. The types of token supported are asset report token and employment report token. There can be at most 1 of each type can be in the array.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "eYupqX1mZkEuQRx",
  "updated": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-audit-copy-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[CreditAuditCopyTokenUpdateResponse](#schemacreditauditcopytokenupdateresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Check income verification eligibility and optimize conversion

<a id="opIdcreditPayrollIncomePrecheck"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/payroll_income/precheck \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_tokens": [
      "string"
    ],
    "client_id": "string",
    "employer": {
      "address": {
        "city": "string",
        "country": "string",
        "postal_code": "string",
        "region": "string",
        "street": "string"
      },
      "name": "string",
      "tax_id": "string",
      "url": "string"
    },
    "payroll_institution": {
      "name": "string"
    },
    "secret": "string",
    "us_military_info": {
      "branch": "string",
      "is_active_duty": true
    },
    "user_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/payroll_income/precheck`

`/credit/payroll_income/precheck` is an optional endpoint that can be called before initializing a Link session for income verification. It evaluates whether a given user is supportable by digital income verification. If the user is eligible for digital verification, that information will be associated with the user token, and in this way will generate a Link UI optimized for the end user and their specific employer. If the user cannot be confirmed as eligible, the user can still use the income verification flow, but they may be required to manually upload a paystub to verify their income.

While all request fields are optional, providing `employer` data will increase the chance of receiving a useful result.

When testing in Sandbox, you can control the results by providing special test values in the `employer` and `access_tokens` fields. `employer_good` and `employer_bad` will result in `HIGH` and `LOW` confidence values, respectively. `employer_multi` will result in a `HIGH` confidence with multiple payroll options. Likewise, `access_good` and `access_bad` will result in `HIGH` and `LOW` confidence values, respectively. Any other value for `employer` and `access_tokens` in Sandbox will result in `UNKNOWN` confidence.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditpayroll_incomeprecheck">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "client_id": "string",
  "employer": {
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "street": "string"
    },
    "name": "string",
    "tax_id": "string",
    "url": "string"
  },
  "payroll_institution": {
    "name": "string"
  },
  "secret": "string",
  "us_military_info": {
    "branch": "string",
    "is_active_duty": true
  },
  "user_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="check-income-verification-eligibility-and-optimize-conversion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditPayrollIncomePrecheckRequest](#schemacreditpayrollincomeprecheckrequest)|true|none|
|» access_tokens|body|[[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)]|false|An array of access tokens corresponding to Items belonging to the user whose eligibility is being checked. Note that if the Items specified here are not already initialized with `transactions`, providing them in this field will cause these Items to be initialized with (and billed for) the Transactions product.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» employer|body|[IncomeVerificationPrecheckEmployer](#schemaincomeverificationprecheckemployer)|false|Information about the end user's employer|
|» payroll_institution|body|[IncomeVerificationPrecheckPayrollInstitution](#schemaincomeverificationprecheckpayrollinstitution)|false|Information about the end user's payroll institution|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» us_military_info|body|[IncomeVerificationPrecheckMilitaryInfo](#schemaincomeverificationprecheckmilitaryinfo)|false|Data about military info in the income verification precheck.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the User data is being requested for.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "confidence": "HIGH",
  "request_id": "lMjeOeu9X1VUh1F"
}
```

<h3 id="check-income-verification-eligibility-and-optimize-conversion-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[CreditPayrollIncomePrecheckResponse](#schemacreditpayrollincomeprecheckresponse)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Create a relay token to share an Asset Report with a partner client (beta)

<a id="opIdcreditRelayCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/relay/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "report_tokens": [
      "string"
    ],
    "secondary_client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "webhook": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/relay/create`

Plaid can share an Asset Report directly with a participating third party on your behalf. The shared Asset Report is the exact same Asset Report originally created in `/asset_report/create`.

To grant a third party access to an Asset Report, use the `/credit/relay/create` endpoint to create a `relay_token` and then pass that token to your third party. Each third party has its own `secondary_client_id`; for example, `ce5bd328dcd34123456`. You'll need to create a separate `relay_token` for each third party that needs access to the report on your behalf.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#creditrelaycreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "report_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "secondary_client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "webhook": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-relay-token-to-share-an-asset-report-with-a-partner-client-beta-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditRelayCreateRequest](#schemacreditrelaycreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» report_tokens|body|[string]|true|List of report token strings, with at most one token of each report type. Currently only Asset Report token is supported.|
|» secondary_client_id|body|string|true|The `secondary_client_id` is the client id of the third party with whom you would like to share the relay token.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» webhook|body|string \| null|false|URL to which Plaid will send webhooks when the Secondary Client successfully retrieves an Asset Report by calling `/credit/relay/get`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "relay_token": "credit-relay-production-3TAU2CWVYBDVRHUCAAAI27ULU4",
  "request_id": "Iam3b"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-relay-token-to-share-an-asset-report-with-a-partner-client-beta-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[CreditRelayCreateResponse](#schemacreditrelaycreateresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Retrieve the reports associated with a relay token that was shared with you (beta)

<a id="opIdcreditRelayGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/relay/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "relay_token": "string",
    "report_type": "assets",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/relay/get`

`/credit/relay/get` allows third parties to receive a report that was shared with them, using a `relay_token` that was created by the report owner.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#creditrelayget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "relay_token": "string",
  "report_type": "assets",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-the-reports-associated-with-a-relay-token-that-was-shared-with-you-beta-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditRelayGetRequest](#schemacreditrelaygetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» relay_token|body|string|true|The `relay_token` granting access to the report you would like to get.|
|» report_type|body|[ReportType](#schemareporttype)|true|The report type. It can be `assets` or `income`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» report_type|assets|
|» report_type|income|

## Refresh a report of a relay token (beta)

<a id="opIdcreditRelayRefresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/relay/refresh \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "relay_token": "string",
    "report_type": "assets",
    "secret": "string",
    "webhook": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/relay/refresh`

The `/credit/relay/refresh` endpoint allows third parties to refresh a report that was relayed to them, using a `relay_token` that was created by the report owner. A new report will be created with the original report parameters, but with the most recent data available based on the `days_requested` value of the original report.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#creditrelayrefresh">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "relay_token": "string",
  "report_type": "assets",
  "secret": "string",
  "webhook": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="refresh-a-report-of-a-relay-token-beta-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditRelayRefreshRequest](#schemacreditrelayrefreshrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» relay_token|body|string|true|The `relay_token` granting access to the report you would like to refresh.|
|» report_type|body|[ReportType](#schemareporttype)|true|The report type. It can be `assets` or `income`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» webhook|body|string \| null|false|The URL registered to receive webhooks when the report of a relay token has been refreshed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» report_type|assets|
|» report_type|income|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "asset_report_id": "bf3a0490-344c-4620-a219-2693162e4b1d",
  "relay_token": "credit-relay-sandbox-8218d5f8-6d6d-403d-92f5-13a9afaa4398",
  "request_id": "NBZaq"
}
```

<h3 id="refresh-a-report-of-a-relay-token-beta-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[CreditRelayRefreshResponse](#schemacreditrelayrefreshresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Remove relay token (beta)

<a id="opIdcreditRelayRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/relay/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "relay_token": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/relay/remove`

The `/credit/relay/remove` endpoint allows you to invalidate a `relay_token`. The third party holding the token will no longer be able to access or refresh the reports which the `relay_token` gives access to. The original report, associated Items, and other relay tokens that provide access to the same report are not affected and will remain accessible after removing the given `relay_token`.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#creditrelayremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "relay_token": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-relay-token-beta-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditRelayRemoveRequest](#schemacreditrelayremoverequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» relay_token|body|string|true|The `relay_token` you would like to revoke.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "removed": true,
  "request_id": "m8MDnv9okwxFNBV"
}
```

|200|OK|OK|[CreditRelayRemoveResponse](#schemacreditrelayremoveresponse)|

clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

`POST /credit/sessions/get`

This endpoint can be used for your end users after they complete the Link flow. This endpoint returns a list of Link sessions that your user completed, where each session includes the results from the Link flow.

These results include details about the Item that was created and some product related metadata (showing, for example, whether the user finished the bank income verification step).

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditsessionsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string"
}
```

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Search employer database

<a id="opIdemployersSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/employers/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "products": [
      "string"
    ],
    "query": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /employers/search`

`/employers/search` allows you the ability to search Plaid’s database of known employers, for use with Deposit Switch. You can use this endpoint to look up a user's employer in order to confirm that they are supported. Users with non-supported employers can then be routed out of the Deposit Switch flow.

The data in the employer database is currently limited. As the Deposit Switch and Income products progress through their respective beta periods, more employers are being regularly added. Because the employer database is frequently updated, we recommend that you do not cache or store data from this endpoint for more than a day.

<a href="/api/employers/#employerssearch">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "products": [
    "string"
  ],
  "query": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="search-employer-database-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[EmployersSearchRequest](#schemaemployerssearchrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» products|body|[string]|true|The Plaid products the returned employers should support. Currently, this field must be set to `"deposit_switch"`.|
|» query|body|string|true|The employer name to be searched for.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "employers": [
    {
      "address": {
        "city": "San Francisco",
        "country": "US",
        "postal_code": "94103",
        "region": "CA",
        "street": "1098 Harrison St"
      },
      "confidence_score": 1,
      "employer_id": "emp_1",
      "name": "Plaid Inc."
    }
  ],
  "request_id": "ixTBLZGvhD4NnmB"
}
```

## Retrieve identity data

<a id="opIdidentityGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/identity/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "account_ids": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /identity/get`

The `/identity/get` endpoint allows you to retrieve various account holder information on file with the financial institution, including names, emails, phone numbers, and addresses. Only name data is guaranteed to be returned; other fields will be empty arrays if not provided by the institution.

This request may take some time to complete if identity was not specified as an initial product when creating the Item. This is because Plaid must communicate directly with the institution to retrieve the data.

Note: In API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier, the `owners` object is not returned, and instead identity information is returned in the top level `identity` object. For more details, see [Plaid API versioning](https://plaid.com/docs/api/versioning/#version-2019-05-29).

<a href="/api/products/identity/#identityget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-identity-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IdentityGetRequest](#schemaidentitygetrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[IdentityGetRequestOptions](#schemaidentitygetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/identity/get` results.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
