```bash
      "email_address": "string",
      "legal_name": "string",
      "phone_number": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /identity/match`

The `/identity/match` endpoint generates a match score, which indicates how well the provided identity data matches the identity information on file with the account holder's financial institution.

This request may take some time to complete if Identity was not specified as an initial product when creating the Item. This is because Plaid must communicate directly with the institution to retrieve the data.

<a href="/api/products/identity/#identitymatch">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "secret": "string",
  "user": {
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "street": "string"
    },
    "email_address": "string",
    "legal_name": "string",
    "phone_number": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-identity-match-score-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IdentityMatchRequest](#schemaidentitymatchrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[IdentityMatchRequestOptions](#schemaidentitymatchrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter /identity/match results|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user|body|[IdentityMatchUser](#schemaidentitymatchuser)|false|The user's legal name, phone number, email address and address used to perform fuzzy match.|

## Create a new identity verification

<a id="opIdidentityVerificationCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/identity_verification/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "gave_consent": true,
    "is_idempotent": true,
    "is_shareable": true,
    "secret": "string",
    "template_id": "idvtmp_4FrXJvfQU3zGUR",
    "user": {
      "address": {
        "city": "Pawnee",
        "country": "US",
        "postal_code": "46001",
        "region": "IN",
        "street": "123 Main St.",
        "street2": "Unit 42"
      },
      "client_user_id": "your-db-id-3b24110",
      "date_of_birth": "1990-05-29",
      "email_address": "user@example.com",
      "id_number": {
        "type": "us_ssn",
        "value": "123456789"
      },
      "name": {
        "family_name": "Knope",
        "given_name": "Leslie"
      },
      "phone_number": "+19876543212"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /identity_verification/create`

Create a new Identity Verification for the user specified by the `client_user_id` field. The requirements and behavior of the verification are determined by the `template_id` provided.
If you don't know whether the associated user already has an active Identity Verification, you can specify `"is_idempotent": true` in the request body. With idempotency enabled, a new Identity Verification will only be created if one does not already exist for the associated `client_user_id` and `template_id`. If an Identity Verification is found, it will be returned unmodified with an `200 OK` HTTP status code.


<a href="/api/products/identity-verification/#identity_verificationcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "gave_consent": true,
  "is_idempotent": true,
  "is_shareable": true,
  "secret": "string",
  "template_id": "idvtmp_4FrXJvfQU3zGUR",
  "user": {
    "address": {
      "city": "Pawnee",
      "country": "US",
      "postal_code": "46001",
      "region": "IN",
      "street": "123 Main St.",
      "street2": "Unit 42"
    },
    "client_user_id": "your-db-id-3b24110",
    "date_of_birth": "1990-05-29",
    "email_address": "user@example.com",
    "id_number": {
      "type": "us_ssn",
      "value": "123456789"
    },
    "name": {
      "family_name": "Knope",
      "given_name": "Leslie"
    },
    "phone_number": "+19876543212"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-identity-verification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IdentityVerificationCreateRequest](#schemaidentityverificationcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» gave_consent|body|[IdentityVerificationConsent](#schemaidentityverificationconsent)|true|A flag specifying whether the end user has already agreed to a privacy policy specifying that their data will be shared with Plaid for verification purposes.<br><br>If `gave_consent` is set to `true`, the `accept_tos` step will be marked as `skipped` and the end user's session will start at the next step requirement.|
|» is_idempotent|body|[IdempotencyFlag](#schemaidempotencyflag)|false|An optional flag specifying how you would like Plaid to handle attempts to create an Identity Verification when an Identity Verification already exists for the provided `client_user_id` and `template_id`.<br>If idempotency is enabled, Plaid will return the existing Identity Verification. If idempotency is disabled, Plaid will reject the request with a `400 Bad Request` status code if an Identity Verification already exists for the supplied `client_user_id` and `template_id`.|
|» is_shareable|body|boolean|true|A flag specifying whether you would like Plaid to expose a shareable URL for the verification being created.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» template_id|body|[IdentityVerificationTemplateID](#schemaidentityverificationtemplateid)|true|ID of the associated Identity Verification template.|
|» user|body|[IdentityVerificationRequestUser](#schemaidentityverificationrequestuser)|true|User information collected outside of Link, most likely via your own onboarding process.<br><br>Each of the following identity fields are optional:<br><br>`email_address`<br><br>`phone_number`<br><br>`date_of_birth`<br><br>`name`<br><br>`address`<br><br>`id_number`<br><br>Specifically, these fields are optional in that they can either be fully provided (satisfying every required field in their subschema) or omitted from the request entirely by not providing the key or value.<br>Providing these fields via the API will result in Link skipping the data collection process for the associated user. All verification steps enabled in the associated Identity Verification Template will still be run. Verification steps will either be run immediately, or once the user completes the `accept_tos` step, depending on the value provided to the `gave_consent` field.|

## Retry an Identity Verification

<a id="opIdidentityVerificationRetry"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/identity_verification/retry \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_user_id": "your-db-id-3b24110",
    "secret": "string",
    "steps": {
      "documentary_verification": true,
      "kyc_check": true,
      "selfie_check": true,
      "verify_sms": true
    },
    "strategy": "reset",
    "template_id": "idvtmp_4FrXJvfQU3zGUR"
  }'
```

`POST /identity_verification/retry`

Allow a customer to retry their identity verification

<a href="/api/products/identity-verification/#identity_verificationretry">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_user_id": "your-db-id-3b24110",
  "secret": "string",
  "steps": {
    "documentary_verification": true,
    "kyc_check": true,
    "selfie_check": true,
    "verify_sms": true
  },
  "strategy": "reset",
  "template_id": "idvtmp_4FrXJvfQU3zGUR"
}
```

<h3 id="retry-an-identity-verification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IdentityVerificationRetryRequest](#schemaidentityverificationretryrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_user_id|body|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|An identifier to help you connect this object to your internal systems. For example, your database ID corresponding to this object.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» steps|body|[IdentityVerificationRetryRequestStepsObject](#schemaidentityverificationretryrequeststepsobject)|false|Instructions for the `custom` retry strategy specifying which steps should be required or skipped.<br><br><br>Note:<br><br><br>This field must be provided when the retry strategy is `custom` and must be omitted otherwise.<br><br>Custom retries override settings in your Plaid Template. For example, if your Plaid Template has `verify_sms` disabled, a custom retry with `verify_sms` enabled will still require the step.<br><br>The `selfie_check` step is currently not supported on the sandbox server. Sandbox requests will silently disable the `selfie_check` step when provided.|
|» strategy|body|[Strategy](#schemastrategy)|true|An instruction specifying what steps the new Identity Verification attempt should require the user to complete:<br><br><br>`reset` - Restart the user at the beginning of the session, regardless of whether they successfully completed part of their previous session.<br><br>`incomplete` - Start the new session at the step that the user failed in the previous session, skipping steps that have already been successfully completed.<br><br>`infer` - If the most recent Identity Verification attempt associated with the given `client_user_id` has a status of `failed` or `expired`, retry using the `incomplete` strategy. Otherwise, use the `reset` strategy.<br><br>`custom` - Start the new session with a custom configuration, specified by the value of the `steps` field<br><br>Note:<br><br>The `incomplete` strategy cannot be applied if the session's failing step is `screening` or `risk_check`.<br><br>The `infer` strategy cannot be applied if the session's status is still `active`|
|» template_id|body|[IdentityVerificationTemplateID](#schemaidentityverificationtemplateid)|true|ID of the associated Identity Verification template.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» strategy|reset|
|» strategy|incomplete|
|» strategy|infer|
|» strategy|custom|

<a id="opIdincomeVerificationCreate"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/income/verification/create \

```

`POST /income/verification/create`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/income/verification/create` begins the income verification process by returning an `income_verification_id`. You can then provide the `income_verification_id` to `/link/token/create` under the `income_verification` parameter in order to create a Link instance that will prompt the user to go through the income verification flow. Plaid will fire an `INCOME` webhook once the user completes the Payroll Income flow, or when the uploaded documents in the Document Income flow have finished processing. 

<a href="/api/products/income/#incomeverificationcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "access_tokens": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "precheck_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "webhook": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="deprecated-create-an-income-verification-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IncomeVerificationCreateRequest](#schemaincomeverificationcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[IncomeVerificationCreateRequestOptions](#schemaincomeverificationcreaterequestoptions)|false|Optional arguments for `/income/verification/create`|
|» precheck_id|body|string|false|The ID of a precheck created with `/income/verification/precheck`. Will be used to improve conversion of the income verification flow.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» webhook|body|string|true|The URL endpoint to which Plaid should send webhooks related to the progress of the income verification process.|

## (Deprecated) Download the original documents used for income verification

<a id="opIdincomeVerificationDocumentsDownload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/income/verification/documents/download \
  -X POST \

  }'
```

`POST /income/verification/documents/download`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/income/verification/documents/download` provides the ability to download the source documents associated with the verification.

If Document Income was used, the documents will be those the user provided in Link. For Payroll Income, the most recent files available
for download from the payroll provider will be available from this endpoint.

The response to `/income/verification/documents/download` is a ZIP file in binary data. If a `document_id` is passed, a single document will be contained in this file.
If not, the response will contain all documents associated with the verification.

The `request_id` is returned in the `Plaid-Request-ID` header.

<a href="/api/products/income/#incomeverificationdocumentsdownload">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "document_id": "string",
  "income_verification_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="deprecated-download-the-original-documents-used-for-income-verification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IncomeVerificationDocumentsDownloadRequest](#schemaincomeverificationdocumentsdownloadrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessTokenNullable](#schemaaccesstokennullable)|false|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» document_id|body|string \| null|false|The document ID to download. If passed, a single document will be returned in the resulting zip file, rather than all document|
|» income_verification_id|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The ID of the verification.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

`POST /income/verification/paystubs/get`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/income/verification/paystubs/get` returns the information collected from the paystubs that were used to verify an end user's income. It can be called once the status of the verification has been set to `VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_COMPLETE`, as reported by the `INCOME: verification_status` webhook. Attempting to call the endpoint before verification has been completed will result in an error.

This endpoint has been deprecated; new integrations should use `/credit/payroll_income/get` instead.

<a href="/api/products/income/#incomeverificationpaystubsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "income_verification_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

`POST /income/verification/precheck`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/income/verification/precheck` is an optional endpoint that can be called before initializing a Link session for income verification. It evaluates whether a given user is supportable by digital income verification and returns a `precheck_id` that can be provided to `/link/token/create`. If the user is eligible for digital verification, providing the `precheck_id` in this way will generate a Link UI optimized for the end user and their specific employer. If the user cannot be confirmed as eligible, the `precheck_id` can still be provided to `/link/token/create` and the user can still use the income verification flow, but they may be required to manually upload a paystub to verify their income.

While all request fields are optional, providing either `employer` or `transactions_access_tokens` data will increase the chance of receiving a useful result.

This endpoint has been deprecated; new integrations should use `/credit/payroll_income/precheck` instead.

<a href="/api/products/income/#incomeverificationprecheck">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "employer": {
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "region": "string",
```

## (Deprecated) Retrieve information from the tax documents used for income verification

<a id="opIdincomeVerificationTaxformsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/income/verification/taxforms/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "income_verification_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /income/verification/taxforms/get`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/income/verification/taxforms/get` returns the information collected from forms that were used to verify an end user''s income. It can be called once the status of the verification has been set to `VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_COMPLETE`, as reported by the `INCOME: verification_status` webhook. Attempting to call the endpoint before verification has been completed will result in an error.

This endpoint has been deprecated; new integrations should use `/credit/payroll_income/get` instead.

<a href="/api/products/income/#incomeverificationtaxformsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "income_verification_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

|» income_verification_id|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The ID of the verification.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Get details of all supported institutions

<a id="opIdinstitutionsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/institutions/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "count": 1,
    "country_codes": [
      "US"
    ],
    "offset": 0,
    "options": {
      "include_auth_metadata": false,
      "include_optional_metadata": true,
      "include_payment_initiation_metadata": false,
      "oauth": true,
      "products": [
        "assets"
      ],
      "routing_numbers": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /institutions/get`

Returns a JSON response containing details on all financial institutions currently supported by Plaid. Because Plaid supports thousands of institutions, results are paginated.

If there is no overlap between an institution’s enabled products and a client’s enabled products, then the institution will be filtered out from the response. As a result, the number of institutions returned may not match the count specified in the call.

<a href="/api/institutions/#institutionsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "count": 1,
  "country_codes": [
    "US"
  ],
  "offset": 0,
  "options": {
    "include_auth_metadata": false,
    "include_optional_metadata": true,
    "include_payment_initiation_metadata": false,
    "oauth": true,
    "products": [
      "assets"
    ],
    "routing_numbers": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-details-of-all-supported-institutions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InstitutionsGetRequest](#schemainstitutionsgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» count|body|integer|true|The total number of Institutions to return.|
|» country_codes|body|[[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)]|true|Specify an array of Plaid-supported country codes this institution supports, using the ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country code standard.<br><br>In API versions 2019-05-29 and earlier, the `country_codes` parameter is an optional parameter within the `options` object and will default to `[US]` if it is not supplied.<br>|
|» offset|body|integer|true|The number of Institutions to skip.|
|» options|body|[InstitutionsGetRequestOptions](#schemainstitutionsgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/institutions/get` results.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

```bash
curl https://example.com/institutions/search \

        "payment_id": "string"
      }

    "query": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /institutions/search`

Returns a JSON response containing details for institutions that match the query parameters, up to a maximum of ten institutions per query.

Versioning note: API versions 2019-05-29 and earlier allow use of the `public_key` parameter instead of the `client_id` and `secret` parameters to authenticate to this endpoint. The `public_key` parameter has since been deprecated; all customers are encouraged to use `client_id` and `secret` instead.


<a href="/api/institutions/#institutionssearch">External documentation</a>

```json
    "oauth": true,

      "consent_id": "string",
      "payment_id": "string"
    }

    "assets"
  ],
  "query": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="search-institutions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InstitutionsSearchRequest](#schemainstitutionssearchrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» country_codes|body|[[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)]|true|Specify an array of Plaid-supported country codes this institution supports, using the ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country code standard. In API versions 2019-05-29 and earlier, the `country_codes` parameter is an optional parameter within the `options` object and will default to `[US]` if it is not supplied.<br>|
|» options|body|[InstitutionsSearchRequestOptions](#schemainstitutionssearchrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/institutions/search` results.|
|» products|body|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|true|Filter the Institutions based on whether they support all products listed in `products`. Provide `null` to get institutions regardless of supported products. Note that when `auth` is specified as a product, if you are enabled for Instant Match or Automated Micro-deposits, institutions that support those products will be returned even if `auth` is not present in their product array.|
|» query|body|string|true|The search query. Institutions with names matching the query are returned|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Get Investment holdings

<a id="opIdinvestmentsHoldingsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/investments/holdings/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "account_ids": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /investments/holdings/get`

The `/investments/holdings/get` endpoint allows developers to receive user-authorized stock position data for `investment`-type accounts.

<a href="/api/products/investments/#investmentsholdingsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-investment-holdings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InvestmentsHoldingsGetRequest](#schemainvestmentsholdingsgetrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[InvestmentHoldingsGetRequestOptions](#schemainvestmentholdingsgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/investments/holdings/get` results. If provided, must not be `null`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Get investment transactions

<a id="opIdinvestmentsTransactionsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/investments/transactions/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "end_date": "1970-01-01",
    "options": {
      "account_ids": [
        "string"
      ],
      "count": 100,
      "offset": 0
    },
    "secret": "string",
    "start_date": "1970-01-01"
  }'
```

`POST /investments/transactions/get`

The `/investments/transactions/get` endpoint allows developers to retrieve up to 24 months of user-authorized transaction data for investment accounts.

Transactions are returned in reverse-chronological order, and the sequence of transaction ordering is stable and will not shift.

Due to the potentially large number of investment transactions associated with an Item, results are paginated. Manipulate the count and offset parameters in conjunction with the `total_investment_transactions` response body field to fetch all available investment transactions.

Note that Investments does not have a webhook to indicate when initial transaction data has loaded. Instead, if transactions data is not ready when `/investments/transactions/get` is first called, Plaid will wait for the data. For this reason, calling `/investments/transactions/get` immediately after Link may take up to one to two minutes to return.

<a href="/api/products/investments/#investmentstransactionsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "end_date": "1970-01-01",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "count": 100,
    "offset": 0
  },
  "secret": "string",
  "start_date": "1970-01-01"
}
```

<h3 id="get-investment-transactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InvestmentsTransactionsGetRequest](#schemainvestmentstransactionsgetrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» end_date|body|string(date)|true|The most recent date for which to fetch transaction history. Dates should be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.|
|» options|body|[InvestmentsTransactionsGetRequestOptions](#schemainvestmentstransactionsgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/investments/transactions/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» start_date|body|string(date)|true|The earliest date for which to fetch transaction history. Dates should be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.|

## Invalidate access_token

<a id="opIditemAccessTokenInvalidate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/item/access_token/invalidate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /item/access_token/invalidate`

By default, the `access_token` associated with an Item does not expire and should be stored in a persistent, secure manner.

You can use the `/item/access_token/invalidate` endpoint to rotate the `access_token` associated with an Item. The endpoint returns a new `access_token` and immediately invalidates the previous `access_token`.


<a href="/api/tokens/#itemaccess_tokeninvalidate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="invalidate-accesstoken-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemAccessTokenInvalidateRequest](#schemaitemaccesstokeninvalidaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "new_access_token": "access-sandbox-8ab976e6-64bc-4b38-98f7-731e7a349970",
  "request_id": "m8MDnv9okwxFNBV"
}
```

<h3 id="invalidate-accesstoken-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[ItemAccessTokenInvalidateResponse](#schemaitemaccesstokeninvalidateresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret

## Update the scopes of access for a particular application

<a id="opIditemApplicationScopesUpdate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/item/application/scopes/update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "application_id": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "context": "ENROLLMENT",
    "scopes": {
      "accounts": [
        {
          "account_product_access": {
            "account_data": true,
            "statements": true,
            "tax_documents": true
          },
          "authorized": true,
          "unique_id": "string"
        }
      ],
      "new_accounts": true,
      "product_access": {
        "accounts_details_transactions": true,
        "accounts_routing_number": true,
        "accounts_statements": true,
        "accounts_tax_statements": true,
        "auth": true,
        "customers_profiles": true,
        "identity": true,
        "statements": true,
        "transactions": true
      }
    },
    "secret": "string",
    "state": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /item/application/scopes/update`

Enable consumers to update product access on selected accounts for an application.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "application_id": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "context": "ENROLLMENT",
  "scopes": {
    "accounts": [
      {
        "account_product_access": {
          "account_data": true,
          "statements": true,
          "tax_documents": true
        },
        "authorized": true,
        "unique_id": "string"
      }
    ],
    "new_accounts": true,
    "product_access": {
      "accounts_details_transactions": true,
      "accounts_routing_number": true,
      "accounts_statements": true,
      "accounts_tax_statements": true,
      "auth": true,
      "customers_profiles": true,
      "identity": true,
      "statements": true,
      "transactions": true
    }
  },
  "secret": "string",
  "state": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-scopes-of-access-for-a-particular-application-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemApplicationScopesUpdateRequest](#schemaitemapplicationscopesupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» application_id|body|[ApplicationID](#schemaapplicationid)|true|This field will map to the application ID that is returned from /item/applications/list, or provided to the institution in an oauth redirect.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» context|body|[ScopesContext](#schemascopescontext)|true|An indicator for when scopes are being updated. When scopes are updated via enrollment (i.e. OAuth), the partner must send `ENROLLMENT`. When scopes are updated in a post-enrollment view, the partner must send `PORTAL`.|
|» scopes|body|[Scopes](#schemascopes)|true|The scopes object|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» state|body|[ScopesState](#schemascopesstate)|false|When scopes are updated during enrollment, this field must be populated with the state sent to the partner in the OAuth Login URI. This field is required when the context is `ENROLLMENT`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» context|ENROLLMENT|
|» context|PORTAL|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "causes": [
    null
  ],
  "display_message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "error_code": "string",
  "error_message": "string",
  "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "request_id": "string",
  "status": 0,
  "suggested_action": "string"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success|[ItemApplicationScopesUpdateResponse](#schemaitemapplicationscopesupdateresponse)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|

## Import Item

<a id="opIditemImport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/item/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "webhook": "string"
    },
    "products": [
      "assets"
    ],
    "secret": "string",
    "user_auth": {
      "auth_token": "string",
      "user_id": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /item/import`

`/item/import` creates an Item via your Plaid Exchange Integration and returns an `access_token`. As part of an `/item/import` request, you will include a User ID (`user_auth.user_id`) and Authentication Token (`user_auth.auth_token`) that enable data aggregation through your Plaid Exchange API endpoints. These authentication principals are to be chosen by you.

Upon creating an Item via `/item/import`, Plaid will automatically begin an extraction of that Item through the Plaid Exchange infrastructure you have already integrated. This will automatically generate the Plaid native account ID for the account the user will switch their direct deposit to (`target_account_id`).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "webhook": "string"
  },
  "products": [
    "assets"
  ],
  "secret": "string",
  "user_auth": {
    "auth_token": "string",
    "user_id": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="import-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemImportRequest](#schemaitemimportrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[ItemImportRequestOptions](#schemaitemimportrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to configure `/item/import` request.|
|» products|body|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|true|Array of product strings|

## Create public token

<a id="opIditemCreatePublicToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/item/public_token/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /item/public_token/create`

Note: As of July 2020, the `/item/public_token/create` endpoint is deprecated. Instead, use `/link/token/create` with an `access_token` to create a Link token for use with [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode).

If you need your user to take action to restore or resolve an error associated with an Item, generate a public token with the `/item/public_token/create` endpoint and then initialize Link with that `public_token`.

A `public_token` is one-time use and expires after 30 minutes. You use a `public_token` to initialize Link in [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode) for a particular Item. You can generate a `public_token` for an Item even if you did not use Link to create the Item originally.

The `/item/public_token/create` endpoint is **not** used to create your initial `public_token`. If you have not already received an `access_token` for a specific Item, use Link to obtain your `public_token` instead. See the [Quickstart](https://plaid.com/docs/quickstart) for more information.

<a href="/api/tokens/#itempublic_tokencreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-public-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemPublicTokenCreateRequest](#schemaitempublictokencreaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "public_token": "public-sandbox-b0e2c4ee-a763-4df5-bfe9-46a46bce993d",
  "request_id": "Aim3b"
}
```

<h3 id="create-public-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|200|OK|OK|[ItemPublicTokenCreateResponse](#schemaitempublictokencreateresponse)|

## Exchange public token for an access token

<a id="opIditemPublicTokenExchange"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/item/public_token/exchange \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "public_token": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /item/public_token/exchange`

Exchange a Link `public_token` for an API `access_token`. Link hands off the `public_token` client-side via the `onSuccess` callback once a user has successfully created an Item. The `public_token` is ephemeral and expires after 30 minutes. An `access_token` does not expire, but can be revoked by calling `/item/remove`.

The response also includes an `item_id` that should be stored with the `access_token`. The `item_id` is used to identify an Item in a webhook. The `item_id` can also be retrieved by making an `/item/get` request.

<a href="/api/tokens/#itempublic_tokenexchange">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "public_token": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="exchange-public-token-for-an-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemPublicTokenExchangeRequest](#schemaitempublictokenexchangerequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» public_token|body|string|true|Your `public_token`, obtained from the Link `onSuccess` callback or `/sandbox/item/public_token/create`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "access-sandbox-de3ce8ef-33f8-452c-a685-8671031fc0f6",
  "item_id": "M5eVJqLnv3tbzdngLDp9FL5OlDNxlNhlE55op",
  "request_id": "Aim3b"
}
```

<h3 id="exchange-public-token-for-an-access-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[ItemPublicTokenExchangeResponse](#schemaitempublictokenexchangeresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Remove an Item

<a id="opIditemRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/item/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /item/remove`

The `/item/remove` endpoint allows you to remove an Item. Once removed, the `access_token`, as well as any processor tokens or bank account tokens associated with the Item, is no longer valid and cannot be used to access any data that was associated with the Item.

Note that in the Development environment, issuing an `/item/remove`  request will not decrement your live credential count. To increase your credential account in Development, contact Support.

Also note that for certain OAuth-based institutions, an Item removed via `/item/remove` may still show as an active connection in the institution's OAuth permission manager.

API versions 2019-05-29 and earlier return a `removed` boolean as part of the response.

<a href="/api/items/#itemremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Retrieve Liabilities data

<a id="opIdliabilitiesGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/liabilities/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "account_ids": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /liabilities/get`

The `/liabilities/get` endpoint returns various details about an Item with loan or credit accounts. Liabilities data is available primarily for US financial institutions, with some limited coverage of Canadian institutions. Currently supported account types are account type `credit` with account subtype `credit card` or `paypal`, and account type `loan` with account subtype `student` or `mortgage`. To limit accounts listed in Link to types and subtypes supported by Liabilities, you can use the `account_filters` parameter when [creating a Link token](https://plaid.com/docs/api/tokens/#linktokencreate).

The types of information returned by Liabilities can include balances and due dates, loan terms, and account details such as original loan amount and guarantor. Data is refreshed approximately once per day; the latest data can be retrieved by calling `/liabilities/get`.

Note: This request may take some time to complete if `liabilities` was not specified as an initial product when creating the Item. This is because Plaid must communicate directly with the institution to retrieve the additional data.

<a href="/api/products/liabilities/#liabilitiesget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-liabilities-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LiabilitiesGetRequest](#schemaliabilitiesgetrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[LiabilitiesGetRequestOptions](#schemaliabilitiesgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/liabilities/get` results. If provided, `options` cannot be null.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Exchange the Link Correlation Id for a Link Token

<a id="opIdlinkOauthCorrelationIdExchange"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/link/oauth/correlation_id/exchange \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "link_correlation_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /link/oauth/correlation_id/exchange`

Exchange an OAuth `link_correlation_id` for the corresponding `link_token`. The `link_correlation_id` is only available for 'payment_initiation' products and is provided to the client via the OAuth `redirect_uri` as a query parameter.
The `link_correlation_id` is ephemeral and expires in a brief period, after which it can no longer be exchanged for the 'link_token'.

<a href="/api/oauth/#linkcorrelationid">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "link_correlation_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="exchange-the-link-correlation-id-for-a-link-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LinkOAuthCorrelationIdExchangeRequest](#schemalinkoauthcorrelationidexchangerequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» link_correlation_id|body|string|true|A `link_correlation_id` from a received OAuth redirect URI callback|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
```

`POST /link/token/create`

The `/link/token/create` endpoint creates a `link_token`, which is required as a parameter when initializing Link. Once Link has been initialized, it returns a `public_token`, which can then be exchanged for an `access_token` via `/item/public_token/exchange` as part of the main Link flow.

A `link_token` generated by `/link/token/create` is also used to initialize other Link flows, such as the update mode flow for tokens with expired credentials, or the Payment Initiation (Europe) flow.

<a href="/api/tokens/#linktokencreate">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="create-link-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequest](#schemalinktokencreaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|string|false|The `access_token` associated with the Item to update or reference, used when updating, modifying, or accessing an existing `access_token`. Used when launching Link in update mode, when completing the Same-day (manual) Micro-deposit flow, or (optionally) when initializing Link for a returning user as part of the Transfer UI flow.|
|» account_filters|body|[LinkTokenAccountFilters](#schemalinktokenaccountfilters)|false|By default, Link will provide limited account filtering: it will only display Institutions that are compatible with all products supplied in the `products` parameter of `/link/token/create`, and, if `auth` is specified in the `products` array, will also filter out accounts other than `checking` and `savings` accounts on the Account Select pane. You can further limit the accounts shown in Link by using `account_filters` to specify the account subtypes to be shown in Link. Only the specified subtypes will be shown. This filtering applies to both the Account Select view (if enabled) and the Institution Select view. Institutions that do not support the selected subtypes will be omitted from Link. To indicate that all subtypes should be shown, use the value `"all"`. If the `account_filters` filter is used, any account type for which a filter is not specified will be entirely omitted from Link. For a full list of valid types and subtypes, see the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema).<br><br>For institutions using OAuth, the filter will not affect the list of accounts shown by the bank in the OAuth window.<br>|
|» additional_consented_products|body|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|(Beta) This field has no effect unless you are participating in the Product Scope Transparency beta program.<br>List of additional Plaid product(s) you wish to collect consent for. These products will not be billed until you start using them by calling the relevant endpoints.<br><br>`balance` is *not* a valid value, the Balance product does not require explicit initialization and will automatically have consent collected.<br><br>Institutions that do not support these products will still be shown in Link|
|» android_package_name|body|string|false|The name of your app's Android package. Required if using the `link_token` to initialize Link on Android. When creating a `link_token` for initializing Link on other platforms, this field must be left blank. Any package name specified here must also be added to the Allowed Android package names setting on the [developer dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api). |
|» auth|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequestAuth](#schemalinktokencreaterequestauth)|false|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Auth product. This field can be used to enable or disable extended Auth flows for the resulting Link session. Omitting any field will result in a default that can be configured by your account manager.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_name|body|string|true|The name of your application, as it should be displayed in Link. Maximum length of 30 characters. If a value longer than 30 characters is provided, Link will display "This Application" instead.|
|» country_codes|body|[[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)]|true|Specify an array of Plaid-supported country codes using the ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country code standard. Institutions from all listed countries will be shown. For a complete mapping of supported products by country, see https://plaid.com/global/.<br><br>If Link is launched with multiple country codes, only products that you are enabled for in all countries will be used by Link. Note that while all countries are enabled by default in Sandbox and Development, in Production only US and Canada are enabled by default. To gain access to European institutions in the Production environment, [file a product access Support ticket](https://dashboard.plaid.com/support/new/product-and-development/product-troubleshooting/request-product-access) via the Plaid dashboard. If you initialize with a European country code, your users will see the European consent panel during the Link flow.<br><br>If using a Link customization, make sure the country codes in the customization match those specified in `country_codes`. If both `country_codes` and a Link customization are used, the value in `country_codes` may override the value in the customization.<br><br>If using the Auth features Instant Match, Same-day Micro-deposits, or Automated Micro-deposits, `country_codes` must be set to `['US']`.|
|» deposit_switch|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequestDepositSwitch](#schemalinktokencreaterequestdepositswitch)|false|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Deposit Switch (beta) product. This field is required if `deposit_switch` is included in the `products` array.|
|» employment|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequestEmployment](#schemalinktokencreaterequestemployment)|false|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Employment product. This field is required if `employment` is included in the `products` array.|
|» eu_config|body|[LinkTokenEUConfig](#schemalinktokeneuconfig)|false|Configuration parameters for EU flows|
|» identity_verification|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequestIdentityVerification](#schemalinktokencreaterequestidentityverification)|false|Specifies option for initializing Link for use with the Identity Verification product.|
|» income_verification|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequestIncomeVerification](#schemalinktokencreaterequestincomeverification)|false|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Income product. This field is required if `income_verification` is included in the `products` array.|
|» institution_data|body|[LinkTokenCreateInstitutionData](#schemalinktokencreateinstitutiondata)|false|A map containing data used to highlight institutions in Link.|
|» institution_id|body|string|false|Used for certain Europe-only configurations, as well as certain legacy use cases in other regions.|
|» investments|body|[LinkTokenInvestments](#schemalinktokeninvestments)|false|Configuration parameters for the Investments product|
|» language|body|string|true|The language that Link should be displayed in.<br><br>Supported languages are:<br>- Danish (`'da'`)<br>- Dutch (`'nl'`)<br>- English (`'en'`)<br>- Estonian (`'et'`)<br>- French (`'fr'`)<br>- German (`'de'`)<br>- Italian (`'it'`)<br>- Latvian (`'lv'`)<br>- Lithuanian (`'lt'`)<br>- Norwegian (`'no'`)<br>- Polish (`'po'`)<br>- Romanian (`'ro'`)<br>- Spanish (`'es'`)<br>- Swedish (`'se'`)<br><br>When using a Link customization, the language configured here must match the setting in the customization, or the customization will not be applied.|
|» link_customization_name|body|string|false|The name of the Link customization from the Plaid Dashboard to be applied to Link. If not specified, the `default` customization will be used. When using a Link customization, the language in the customization must match the language selected via the `language` parameter, and the countries in the customization should match the country codes selected via `country_codes`.|
|» payment_initiation|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequestPaymentInitiation](#schemalinktokencreaterequestpaymentinitiation)|false|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Payment Initiation (Europe) product. This field is required if `payment_initiation` is included in the `products` array. Either `payment_id` or `consent_id` must be provided.|
|» products|body|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|List of Plaid product(s) you wish to use. If launching Link in update mode, should be omitted; required otherwise.<br><br>`balance` is *not* a valid value, the Balance product does not require explicit initialization and will automatically be initialized when any other product is initialized.<br><br>The products specified here will determine which institutions will be available to your users in Link. Only institutions that support *all* requested products can be selected; a if a user attempts to select an institution that does not support a listed product, a "Connectivity not supported" error message will appear in Link. To maximize the number of institutions available, initialize Link with the minimal product set required for your use case. Additional products can be added after Link initialization by calling the relevant endpoints. For details and exceptions, see [Choosing when to initialize products](https://plaid.com/docs/link/initializing-products/).<br><br>Note that, unless you have opted to disable Instant Match support, institutions that support Instant Match will also be shown in Link if `auth` is specified as a product, even though these institutions do not contain `auth` in their product array.<br><br>In Production, you will be billed for each product that you specify when initializing Link. Note that a product cannot be removed from an Item once the Item has been initialized with that product. To stop billing on an Item for subscription-based products, such as Liabilities, Investments, and Transactions, remove the Item via `/item/remove`.|
|» redirect_uri|body|string|false|A URI indicating the destination where a user should be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or via a webview. The `redirect_uri` should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production or Development, must be an https URI. To specify any subdomain, use `*` as a wildcard character, e.g. `https://*.example.com/oauth.html`. If `android_package_name` is specified, this field should be left blank.  Note that any redirect URI must also be added to the Allowed redirect URIs list in the [developer dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api).|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» transfer|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequestTransfer](#schemalinktokencreaterequesttransfer)|false|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Transfer product.|
|» update|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequestUpdate](#schemalinktokencreaterequestupdate)|false|Specifies options for initializing Link for [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode).|
|» user|body|[LinkTokenCreateRequestUser](#schemalinktokencreaterequestuser)|true|An object specifying information about the end user who will be linking their account.|
|» user_token|body|string|false|A user token generated using `/user/create`. Any Item created during the Link session will be associated with the user.|
|» webhook|body|string|false|The destination URL to which any webhooks should be sent.|

## Get Link Token

<a id="opIdlinkTokenGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/link/token/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "link_token": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /link/token/get`

The `/link/token/get` endpoint gets information about a previously-created `link_token` using the
`/link/token/create` endpoint. It can be useful for debugging purposes.

<a href="/api/tokens/#linktokenget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "link_token": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-link-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LinkTokenGetRequest](#schemalinktokengetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» link_token|body|string|true|A `link_token` from a previous invocation of `/link/token/create`|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created_at": "2020-12-02T21:14:54Z",
```

## Create Link Delivery session

<a id="opIdlinkDeliveryCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/link_delivery/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "communication_methods": [
      {
        "address": "string",
        "method": "SMS"
      }
    ],
    "link_token": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /link_delivery/create`

Use the `/link_delivery/create` endpoint to create a Link Delivery session.

<a href="/docs/assets/waitlist/link-delivery/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "communication_methods": [
    {
      "address": "string",
      "method": "SMS"
    }
  ],
  "link_token": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-link-delivery-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LinkDeliveryCreateRequest](#schemalinkdeliverycreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» communication_methods|body|[[LinkDeliveryCommunicationMethod](#schemalinkdeliverycommunicationmethod)]|true|The list of communication methods to send the Link Delivery URL to.|
|» link_token|body|string|true|A `link_token` from a previous invocation of `/link/token/create` with Link Delivery enabled.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

<h3 id="creates-a-new-end-customer-for-a-plaid-reseller-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PartnerCustomerCreateRequest](#schemapartnercustomercreaterequest)|true|none|
|» address|body|[PartnerEndCustomerAddress](#schemapartnerendcustomeraddress)|true|The end customer's address.|
|» application_name|body|string|true|The name of the end customer's application. This will be shown to end users when they go through the Plaid Link flow.|
|» assets_under_management|body|[PartnerEndCustomerAssetsUnderManagement](#schemapartnerendcustomerassetsundermanagement)|false|Assets under management for the given end customer. Required for end customers with monthly service commitments.|
|» billing_contact|body|[PartnerEndCustomerBillingContact](#schemapartnerendcustomerbillingcontact)|false|The billing contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's technical contact if omitted.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» company_name|body|string|true|The company name of the end customer being created. This will be used to display the end customer in the Plaid Dashboard. It will not be shown to end users.|
|» create_link_customization|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the end customer's default Link customization will be set to match the partner's. You can always change the end customer's Link customization in the Plaid Dashboard. See the [Link Customization docs](https://plaid.com/docs/link/customization/) for more information.|
|» customer_support_info|body|[PartnerEndCustomerCustomerSupportInfo](#schemapartnerendcustomercustomersupportinfo)|false|This information is public. Users of your app will see this information when managing connections between your app and their bank accounts in Plaid Portal. Defaults to partner's customer support info if omitted.|
|» is_bank_addendum_completed|body|boolean|true|Denotes whether the partner has forwarded the Plaid bank addendum to the end customer.|
|» is_diligence_attested|body|boolean|true|Denotes whether or not the partner has completed attestation of diligence for the end customer to be created.|
|» legal_entity_name|body|string|true|The end customer's legal name. This will be shared with financial institutions as part of the OAuth registration process. It will not be shown to end users.|
|» logo|body|string|false|Base64-encoded representation of the end customer's logo. Must be a PNG of size 1024x1024 under 4MB. The logo will be shared with financial institutions and shown to the end user during Link flows. A logo is required if `create_link_customization` is `true`. If `create_link_customization` is `false` and the logo is omitted, a stock logo will be used.|
|» products|body|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|true|The products to be enabled for the end customer.|
|» redirect_uris|body|[string]|false|A list of URIs indicating the destination(s) where a user can be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or via a webview. URIs should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production or Development, URIs must use https. To specify any subdomain, use `*` as a wildcard character, e.g. `https://*.example.com/oauth.html`. To modify redirect URIs for an end customer after creating them, go to the end customer's [API page](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api) in the Dashboard.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» technical_contact|body|[PartnerEndCustomerTechnicalContact](#schemapartnerendcustomertechnicalcontact)|false|The technical contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's technical contact if omitted.|
|» website|body|string|true|The end customer's website.|

The `/partner/customer/remove` endpoint is used by reseller partners to remove an end customer. Removing an end customer will remove it from view in the Plaid Dashboard and deactivate its API keys. `POST /payment_initiation/consent/create`

The `/payment_initiation/consent/create` endpoint is used to create a payment consent, which can be used to initiate payments on behalf of the user. Payment consents are created with `UNAUTHORISED` status by default and must be authorised by the user before payments can be initiated.

Consents can be limited in time and scope, and have constraints that describe limitations for payments.

<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationconsentcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "constraints": {
    "max_payment_amount": {
      "currency": "GBP",
      "value": 0
    },
    "periodic_amounts": [
      {
        "alignment": "CALENDAR",
        "amount": {
          "currency": "GBP",
          "value": 0
        },
        "interval": "DAY"
      }
    ],
    "valid_date_time": {
      "from": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "to": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  },
  "options": {
    "bacs": {
      "account": "string",
      "sort_code": "string"
    },
    "iban": "stringstringstr",
    "request_refund_details": true
  },
  "recipient_id": "string",
  "reference": "string",
  "scopes": [
    "ME_TO_ME"
  ],
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-payment-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationConsentCreateRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» constraints|body|[PaymentInitiationConsentConstraints](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentconstraints)|true|Limitations that will be applied to payments initiated using the payment consent.|
|» options|body|[ExternalPaymentInitiationConsentOptions](#schemaexternalpaymentinitiationconsentoptions)|false|Additional payment consent options|
|» recipient_id|body|string|true|The ID of the recipient the payment consent is for. The created consent can be used to transfer funds to this recipient only.|
|» reference|body|string|true|A reference for the payment consent. This must be an alphanumeric string with at most 18 characters and must not contain any special characters.|
|» scopes|body|[[PaymentInitiationConsentScope](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentscope)]|true|An array of payment consent scopes.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. ## Create a payment

<a id="opIdpaymentInitiationPaymentCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/payment/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": {
      "currency": "GBP",
      "value": 0
    },
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "bacs": {
        "account": "string",
        "sort_code": "string"
      },
      "iban": "stringstringstr",
      "request_refund_details": true,
      "scheme": null
    },
    "recipient_id": "string",
    "reference": "string",
    "schedule": {
      "adjusted_start_date": "1970-01-01",
      "end_date": "1970-01-01",
      "interval": "WEEKLY",
      "interval_execution_day": 0,
      "start_date": "1970-01-01"
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/payment/create`

After creating a payment recipient, you can use the `/payment_initiation/payment/create` endpoint to create a payment to that recipient.  Payments can be one-time or standing order (recurring) and can be denominated in either EUR, GBP or other chosen [currency](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiation-payment-create-request-amount-currency).  If making domestic GBP-denominated payments, your recipient must have been created with BACS numbers. In general, EUR-denominated payments will be sent via SEPA Credit Transfer, GBP-denominated payments will be sent via the Faster Payments network and for non-Eurozone markets typically via the local payment scheme, but the payment network used will be determined by the institution. Payments sent via Faster Payments will typically arrive immediately, while payments sent via SEPA Credit Transfer or other local payment schemes will typically arrive in one business day.

Standing orders (recurring payments) must be denominated in GBP and can only be sent to recipients in the UK. Once created, standing order payments cannot be modified or canceled via the API. An end user can cancel or modify a standing order directly on their banking application or website, or by contacting the bank. Standing orders will follow the payment rules of the underlying rails (Faster Payments in UK). Payments can be sent Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. If the pre-arranged date falls on a weekend or bank holiday, the payment is made on the next working day. It is not possible to guarantee the exact time the payment will reach the recipient’s account, although at least 90% of standing order payments are sent by 6am.

In the Development environment, payments must be below 5 GBP or other chosen [currency](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiation-payment-create-request-amount-currency). For details on any payment limits in Production, contact your Plaid Account Manager.

<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationpaymentcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": {
    "currency": "GBP",
    "value": 0
  },
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "bacs": {
      "account": "string",
      "sort_code": "string"
    },
    "iban": "stringstringstr",
    "request_refund_details": true,
    "scheme": null
  },
  "recipient_id": "string",
  "reference": "string",
  "schedule": {
    "adjusted_start_date": "1970-01-01",
    "end_date": "1970-01-01",
    "interval": "WEEKLY",
    "interval_execution_day": 0,
    "start_date": "1970-01-01"
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationPaymentCreateRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» amount|body|[PaymentAmount](#schemapaymentamount)|true|The amount and currency of a payment|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[ExternalPaymentOptions](#schemaexternalpaymentoptions)|false|Additional payment options|
|» recipient_id|body|string|true|The ID of the recipient the payment is for.|
|» reference|body|string|true|A reference for the payment. This must be an alphanumeric string with at most 18 characters and must not contain any special characters (since not all institutions support them).<br>In order to track settlement via Payment Confirmation, each payment must have a unique reference. If the reference provided through the API is not unique, Plaid will adjust it.<br>Both the originally provided and automatically adjusted references (if any) can be found in the `reference` and `adjusted_reference` fields, respectively.|
|» schedule|body|[ExternalPaymentScheduleRequest](#schemaexternalpaymentschedulerequest)|false|The schedule that the payment will be executed on. If a schedule is provided, the payment is automatically set up as a standing order. If no schedule is specified, the payment will be executed only once.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "payment_id": "payment-id-sandbox-feca8a7a-5591-4aef-9297-f3062bb735d3",
  "request_id": "4ciYVmesrySiUAB",
  "status": "PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED"
}
```
