`POST /payment_initiation/payment/list`

The `/payment_initiation/payment/list` endpoint can be used to retrieve all created payments. By default, the 10 most recent payments are returned. You can request more payments and paginate through the results using the optional `count` and `cursor` parameters.

<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationpaymentlist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "consent_id": "string",
  "count": 10,
  "cursor": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-payments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationPaymentListRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentlistrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» consent_id|body|string \| null|false|The consent ID. If specified, only payments, executed using this consent, will be returned.|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of payments to return. If `count` is not specified, a maximum of 10 payments will be returned, beginning with the most recent payment before the cursor (if specified).|
|» cursor|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|A string in RFC 3339 format (i.e. "2019-12-06T22:35:49Z"). Only payments created before the cursor will be returned.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
```

## Reverse an existing payment

<a id="opIdpaymentInitiationPaymentReverse"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/payment/reverse \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": {
      "currency": "GBP",
      "value": 0
    },
    "client_id": "string",
    "idempotency_key": "string",
    "payment_id": "string",
    "reference": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/payment/reverse`

Reverse a settled payment from a Plaid virtual account.

The original payment must be in a settled state to be refunded.
To refund partially, specify the amount as part of the request.
If the amount is not specified, the refund amount will be equal to all
of the remaining payment amount that has not been refunded yet.
If the remaining amount is less than one unit of currency
(e.g. 1 GBP or 1 EUR), the refund will fail.

The refund will go back to the source account that initiated the payment.
The original payment must have been initiated to a Plaid virtual account
so that this account can be used to initiate the refund.


<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationpaymentreverse">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": {
    "currency": "GBP",
    "value": 0
  },
  "client_id": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "payment_id": "string",
  "reference": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="reverse-an-existing-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationPaymentReverseRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentreverserequest)|true|none|
|» amount|body|[PaymentAmountToRefund](#schemapaymentamounttorefund)|false|The amount and currency of a payment|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» idempotency_key|body|[WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey](#schemawallettransactionidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique wallet transaction. Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a wallet transaction fails due to a network connection error, then after a minimum delay of one minute, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single wallet transaction is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any transaction that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 24 hours of the first request, from being processed.|
|» payment_id|body|string|true|The ID of the payment to reverse|
|» reference|body|string|true|A reference for the refund. This must be an alphanumeric string with 6 to 18 characters and must not contain any special characters or spaces.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "refund_id": "wallet-transaction-id-production-c5f8cd31-6cae-4cad-9b0d-f7c10be9cc4b",
  "request_id": "HtlKzBX0fMeF7mU",
  "status": "INITIATED"
}
```

<h3 id="reverse-an-existing-payment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[PaymentInitiationPaymentReverseResponse](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentreverseresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Create payment token

<a id="opIdcreatePaymentToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/payment/token/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "payment_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/payment/token/create`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

The `/payment_initiation/payment/token/create` endpoint has been deprecated. New Plaid customers will be unable to use this endpoint, and existing customers are encouraged to migrate to the newer, `link_token`-based flow. The recommended flow is to provide the `payment_id` to `/link/token/create`, which returns a `link_token` used to initialize Link.

The `/payment_initiation/payment/token/create` is used to create a `payment_token`, which can then be used in Link initialization to enter a payment initiation flow. You can only use a `payment_token` once. If this attempt fails, the end user aborts the flow, or the token expires, you will need to create a new payment token. Creating a new payment token does not require end user input.

<a href="/link/maintain-legacy-integration/#creating-a-payment-token">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "payment_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-payment-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationPaymentTokenCreateRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymenttokencreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» payment_id|body|string|true|The `payment_id` returned from `/payment_initiation/payment/create`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "payment_token": "payment-token-sandbox-feca8a7a-5591-4aef-9297-f3062bb735d3",
  "payment_token_expiration_time": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "request_id": "4ciYVmesrySiUAB"
}
```

## Create payment recipient

<a id="opIdpaymentInitiationRecipientCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/recipient/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "st",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "street": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "bacs": {
      "account": "string",
      "sort_code": "string"
    },
    "client_id": "string",
    "iban": "stringstringstr",
    "name": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/recipient/create`

Create a payment recipient for payment initiation.  The recipient must be in Europe, within a country that is a member of the Single Euro Payment Area (SEPA) or a non-Eurozone country [supported](https://plaid.com/global) by Plaid. For a standing order (recurring) payment, the recipient must be in the UK.

It is recommended to use `bacs` in the UK and `iban` in EU.

The endpoint is idempotent: if a developer has already made a request with the same payment details, Plaid will return the same `recipient_id`.


<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationrecipientcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": {
    "city": "string",
    "country": "st",
    "postal_code": "string",
    "street": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "bacs": {
    "account": "string",
    "sort_code": "string"
  },
  "client_id": "string",
  "iban": "stringstringstr",
  "name": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-payment-recipient-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationRecipientCreateRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationrecipientcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» address|body|[PaymentInitiationAddress](#schemapaymentinitiationaddress)|false|The optional address of the payment recipient.|
|» bacs|body|[RecipientBACSNullable](#schemarecipientbacsnullable)|false|An object containing a BACS account number and sort code. If an IBAN is not provided or if this recipient needs to accept domestic GBP-denominated payments, BACS data is required.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» iban|body|string \| null|false|The International Bank Account Number (IBAN) for the recipient. If BACS data is not provided, an IBAN is required.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the recipient. We recommend using strings of length 18 or less and avoid special characters to ensure compatibility with all institutions.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "recipient_id": "recipient-id-sandbox-9b6b4679-914b-445b-9450-efbdb80296f6",
  "request_id": "4zlKapIkTm8p5KM"
}
```

<h3 id="create-payment-recipient-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[PaymentInitiationRecipientCreateResponse](#schemapaymentinitiationrecipientcreateresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

## Retrieve Auth data

<a id="opIdprocessorAuthGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/auth/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "processor_token": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /processor/auth/get`

The `/processor/auth/get` endpoint returns the bank account and bank identification number (such as the routing number, for US accounts), for a checking or savings account that''s associated with a given `processor_token`. The endpoint also returns high-level account data and balances when available.

Versioning note: API versions 2019-05-29 and earlier use a different schema for the `numbers` object returned by this endpoint. For details, see [Plaid API versioning](https://plaid.com/docs/api/versioning/#version-2020-09-14).


<a href="/api/processors/#processorauthget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "processor_token": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-auth-data-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProcessorAuthGetRequest](#schemaprocessorauthgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» processor_token|body|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Retrieve Balance data

<a id="opIdprocessorBalanceGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/balance/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "min_last_updated_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "processor_token": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /processor/balance/get`

The `/processor/balance/get` endpoint returns the real-time balance for each of an Item's accounts. While other endpoints may return a balance object, only `/processor/balance/get` forces the available and current balance fields to be refreshed rather than cached. 

<a href="/api/processors/#processorbalanceget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "min_last_updated_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "processor_token": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-balance-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProcessorBalanceGetRequest](#schemaprocessorbalancegetrequest)|true|The `/processor/balance/get` endpoint returns the real-time balance for the account associated with a given `processor_token`.<br><br>The current balance is the total amount of funds in the account. The available balance is the current balance less any outstanding holds or debits that have not yet posted to the account.<br><br>Note that not all institutions calculate the available balance. In the event that available balance is unavailable from the institution, Plaid will return an available balance value of `null`.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[ProcessorBalanceGetRequestOptions](#schemaprocessorbalancegetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/processor/balance/get` results.|
|» processor_token|body|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "account": {
    "account_id": "QKKzevvp33HxPWpoqn6rI13BxW4awNSjnw4xv",
    "balances": {
      "available": 100,
      "current": 110,
      "iso_currency_code": "USD",
      "limit": null,
      "unofficial_currency_code": null
    },
    "mask": "0000",
    "name": "Plaid Checking",
    "official_name": "Plaid Gold Checking",
    "subtype": "checking",
    "type": "depository"
  },

}
```

<a id="opIdprocessorBankTransferCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/bank_transfer/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "ach_class": "ccd",
    "amount": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "custom_tag": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "idempotency_key": "string",
    "iso_currency_code": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "network": "ach",
    "origination_account_id": "string",
    "processor_token": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "type": "debit",
    "user": {
      "email_address": "string",
      "legal_name": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /processor/bank_transfer/create`

Use the `/processor/bank_transfer/create` endpoint to initiate a new bank transfer as a processor

<a href="/api/processors/#bank_transfercreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ach_class": "ccd",
  "amount": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "custom_tag": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "network": "ach",
  "origination_account_id": "string",
  "processor_token": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "type": "debit",
  "user": {
    "email_address": "string",
    "legal_name": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-bank-transfer-as-a-processor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProcessorBankTransferCreateRequest](#schemaprocessorbanktransfercreaterequest)|true|none|
|» ach_class|body|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|» amount|body|[BankTransferAmount](#schemabanktransferamount)|true|The amount of the bank transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» custom_tag|body|string \| null|false|An arbitrary string provided by the client for storage with the bank transfer. May be up to 100 characters.|
|» description|body|string|true|The transfer description. Maximum of 10 characters.|
|» idempotency_key|body|[BankTransferIdempotencyKey](#schemabanktransferidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique bank transfer. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a bank transfer fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single bank transfer is created.|
|» iso_currency_code|body|string|true|The currency of the transfer amount – should be set to "USD".|
|» metadata|body|[BankTransferMetadata](#schemabanktransfermetadata)|false|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|» network|body|[BankTransferNetwork](#schemabanktransfernetwork)|true|The network or rails used for the transfer. Valid options are `ach`, `same-day-ach`, or `wire`.|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|Plaid’s unique identifier for the origination account for this transfer. If you have more than one origination account, this value must be specified.|
|» processor_token|body|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» type|body|[BankTransferType](#schemabanktransfertype)|true|The type of bank transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|
|» user|body|[BankTransferUser](#schemabanktransferuser)|true|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» ach_class|ccd|
|» ach_class|ppd|
|» ach_class|tel|
|» ach_class|web|
|» network|ach|
|» network|same-day-ach|
|» network|wire|
|» type|debit|
|» type|credit|

## Report whether you initiated an ACH transaction

<a id="opIdprocessorSignalDecisionReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/signal/decision/report \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount_instantly_available": 0,
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_transaction_id": "string",
    "days_funds_on_hold": 0,
    "decision_outcome": "APPROVE",
    "initiated": true,
    "payment_method": "SAME_DAY_ACH",
    "processor_token": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /processor/signal/decision/report`

After calling `/processor/signal/evaluate`, call `/processor/signal/decision/report` to report whether the transaction was initiated. This endpoint will return an [`INVALID_FIELD`](/docs/errors/invalid-request/#invalid_field) error if called a second time with a different value for `initiated`.

<a href="/api/processors/#processorsignaldecisionreport">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount_instantly_available": 0,
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_transaction_id": "string",
  "days_funds_on_hold": 0,
  "decision_outcome": "APPROVE",
  "initiated": true,
  "payment_method": "SAME_DAY_ACH",
  "processor_token": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="report-whether-you-initiated-an-ach-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProcessorSignalDecisionReportRequest](#schemaprocessorsignaldecisionreportrequest)|true|none|
|» amount_instantly_available|body|number(double) \| null|false|The amount (in USD) made available to your customers instantly following the debit transaction. It could be a partial amount of the requested transaction (example: 102.05).|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_transaction_id|body|string|true|Must be the same as the `client_transaction_id` supplied when calling `/signal/evaluate`|
|» days_funds_on_hold|body|integer \| null|false|The actual number of days (hold time) since the ACH debit transaction that you wait before making funds available to your customers. The holding time could affect the ACH return rate.<br><br>For example, use 0 if you make funds available to your customers instantly or the same day following the debit transaction, or 1 if you make funds available the next day following the debit initialization.|
|» decision_outcome|body|[SignalDecisionOutcome](#schemasignaldecisionoutcome)|false|The payment decision from the risk assessment.<br><br>`APPROVE`: approve the transaction without requiring further actions from your customers. For example, use this field if you are placing a standard hold for all the approved transactions before making funds available to your customers. You should also use this field if you decide to accelerate the fund availability for your customers.<br><br>`REVIEW`: the transaction requires manual review<br><br>`REJECT`: reject the transaction<br><br>`TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES`: for example, placing a longer hold on funds than those approved transactions or introducing customer frictions such as step-up verification/authentication<br><br>`NOT_EVALUATED`: if only logging the Signal results without using them<br><br>Possible values:  `APPROVE`, `REVIEW`, `REJECT`, `TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES`, `NOT_EVALUATED`<br>|
|» initiated|body|boolean|true|`true` if the ACH transaction was initiated, `false` otherwise.<br><br>This field must be returned as a boolean. If formatted incorrectly, this will result in an [`INVALID_FIELD`](/docs/errors/invalid-request/#invalid_field) error.|
|» payment_method|body|[SignalPaymentMethod](#schemasignalpaymentmethod)|false|The payment method to complete the transaction after the risk assessment. It may be different from the default payment method.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by NACHA. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day<br><br>`NEXT_DAY_ACH`: Next Day ACH settlement for debit transactions, offered by some payment processors<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: standard ACH by NACHA<br><br>`REAL_TIME_PAYMENTS`: real-time payments such as RTP and FedNow<br><br>`DEBIT_CARD`: if the default payment is over debit card networks<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: if there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods<br><br>Possible values: `SAME_DAY_ACH`, `NEXT_DAY_ACH`, `STANDARD_ACH`, `REAL_TIME_PAYMENTS`, `DEBIT_CARD`, `MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`<br>|
|» processor_token|body|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

#### Enumerated Values

## Evaluate a planned ACH transaction

<a id="opIdprocessorSignalEvaluate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/signal/evaluate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 0,
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_transaction_id": "string",
    "client_user_id": "string",
    "default_payment_method": "string",
    "device": {
      "ip_address": "string",
      "user_agent": "string"
    },
    "is_recurring": true,
    "processor_token": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user": {
      "address": {
        "city": "string",
        "country": "string",
        "postal_code": "string",
        "region": "string",
        "street": "string"
      },
      "email_address": "string",
      "name": {
        "family_name": "string",
        "given_name": "string",
        "middle_name": "string",
        "prefix": "string",
        "suffix": "string"
      },
      "phone_number": "string"
    },
    "user_present": true
  }'
```

`POST /processor/signal/evaluate`

Use `/processor/signal/evaluate` to evaluate a planned ACH transaction as a processor to get a return risk assessment (such as a risk score and risk tier) and additional risk signals.

In order to obtain a valid score for an ACH transaction, Plaid must have an access token for the account, and the Item must be healthy (receiving product updates) or have recently been in a healthy state. If the transaction does not meet eligibility requirements, an error will be returned corresponding to the underlying cause. If `/processor/signal/evaluate` is called on the same transaction multiple times within a 24-hour period, cached results may be returned. For more information please refer to our error documentation on [item errors](/docs/errors/item/) and [Link in Update Mode](/docs/link/update-mode/).

Note: This request may take some time to complete if Signal is being added to an existing Item. This is because Plaid must communicate directly with the institution when retrieving the data for the first time.

<a href="/api/processors/#processorsignalevaluate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_transaction_id": "string",
  "client_user_id": "string",
  "default_payment_method": "string",
  "device": {
    "ip_address": "string",
    "user_agent": "string"
  },
  "is_recurring": true,
  "processor_token": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user": {
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "street": "string"
    },
    "email_address": "string",
    "name": {
      "family_name": "string",
      "given_name": "string",
      "middle_name": "string",
      "prefix": "string",
      "suffix": "string"
    },
    "phone_number": "string"
  },
  "user_present": true
}
```

<h3 id="evaluate-a-planned-ach-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProcessorSignalEvaluateRequest](#schemaprocessorsignalevaluaterequest)|true|none|
|» amount|body|number(double)|true|The transaction amount, in USD (e.g. `102.05`)|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_transaction_id|body|string|true|The unique ID that you would like to use to refer to this transaction. For your convenience mapping your internal data, you could use your internal ID/identifier for this transaction. The max length for this field is 36 characters.|
|» client_user_id|body|string|false|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. This ID is used to correlate requests by a user with multiple Items. The max length for this field is 36 characters. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|» default_payment_method|body|string \| null|false|The default ACH or non-ACH payment method to complete the transaction.<br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by NACHA. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day<br>`NEXT_DAY_ACH`: Next Day ACH settlement for debit transactions, offered by some payment processors<br>`STANDARD_ACH`: standard ACH by NACHA<br>`REAL_TIME_PAYMENTS`: real-time payments such as RTP and FedNow<br>`DEBIT_CARD`: if the default payment is over debit card networks<br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: if there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods<br>Possible values:  `SAME_DAY_ACH`, `NEXT_DAY_ACH`, `STANDARD_ACH`, `REAL_TIME_PAYMENTS`, `DEBIT_CARD`, `MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`|
|» device|body|[SignalDevice](#schemasignaldevice)|false|Details about the end user's device|
|» is_recurring|body|boolean \| null|false|**true** if the ACH transaction is a recurring transaction; **false** otherwise |
|» processor_token|body|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user|body|[SignalUser](#schemasignaluser)|false|Details about the end user initiating the transaction (i.e., the account holder).|
|» user_present|body|boolean \| null|false|`true` if the end user is present while initiating the ACH transfer and the endpoint is being called; `false` otherwise (for example, when the ACH transfer is scheduled and the end user is not present, or you call this endpoint after the ACH transfer but before submitting the Nacha file for ACH processing).|

## Create Stripe bank account token

<a id="opIdprocessorStripeBankAccountTokenCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/stripe/bank_account_token/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "account_id": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /processor/stripe/bank_account_token/create`


Used to create a token suitable for sending to Stripe to enable Plaid-Stripe integrations. For a detailed guide on integrating Stripe, see [Add Stripe to your app](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/partnerships/stripe/).

Note that the Stripe bank account token is a one-time use token. To store bank account information for later use, you can use a Stripe customer object and create an associated bank account from the token, or you can use a Stripe Custom account and create an associated external bank account from the token. This bank account information should work indefinitely, unless the user's bank account information changes or they revoke Plaid's permissions to access their account. Stripe bank account information cannot be modified once the bank account token has been created. If you ever need to change the bank account details used by Stripe for a specific customer, have the user go through Link again and create a new bank account token from the new `access_token`.

Bank account tokens can also be revoked, using `/item/remove`.'

<a href="/api/processors/#processorstripebank_account_tokencreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "account_id": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-stripe-bank-account-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProcessorStripeBankAccountTokenCreateRequest](#schemaprocessorstripebankaccounttokencreaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» account_id|body|string|true|The `account_id` value obtained from the `onSuccess` callback in Link|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "xrQNYZ7Zoh6R7gV",
  "stripe_bank_account_token": "btok_5oEetfLzPklE1fwJZ7SG"
}
```

`POST /processor/token/create`

Used to create a token suitable for sending to one of Plaid's partners to enable integrations. Note that Stripe partnerships use bank account tokens instead; see `/processor/stripe/bank_account_token/create` for creating tokens for use with Stripe integrations. Once created, a processor token for a given Item cannot be modified or updated. If the account must be linked to a new or different partner resource, create a new Item by having the user go through the Link flow again; a new processor token can then be created from the new `access_token`. Processor tokens can also be revoked, using `/item/remove`.

<a href="/api/processors/#processortokencreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json

  "access_token": "string",
  "account_id": "string",
```

`POST /sandbox/bank_transfer/simulate`

Use the `/sandbox/bank_transfer/simulate` endpoint to simulate a bank transfer event in the Sandbox environment.  Note that while an event will be simulated and will appear when using endpoints such as `/bank_transfer/event/sync` or `/bank_transfer/event/list`, no transactions will actually take place and funds will not move between accounts, even within the Sandbox.

<a href="/bank-transfers/reference/#sandboxbank_transfersimulate">External documentation</a>

```json
{
  "bank_transfer_id": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "event_type": "string",
  "failure_reason": {
    "ach_return_code": "string",
    "description": "string"
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

|» event_type|body|string|true|The asynchronous event to be simulated. May be: `posted`, `failed`, or `reversed`.<br><br>An error will be returned if the event type is incompatible with the current transfer status. Compatible status --> event type transitions include:<br><br>`pending` --> `failed`<br><br>`pending` --> `posted`<br><br>`posted` --> `reversed`<br>|
|» failure_reason|body|[BankTransferFailure](#schemabanktransferfailure)|false|The failure reason if the type of this transfer is `"failed"` or `"reversed"`. Null value otherwise.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Fire a test webhook

<a id="opIdsandboxItemFireWebhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/item/fire_webhook \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "webhook_code": "DEFAULT_UPDATE",
    "webhook_type": "AUTH"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/item/fire_webhook`

The `/sandbox/item/fire_webhook` endpoint is used to test that code correctly handles webhooks. This endpoint can trigger the following webhooks:

`DEFAULT_UPDATE`: Transactions update webhook to be fired for a given Sandbox Item. If the Item does not support Transactions, a `SANDBOX_PRODUCT_NOT_ENABLED` error will result.

`NEW_ACCOUNTS_AVAILABLE`: Webhook to be fired for a given Sandbox Item created with Account Select v2.

`AUTH_DATA_UPDATE`: Webhook to be fired for a given Sandbox Item created with Auth as an enabled product.

`RECURRING_TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE`: Recurring Transactions webhook to be fired for a given Sandbox Item. If the Item does not support Recurring Transactions, a `SANDBOX_PRODUCT_NOT_ENABLED` error will result.

`SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE`: Transactions webhook to be fired for a given Sandbox Item.  If the Item does not support Transactions, a `SANDBOX_PRODUCT_NOT_ENABLED` error will result.

Note that this endpoint is provided for developer ease-of-use and is not required for testing webhooks; webhooks will also fire in Sandbox under the same conditions that they would in Production or Development.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxitemfire_webhook">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "webhook_code": "DEFAULT_UPDATE",
  "webhook_type": "AUTH"
}
```

<h3 id="fire-a-test-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SandboxItemFireWebhookRequest](#schemasandboxitemfirewebhookrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» webhook_code|body|string|true|The webhook codes that can be fired by this test endpoint.|
|» webhook_type|body|[WebhookType](#schemawebhooktype)|false|The webhook types that can be fired by this test endpoint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» webhook_code|DEFAULT_UPDATE|
|» webhook_code|NEW_ACCOUNTS_AVAILABLE|
|» webhook_code|AUTH_DATA_UPDATE|
|» webhook_code|RECURRING_TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE|
|» webhook_code|SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE|
|» webhook_type|AUTH|
|» webhook_type|HOLDINGS|
|» webhook_type|INVESTMENTS_TRANSACTIONS|
|» webhook_type|ITEM|
|» webhook_type|LIABILITIES|
|» webhook_type|TRANSACTIONS|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "request_id": "1vwmF5TBQwiqfwP",
  "webhook_fired": true
}
```

```json
  ],

}
```

## Force a Sandbox Item into an error state

<a id="opIdsandboxItemResetLogin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/item/reset_login \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/item/reset_login`

`/sandbox/item/reset_login/` forces an Item into an `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` state in order to simulate an Item whose login is no longer valid. This makes it easy to test Link's [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode) flow in the Sandbox environment.  After calling `/sandbox/item/reset_login`, You can then use Plaid Link update mode to restore the Item to a good state. An `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` webhook will also be fired after a call to this endpoint, if one is associated with the Item.


In the Sandbox, Items will transition to an `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` error state automatically after 30 days, even if this endpoint is not called.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxitemreset_login">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="force-a-sandbox-item-into-an-error-state-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SandboxItemResetLoginRequest](#schemasandboxitemresetloginrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "m8MDnv9okwxFNBV",
  "reset_login": true
}
```

<h3 id="force-a-sandbox-item-into-an-error-state-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[SandboxItemResetLoginResponse](#schemasandboxitemresetloginresponse)|

<aside class="warning">

clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

`POST /sandbox/item/set_verification_status`

The `/sandbox/item/set_verification_status` endpoint can be used to change the verification status of an Item in in the Sandbox in order to simulate the Automated Micro-deposit flow.

Note that not all Plaid developer accounts are enabled for micro-deposit based verification by default. Your account must be enabled for this feature in order to test it in Sandbox. To enable this features or check your status, contact your account manager or [submit a product access Support ticket](https://dashboard.plaid.com/support/new/product-and-development/product-troubleshooting/request-product-access).

For more information on testing Automated Micro-deposits in Sandbox, see [Auth full coverage testing](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/testing#).

## Reset the login of a Payment Profile

<a id="opIdsandboxPaymentProfileResetLogin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/payment_profile/reset_login \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/payment_profile/reset_login`

`/sandbox/payment_profile/reset_login/` forces a Payment Profile into a state where the login is no longer valid. This makes it easy to test update mode for Payment Profile in the Sandbox environment.

 After calling `/sandbox/payment_profile/reset_login`, calls to the `/transfer/authorization/create` with the Payment Profile will result in a `decision_rationale` `PAYMENT_PROFILE_LOGIN_REQUIRED`. You can then use update mode for Payment Profile to restore it into a good state.

 In order to invoke this endpoint, you must first [create a Payment Profile](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/add-to-app/#create-a-payment-profile-optional) and [go through the Link flow](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/add-to-app/#create-a-link-token).

```json
  "secret": "string"
```

`POST /sandbox/public_token/create`

Use the `/sandbox/public_token/create` endpoint to create a valid `public_token`  for an arbitrary institution ID, initial products, and test credentials. The created `public_token` maps to a new Sandbox Item. You can then call `/item/public_token/exchange` to exchange the `public_token` for an `access_token` and perform all API actions. `/sandbox/public_token/create` can also be used with the [`user_custom` test username](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/user-custom) to generate a test account with custom data. `/sandbox/public_token/create` cannot be used with OAuth institutions.

```json
    "income_verification": {
      "bank_income": {
        "days_requested": 0
      },
      "income_source_types": [
        "bank"
      ]
    },
    "override_password": "pass_good",
    "override_username": "user_good",
    "transactions": {
      "end_date": "1970-01-01",

    },
```

## Simulate a transfer event in Sandbox

<a id="opIdsandboxTransferSimulate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/transfer/simulate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "event_type": "string",
    "failure_reason": {
      "ach_return_code": "string",
      "description": "string"
    },
    "secret": "string",
    "transfer_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/transfer/simulate`

Use the `/sandbox/transfer/simulate` endpoint to simulate a transfer event in the Sandbox environment.  Note that while an event will be simulated and will appear when using endpoints such as `/transfer/event/sync` or `/transfer/event/list`, no transactions will actually take place and funds will not move between accounts, even within the Sandbox.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxtransfersimulate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "event_type": "string",
  "failure_reason": {
    "ach_return_code": "string",
    "description": "string"
  },
  "secret": "string",
  "transfer_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="simulate-a-transfer-event-in-sandbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SandboxTransferSimulateRequest](#schemasandboxtransfersimulaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» event_type|body|string|true|The asynchronous event to be simulated. May be: `posted`, `settled`, `failed`, or `returned`.<br><br>An error will be returned if the event type is incompatible with the current transfer status. Compatible status --> event type transitions include:<br><br>`pending` --> `failed`<br><br>`pending` --> `posted`<br><br>`posted` --> `returned`<br><br>`posted` --> `settled`<br>|
|» failure_reason|body|[TransferFailure](#schematransferfailure)|false|The failure reason if the event type for a transfer is `"failed"` or `"returned"`. Null value otherwise.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» transfer_id|body|[TransferID](#schematransferid)|true|Plaid’s unique identifier for a transfer.|

```json
  "request_id": "mdqfuVxeoza6mhu"
}
```

```json
  ],

}
```

## Advance a test clock

<a id="opIdsandboxTransferTestClockAdvance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/transfer/test_clock/advance \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "new_virtual_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "secret": "string",
    "test_clock_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/transfer/test_clock/advance`

Use the `/sandbox/transfer/test_clock/advance` endpoint to advance a `test_clock` in the Sandbox environment.

A test clock object represents an independent timeline and has a `virtual_time` field indicating the current timestamp of the timeline. A test clock can be advanced by incrementing `virtual_time`, but may never go back to a lower `virtual_time`.

If a test clock is advanced, we will simulate the changes that ought to occur during the time that elapsed.
For instance, a client creates a weekly recurring transfer with a test clock set at t. When the client advances the test clock by setting `virtual_time` = t + 15 days, 2 new originations should be created, along with the webhook events.

The advancement of the test clock from its current `virtual_time` should be limited such that there are no more than 20 originations resulting from the advance operation on each `recurring_transfer` associated with the `test_clock`.
For instance, if the recurring transfer associated with this test clock originates once every 4 weeks, you can advance the `virtual_time` up to 80 weeks on each API call.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxtransfertest_clockadvance">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "new_virtual_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "secret": "string",
  "test_clock_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="advance-a-test-clock-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SandboxTransferTestClockAdvanceRequest](#schemasandboxtransfertestclockadvancerequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» new_virtual_time|body|[VirtualTime](#schemavirtualtime)|true|The virtual timestamp on the test clock. This will be of the form `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» test_clock_id|body|[TransferTestClockID](#schematransfertestclockid)|true|Plaid’s unique identifier for a test clock.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "mdqfuVxeoza6mhu"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "causes": [
    null
  ],
  "display_message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "error_code": "string",
  "error_message": "string",
  "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "request_id": "string",
  "status": 0,
  "suggested_action": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="advance-a-test-clock-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|

## Report whether you initiated an ACH transaction

<a id="opIdsignalDecisionReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/signal/decision/report \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount_instantly_available": 0,
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_transaction_id": "string",
    "days_funds_on_hold": 0,
    "decision_outcome": "APPROVE",
    "initiated": true,
    "payment_method": "SAME_DAY_ACH",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /signal/decision/report`

After calling `/signal/evaluate`, call `/signal/decision/report` to report whether the transaction was initiated. This endpoint will return an [`INVALID_FIELD`](/docs/errors/invalid-request/#invalid_field) error if called a second time with a different value for `initiated`.

<a href="/api/products/signal#signaldecisionreport">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount_instantly_available": 0,
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_transaction_id": "string",
  "days_funds_on_hold": 0,
  "decision_outcome": "APPROVE",
  "initiated": true,
  "payment_method": "SAME_DAY_ACH",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="report-whether-you-initiated-an-ach-transaction-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SignalDecisionReportRequest](#schemasignaldecisionreportrequest)|true|none|
|» amount_instantly_available|body|number(double) \| null|false|The amount (in USD) made available to your customers instantly following the debit transaction. It could be a partial amount of the requested transaction (example: 102.05).|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_transaction_id|body|string|true|Must be the same as the `client_transaction_id` supplied when calling `/signal/evaluate`|
|» days_funds_on_hold|body|integer \| null|false|The actual number of days (hold time) since the ACH debit transaction that you wait before making funds available to your customers. The holding time could affect the ACH return rate.<br><br>For example, use 0 if you make funds available to your customers instantly or the same day following the debit transaction, or 1 if you make funds available the next day following the debit initialization.|
|» decision_outcome|body|[SignalDecisionOutcome](#schemasignaldecisionoutcome)|false|The payment decision from the risk assessment.<br><br>`APPROVE`: approve the transaction without requiring further actions from your customers. For example, use this field if you are placing a standard hold for all the approved transactions before making funds available to your customers. You should also use this field if you decide to accelerate the fund availability for your customers.<br><br>`REVIEW`: the transaction requires manual review<br><br>`REJECT`: reject the transaction<br><br>`TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES`: for example, placing a longer hold on funds than those approved transactions or introducing customer frictions such as step-up verification/authentication<br><br>`NOT_EVALUATED`: if only logging the Signal results without using them<br><br>Possible values:  `APPROVE`, `REVIEW`, `REJECT`, `TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES`, `NOT_EVALUATED`<br>|
|» initiated|body|boolean|true|`true` if the ACH transaction was initiated, `false` otherwise.<br><br>This field must be returned as a boolean. If formatted incorrectly, this will result in an [`INVALID_FIELD`](/docs/errors/invalid-request/#invalid_field) error.|
|» payment_method|body|[SignalPaymentMethod](#schemasignalpaymentmethod)|false|The payment method to complete the transaction after the risk assessment. It may be different from the default payment method.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by NACHA. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day<br><br>`NEXT_DAY_ACH`: Next Day ACH settlement for debit transactions, offered by some payment processors<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: standard ACH by NACHA<br><br>`REAL_TIME_PAYMENTS`: real-time payments such as RTP and FedNow<br><br>`DEBIT_CARD`: if the default payment is over debit card networks<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: if there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods<br><br>Possible values: `SAME_DAY_ACH`, `NEXT_DAY_ACH`, `STANDARD_ACH`, `REAL_TIME_PAYMENTS`, `DEBIT_CARD`, `MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`<br>|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» decision_outcome|APPROVE|
|» decision_outcome|REVIEW|
|» decision_outcome|REJECT|
|» decision_outcome|TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES|
|» decision_outcome|NOT_EVALUATED|
|» payment_method|SAME_DAY_ACH|
|» payment_method|NEXT_DAY_ACH|
|» payment_method|STANDARD_ACH|
|» payment_method|REAL_TIME_PAYMENTS|
|» payment_method|DEBIT_CARD|
|» payment_method|MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "mdqfuVxeoza6mhu"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "causes": [
    null
  ],
  "display_message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "error_code": "string",
  "error_message": "string",
  "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "request_id": "string",
  "status": 0,
  "suggested_action": "string"
}
```

## Evaluate a planned ACH transaction

<a id="opIdsignalEvaluate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/signal/evaluate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "account_id": "string",
    "amount": 0,
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_transaction_id": "string",
    "client_user_id": "string",
    "default_payment_method": "string",
    "device": {
      "ip_address": "string",
      "user_agent": "string"
    },
    "is_recurring": true,
    "secret": "string",
    "user": {
      "address": {
        "city": "string",
        "country": "string",
        "postal_code": "string",
        "region": "string",
        "street": "string"
      },
      "email_address": "string",
      "name": {
        "family_name": "string",
        "given_name": "string",
        "middle_name": "string",
        "prefix": "string",
        "suffix": "string"
      },
      "phone_number": "string"
    },
    "user_present": true
  }'
```

`POST /signal/evaluate`

Use `/signal/evaluate` to evaluate a planned ACH transaction to get a return risk assessment (such as a risk score and risk tier) and additional risk signals.

In order to obtain a valid score for an ACH transaction, Plaid must have an access token for the account, and the Item must be healthy (receiving product updates) or have recently been in a healthy state. If the transaction does not meet eligibility requirements, an error will be returned corresponding to the underlying cause. If `/signal/evaluate` is called on the same transaction multiple times within a 24-hour period, cached results may be returned. For more information please refer to the error documentation on [Item errors](/docs/errors/item/) and [Link in Update Mode](/docs/link/update-mode/).

Note: This request may take some time to complete if Signal is being added to an existing Item. This is because Plaid must communicate directly with the institution when retrieving the data for the first time.

<a href="/api/products/signal#signalevaluate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "account_id": "string",
  "amount": 0,
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_transaction_id": "string",
  "client_user_id": "string",
  "default_payment_method": "string",
  "device": {
    "ip_address": "string",
    "user_agent": "string"
  },
  "is_recurring": true,
  "secret": "string",
  "user": {
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "street": "string"
    },
    "email_address": "string",
    "name": {
      "family_name": "string",
      "given_name": "string",
      "middle_name": "string",
      "prefix": "string",
      "suffix": "string"
    },
    "phone_number": "string"
  },
  "user_present": true
}
```

<h3 id="evaluate-a-planned-ach-transaction-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SignalEvaluateRequest](#schemasignalevaluaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» account_id|body|string|true|The Plaid `account_id` of the account that is the funding source for the proposed transaction. The `account_id` is returned in the `/accounts/get` endpoint as well as the [`onSuccess`](/docs/link/ios/#link-ios-onsuccess-linkSuccess-metadata-accounts-id) callback metadata.<br><br>This will return an [`INVALID_ACCOUNT_ID`](/docs/errors/invalid-input/#invalid_account_id) error if the account has been removed at the bank or if the `account_id` is no longer valid.|
|» amount|body|number(double)|true|The transaction amount, in USD (e.g. `102.05`)|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_transaction_id|body|string|true|The unique ID that you would like to use to refer to this transaction. For your convenience mapping your internal data, you could use your internal ID/identifier for this transaction. The max length for this field is 36 characters.|
|» client_user_id|body|string|false|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. This ID is used to correlate requests by a user with multiple Items. The max length for this field is 36 characters. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|» default_payment_method|body|string \| null|false|The default ACH or non-ACH payment method to complete the transaction.<br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by NACHA. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day<br>`NEXT_DAY_ACH`: Next Day ACH settlement for debit transactions, offered by some payment processors<br>`STANDARD_ACH`: standard ACH by NACHA<br>`REAL_TIME_PAYMENTS`: real-time payments such as RTP and FedNow<br>`DEBIT_CARD`: if the default payment is over debit card networks<br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: if there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods<br>Possible values:  `SAME_DAY_ACH`, `NEXT_DAY_ACH`, `STANDARD_ACH`, `REAL_TIME_PAYMENTS`, `DEBIT_CARD`, `MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`|
|» device|body|[SignalDevice](#schemasignaldevice)|false|Details about the end user's device|
|» is_recurring|body|boolean \| null|false|`true` if the ACH transaction is a recurring transaction; `false` otherwise |
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user|body|[SignalUser](#schemasignaluser)|false|Details about the end user initiating the transaction (i.e., the account holder).|
|» user_present|body|boolean \| null|false|`true` if the end user is present while initiating the ACH transfer and the endpoint is being called; `false` otherwise (for example, when the ACH transfer is scheduled and the end user is not present, or you call this endpoint after the ACH transfer but before submitting the Nacha file for ACH processing).|

## Opt-in an Item to Signal

<a id="opIdsignalPrepare"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/signal/prepare \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /signal/prepare`

When Link is not initialized with Signal, call `/signal/prepare` to opt-in that Item to the Signal data collection process, developing a Signal score.

If you are using other Plaid products after Link, e.g. Identity or Assets, call `/signal/prepare` after those product calls are complete.

Example flow: Link is initialized with Auth, call `/auth/get` for the account and routing number, call `/identity/get` to retrieve bank ownership details, then call `/signal/prepare` to begin Signal data collection. Later, once you have obtained details about the proposed transaction from the user, call `/signal/evaluate` for a Signal score. For more information please see [Recommendations for initializing Link with specific product combinations](https://www.plaid.com/docs/link/initializing-products/#recommendations-for-initializing-link-with-specific-product-combinations).

<a href="/api/products/signal#signalprepare">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

|body|body|[TransactionsEnrichGetRequest](#schematransactionsenrichgetrequest)|true|none|
|» account_type|body|string|true|The account type for the requested transactions (either `depository` or `credit`).|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» transactions|body|[[ClientProvidedTransaction](#schemaclientprovidedtransaction)]|true|An array of transaction objects to be enriched by Plaid. Maximum of 100 transactions per request.|

## Get transaction data

<a id="opIdtransactionsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transactions/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "end_date": "1970-01-01",
    "options": {
      "account_ids": [
        "string"
      ],
      "count": 100,
      "include_logo_and_counterparty_beta": false,
      "include_original_description": false,
      "include_personal_finance_category": false,
      "include_personal_finance_category_beta": false,
      "offset": 0
    },
    "secret": "string",
    "start_date": "1970-01-01"
  }'
```

`POST /transactions/get`

The `/transactions/get` endpoint allows developers to receive user-authorized transaction data for credit, depository, and some loan-type accounts (only those with account subtype `student`; coverage may be limited). For transaction history from investments accounts, use the [Investments endpoint](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/investments/) instead. Transaction data is standardized across financial institutions, and in many cases transactions are linked to a clean name, entity type, location, and category. Similarly, account data is standardized and returned with a clean name, number, balance, and other meta information where available.

Transactions are returned in reverse-chronological order, and the sequence of transaction ordering is stable and will not shift.  Transactions are not immutable and can also be removed altogether by the institution; a removed transaction will no longer appear in `/transactions/get`.  For more details, see [Pending and posted transactions](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/transactions-data/#pending-and-posted-transactions).

Due to the potentially large number of transactions associated with an Item, results are paginated. Manipulate the `count` and `offset` parameters in conjunction with the `total_transactions` response body field to fetch all available transactions.

Data returned by `/transactions/get` will be the data available for the Item as of the most recent successful check for new transactions. Plaid typically checks for new data multiple times a day, but these checks may occur less frequently, such as once a day, depending on the institution. An Item's `status.transactions.last_successful_update` field will show the timestamp of the most recent successful update. To force Plaid to check for new transactions, you can use the `/transactions/refresh` endpoint.

Note that data may not be immediately available to `/transactions/get`. Plaid will begin to prepare transactions data upon Item link, if Link was initialized with `transactions`, or upon the first call to `/transactions/get`, if it wasn't. To be alerted when transaction data is ready to be fetched, listen for the [`INITIAL_UPDATE`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#initial_update) and [`HISTORICAL_UPDATE`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#historical_update) webhooks. If no transaction history is ready when `/transactions/get` is called, it will return a `PRODUCT_NOT_READY` error.

<a href="/api/products/transactions/#transactionsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "end_date": "1970-01-01",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "count": 100,
    "include_logo_and_counterparty_beta": false,
    "include_original_description": false,
    "include_personal_finance_category": false,
    "include_personal_finance_category_beta": false,
    "offset": 0
  },
  "secret": "string",
  "start_date": "1970-01-01"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransactionsGetRequest](#schematransactionsgetrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» end_date|body|string(date)|true|The latest date for which data should be returned. Dates should be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.|

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» start_date|body|string(date)|true|The earliest date for which data should be returned. Dates should be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.|

## Fetch recurring transaction streams

<a id="opIdtransactionsRecurringGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transactions/recurring/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "client_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "include_personal_finance_category": false
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /transactions/recurring/get`

The `/transactions/recurring/get` endpoint allows developers to receive a summary of the recurring outflow and inflow streams (expenses and deposits) from a user’s checking, savings or credit card accounts. Additionally, Plaid provides key insights about each recurring stream including the category, merchant, last amount, and more. Developers can use these insights to build tools and experiences that help their users better manage cash flow, monitor subscriptions, reduce spend, and stay on track with bill payments.

This endpoint is offered as an add-on to Transactions. To request access to this endpoint, submit a [product access request](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/products) or contact your Plaid account manager.

This endpoint can only be called on an Item that has already been initialized with Transactions (either during Link, by specifying it in `/link/token/create`; or after Link, by calling `/transactions/get`). After the [`HISTORICAL_UPDATE`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#historical_update) webhook has fired, call `/transactions/recurring/get` to receive the Recurring Transactions streams and subscribe to the [`RECURRING_TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#recurring_transactions_update) webhook.

After the initial call, you can call `/transactions/recurring/get` endpoint at any point in the future to retrieve the latest summary of recurring streams. Listen to the [`RECURRING_TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#recurring_transactions_update) webhook to be notified when new updates are available.

<a href="/api/products/transactions/#transactionsrecurringget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "account_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "client_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "include_personal_finance_category": false
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

|» account_ids|body|[string]|true|A list of `account_ids` to retrieve for the Item<br><br>Note: An error will be returned if a provided `account_id` is not associated with the Item.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» options|body|[TransactionsRecurringGetRequestOptions](#schematransactionsrecurringgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to be used with the request. If specified, `options` must not be `null`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Refresh transaction data

<a id="opIdtransactionsRefresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transactions/refresh \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /transactions/refresh`

`/transactions/refresh` is an optional endpoint for users of the Transactions product. It initiates an on-demand extraction to fetch the newest transactions for an Item. This on-demand extraction takes place in addition to the periodic extractions that automatically occur multiple times a day for any Transactions-enabled Item. If changes to transactions are discovered after calling `/transactions/refresh`, Plaid will fire a webhook: for `/transactions/sync` users, [`SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#sync_updates_available) will be fired if there are any transactions updated, added, or removed. For users of both `/transactions/sync` and `/transactions/get`, [`TRANSACTIONS_REMOVED`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#transactions_removed) will be fired if any removed transactions are detected, and [`DEFAULT_UPDATE`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#default_update) will be fired if any new transactions are detected. New transactions can be fetched by calling `/transactions/get` or `/transactions/sync`. Note that the `/transactions/refresh` endpoint is not supported for Capital One (`ins_128026`) and will result in a `PRODUCT_NOT_SUPPORTED` error if called on an Item from that institution. 

`/transactions/refresh` is offered as an add-on to Transactions and has a separate [fee model](/docs/account/billing/#per-request-flat-fee). To request access to this endpoint, submit a [product access request](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/products) or contact your Plaid account manager.

<a href="/api/products/transactions/#transactionsrefresh">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

```json
  "request_id": "1vwmF5TBQwiqfwP"
}
```

```bash
curl https://example.com/transactions/sync \
```
