```bash
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "count": 100,
    "cursor": "string",
    "options": {
      "include_logo_and_counterparty_beta": false,
      "include_original_description": false,
      "include_personal_finance_category": false
    },
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /transactions/sync`

This endpoint replaces `/transactions/get` and its associated webhooks for most common use-cases.

The `/transactions/sync` endpoint allows developers to subscribe to all transactions associated with an Item and get updates synchronously in a stream-like manner, using a cursor to track which updates have already been seen. `/transactions/sync` provides the same functionality as `/transactions/get` and can be used instead of `/transactions/get` to simplify the process of tracking transactions updates.

This endpoint provides user-authorized transaction data for `credit`, `depository`, and some loan-type accounts (only those with account subtype `student`; coverage may be limited). For transaction history from `investments` accounts, use `/investments/transactions/get` instead.

Returned transactions data is grouped into three types of update, indicating whether the transaction was added, removed, or modified since the last call to the API.

In the first call to `/transactions/sync` for an Item, the endpoint will return all historical transactions data associated with that Item up until the time of the API call (as "adds"), which then generates a `next_cursor` for that Item. In subsequent calls, send the `next_cursor` to receive only the changes that have occurred since the previous call.

Due to the potentially large number of transactions associated with an Item, results are paginated. The `has_more` field specifies if additional calls are necessary to fetch all available transaction updates. Call `/transactions/sync` with the new cursor, pulling all updates, until `has_more` is `false`.

When retrieving paginated updates, track both the `next_cursor` from the latest response and the original cursor from the first call in which `has_more` was `true`; if a call to `/transactions/sync` fails when retrieving a paginated update, the entire pagination request loop must be restarted beginning with the cursor for the first page of the update, rather than retrying only the single request that failed.

Whenever new or updated transaction data becomes available, `/transactions/sync` will provide these updates. Plaid typically checks for new data multiple times a day, but these checks may occur less frequently, such as once a day, depending on the institution. An Item's `status.transactions.last_successful_update` field will show the timestamp of the most recent successful update. To force Plaid to check for new transactions, use the `/transactions/refresh` endpoint.

Note that for newly created Items, data may not be immediately available to `/transactions/sync`. Plaid begins preparing transactions data when the Item is created, but the process can take anywhere from a few seconds to several minutes to complete, depending on the number of transactions available.

To be alerted when new data is available, listen for the [`SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#sync_updates_available) webhook.

<a href="/api/products/transactions/#transactionssync">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "count": 100,
  "cursor": "string",
  "options": {
    "include_logo_and_counterparty_beta": false,
    "include_original_description": false,
    "include_personal_finance_category": false
  },
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-incremental-transaction-updates-on-an-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransactionsSyncRequest](#schematransactionssyncrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item data is being requested for.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» count|body|integer|false|The number of transaction updates to fetch.|
|» cursor|body|string|false|The cursor value represents the last update requested. Providing it will cause the response to only return changes after this update.<br>If omitted, the entire history of updates will be returned, starting with the first-added transactions on the item.<br>Note: The upper-bound length of this cursor is 256 characters of base64.|
|» options|body|[TransactionsSyncRequestOptions](#schematransactionssyncrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to be used with the request. If specified, `options` must not be `null`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

`POST /transfer/authorization/create`

Use the `/transfer/authorization/create` endpoint to determine transfer failure risk.

In Plaid's Sandbox environment the decisions will be returned as follows:

  - To approve a transfer with null rationale code, make an authorization request with an `amount` less than the available balance in the account.

  - To approve a transfer with the rationale code `MANUALLY_VERIFIED_ITEM`, create an Item in Link through the [Same Day Micro-deposits flow](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/testing/#testing-same-day-micro-deposits).

  - To approve a transfer with the rationale code `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED`, [reset the login for an Item](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/#item_login_required).

  - To decline a transfer with the rationale code `NSF`, the available balance on the account must be less than the authorization `amount`. See [Create Sandbox test data](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/user-custom/) for details on how to customize data in Sandbox.

  - To decline a transfer with the rationale code `RISK`, the available balance on the account must be exactly $0. See [Create Sandbox test data](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/user-custom/) for details on how to customize data in Sandbox.

`device.ip_address`, `device.user_agent` are required fields.

For [Guarantee](https://www.plaid.com/docs//transfer/guarantee/), the following fields are required : `idempotency_key`, `user.phone_number` (optional if `email_address` provided), `user.email_address` (optional if `phone_number` provided), `device.ip_address`, `device.user_agent`, and `user_present`.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/#transferauthorizationcreate">External documentation</a>

```json
  },

  "network": "ach",

  "originator_client_id": "string",
  "payment_profile_token": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "type": "debit",
  "user": {

      "country": "string",

      "region": "string",
      "street": "string"
    },
    "email_address": "string",
    "legal_name": "string",
    "phone_number": "string"
  },
  "user_present": true,
  "with_guarantee": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-transfer-authorization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferAuthorizationCreateRequest](#schematransferauthorizationcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[TransferAccessToken](#schematransferaccesstoken)|false|The Plaid `access_token` for the account that will be debited or credited. Required if not using `payment_profile_token`.|
|» account_id|body|[TransferAccountID](#schematransferaccountid)|false|The Plaid `account_id` corresponding to the end-user account that will be debited or credited. Returned only if `account_id` was set on intent creation.|
|» ach_class|body|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|» amount|body|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|» beacon_session_id|body|string \| null|false|The unique identifier returned by Plaid's [beacon](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/guarantee/#using-a-beacon) when it is run on your webpage. Required for Guarantee customers who are not using [Transfer UI](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/using-transfer-ui/) and have a web checkout experience.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» device|body|[TransferAuthorizationDevice](#schematransferauthorizationdevice)|false|Information about the device being used to initiate the authorization.|
|» funding_account_id|body|[TransferFundingAccountIDRequest](#schematransferfundingaccountidrequest)|false|The id of the funding account to use, available in the Plaid Dashboard. This determines which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited. Defaults to the account configured during onboarding.|
|» idempotency_key|body|[TransferAuthorizationIdempotencyKey](#schematransferauthorizationidempotencykey)|false|A random key provided by the client, per unique authorization. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create an authorization fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single authorization is created.<br><br>Failure to provide this key may result in duplicate charges.<br><br>Required for guaranteed ACH customers.|
|» iso_currency_code|body|string|false|The currency of the transfer amount. The default value is "USD".|
|» network|body|[TransferNetwork](#schematransfernetwork)|true|The network or rails used for the transfer.<br><br>For transfers submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for same-day is 9:30 AM Pacific Time and the cutoff for next-day transfers is 5:30 PM Pacific Time. It is recommended to submit a transfer at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. Note that both legs of the transfer will be downgraded if applicable.|
|» origination_account_id|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Plaid's unique identifier for the origination account for this authorization. If not specified, the default account will be used.|
|» originator_client_id|body|string \| null|false|The Plaid client ID that is the originator of this transfer. Only needed if creating transfers on behalf of another client as a third-party sender (TPS).|
|» payment_profile_token|body|[TransferPaymentProfileToken](#schematransferpaymentprofiletoken)|false|The payment profile token associated with the Payment Profile that will be debited or credited. Required if not using `access_token`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» type|body|[TransferType](#schematransfertype)|true|The type of transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|
|» user|body|[TransferAuthorizationUserInRequest](#schematransferauthorizationuserinrequest)|true|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|
|» user_present|body|boolean \| null|false|Required for Guarantee. If the end user is initiating the specific transfer themselves via an interactive UI, this should be `true`; for automatic recurring payments where the end user is not actually initiating each individual transfer, it should be `false`.|
|» with_guarantee|body|boolean \| null|false|If set to `false`, Plaid will not offer a `guarantee_decision` for this request(Guarantee customers only).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» ach_class|ccd|
|» ach_class|ppd|
|» ach_class|tel|
|» ach_class|web|
|» network|ach|
|» network|same-day-ach|
|» network|rtp|
|» type|debit|
|» type|credit|

<h3 id="create-a-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferCreateRequest](#schematransfercreaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[TransferAccessToken](#schematransferaccesstoken)|false|The Plaid `access_token` for the account that will be debited or credited. Required if not using `payment_profile_token`.|
|» account_id|body|[TransferAccountID](#schematransferaccountid)|false|The Plaid `account_id` corresponding to the end-user account that will be debited or credited. Returned only if `account_id` was set on intent creation.|
|» ach_class|body|object|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» amount|body|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|false|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|» authorization_id|body|string|true|Plaid’s unique identifier for a transfer authorization. This parameter also serves the purpose of acting as an idempotency identifier.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» description|body|string|true|The transfer description. Maximum of 10 characters.|
|» idempotency_key|body|[TransferCreateIdempotencyKey](#schematransfercreateidempotencykey)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. `authorization_id` is now used as idempotency instead.<br><br>A random key provided by the client, per unique transfer. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a transfer fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single transfer is created.|
|» iso_currency_code|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** The currency of the transfer amount. The default value is "USD".|
|» metadata|body|[TransferMetadata](#schematransfermetadata)|false|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|» network|body|object|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Plaid’s unique identifier for the origination account for this transfer. If you have more than one origination account, this value must be specified. Otherwise, this field should be left blank.|
|» payment_profile_token|body|[TransferPaymentProfileToken](#schematransferpaymentprofiletoken)|false|The payment profile token associated with the Payment Profile that will be debited or credited. Required if not using `access_token`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» type|body|object|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» user|body|[TransferUserInRequestDeprecated](#schematransferuserinrequestdeprecated)|false|**Deprecated.** The legal name and other information for the account holder.|

## List transfer events

<a id="opIdtransferEventList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/event/list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "account_id": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "count": 25,
    "end_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "event_types": [
      "pending"
    ],
    "funding_account_id": "string",
    "offset": 0,
    "origination_account_id": "string",
    "originator_client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "start_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "sweep_id": "string",
    "transfer_id": "string",
    "transfer_type": "debit"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/event/list`

Use the `/transfer/event/list` endpoint to get a list of transfer events based on specified filter criteria.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/#transfereventlist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_id": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "count": 25,
  "end_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "event_types": [
    "pending"
  ],
  "funding_account_id": "string",
  "offset": 0,
  "origination_account_id": "string",
  "originator_client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "start_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "sweep_id": "string",
  "transfer_id": "string",
  "transfer_type": "debit"
}
```

<h3 id="list-transfer-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferEventListRequest](#schematransfereventlistrequest)|true|none|
|» account_id|body|string \| null|false|The account ID to get events for all transactions to/from an account.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of transfer events to return. If the number of events matching the above parameters is greater than `count`, the most recent events will be returned.|
|» end_date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The end datetime of transfers to list. This should be in RFC 3339 format (i.e. `2019-12-06T22:35:49Z`)|
|» event_types|body|[[TransferEventType](#schematransfereventtype)]|false|Filter events by event type.|
|» funding_account_id|body|string \| null|false|Filter transfer events to only those with the specified `funding_account_id`.|
|» offset|body|integer \| null|false|The offset into the list of transfer events. When `count`=25 and `offset`=0, the first 25 events will be returned. When `count`=25 and `offset`=25, the next 25 events will be returned.|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The origination account ID to get events for transfers from a specific origination account.|
|» originator_client_id|body|string \| null|false|Filter transfer events to only those with the specified originator client.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» start_date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The start datetime of transfers to list. This should be in RFC 3339 format (i.e. `2019-12-06T22:35:49Z`)|
|» sweep_id|body|string|false|Plaid’s unique identifier for a sweep.|
|» transfer_id|body|string \| null|false|Plaid’s unique identifier for a transfer.|
|» transfer_type|body|[TransferEventListTransferType](#schematransfereventlisttransfertype)|false|The type of transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into your origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of your origination account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» event_types|pending|
|» event_types|cancelled|
|» event_types|failed|
|» event_types|posted|
|» event_types|settled|
|» event_types|returned|
|» event_types|swept|
|» event_types|swept_settled|
|» event_types|return_swept|
|» transfer_type|debit|
|» transfer_type|credit|
|» transfer_type|null|

## Sync transfer events

<a id="opIdtransferEventSync"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/event/sync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "after_id": 0,
    "client_id": "string",
    "count": 25,
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/event/sync`

`/transfer/event/sync` allows you to request up to the next 25 transfer events that happened after a specific `event_id`. Use the `/transfer/event/sync` endpoint to guarantee you have seen all transfer events. When using Auth with micro-deposit verification enabled, this endpoint can be used to fetch status updates on ACH micro-deposits. For more details, see [micro-deposit events](https://www.plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/microdeposit-events/).

<a href="/api/products/transfer/#transfereventsync">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "after_id": 0,
  "client_id": "string",
  "count": 25,
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="sync-transfer-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferEventSyncRequest](#schematransfereventsyncrequest)|true|none|
|» after_id|body|integer|true|The latest (largest) `event_id` fetched via the sync endpoint, or 0 initially.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of transfer events to return.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

|» account_id|body|string \| null|false|The Plaid `account_id` corresponding to the end-user account that will be debited or credited.|
|» ach_class|body|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|» amount|body|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» description|body|string|true|A description for the underlying transfer. Maximum of 8 characters.|
|» funding_account_id|body|[TransferFundingAccountIDRequest](#schematransferfundingaccountidrequest)|false|The id of the funding account to use, available in the Plaid Dashboard. This determines which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited. Defaults to the account configured during onboarding.|
|» iso_currency_code|body|string|false|The currency of the transfer amount, e.g. "USD"|
|» metadata|body|[TransferMetadata](#schematransfermetadata)|false|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|» mode|body|[TransferIntentCreateMode](#schematransferintentcreatemode)|true|The direction of the flow of transfer funds.<br><br>`PAYMENT`: Transfers funds from an end user's account to your business account.<br><br>`DISBURSEMENT`: Transfers funds from your business account to an end user's account.|
|» network|body|[TransferIntentCreateNetwork](#schematransferintentcreatenetwork)|false|The network or rails used for the transfer. Defaults to `same-day-ach`.<br><br>For transfers submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for same-day is 9:30 AM Pacific Time and the cutoff for next-day transfers is 5:30 PM Pacific Time. It is recommended to submit a transfer at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. Note that both legs of the transfer will be downgraded if applicable.|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Plaid’s unique identifier for the origination account for the intent. If not provided, the default account will be used.|
|» require_guarantee|body|boolean \| null|false|When `true`, the transfer requires a `GUARANTEED` decision by Plaid to proceed (Guarantee customers only).|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user|body|[TransferUserInRequest](#schematransferuserinrequest)|true|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» ach_class|ccd|
|» ach_class|ppd|
|» ach_class|tel|
|» ach_class|web|
|» mode|PAYMENT|
|» mode|DISBURSEMENT|
|» network|ach|
|» network|same-day-ach|

## List transfers

<a id="opIdtransferList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "count": 25,
    "end_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "funding_account_id": "string",
    "offset": 0,
    "origination_account_id": "string",
    "originator_client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "start_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/list`

Use the `/transfer/list` endpoint to see a list of all your transfers and their statuses. Results are paginated; use the `count` and `offset` query parameters to retrieve the desired transfers.


<a href="/api/products/transfer/#transferlist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "count": 25,
  "end_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "funding_account_id": "string",
  "offset": 0,
  "origination_account_id": "string",
  "originator_client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "start_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="list-transfers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferListRequest](#schematransferlistrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» count|body|integer|false|The maximum number of transfers to return.|
|» end_date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The end datetime of transfers to list. This should be in RFC 3339 format (i.e. `2019-12-06T22:35:49Z`)|
|» funding_account_id|body|string \| null|false|Filter transfers to only those with the specified `funding_account_id`.|
|» offset|body|integer|false|The number of transfers to skip before returning results.|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Filter transfers to only those originated through the specified origination account.|
|» originator_client_id|body|string \| null|false|Filter transfers to only those with the specified originator client.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» start_date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The start datetime of transfers to list. This should be in RFC 3339 format (i.e. `2019-12-06T22:35:49Z`)|

## Migrate account into Transfers

<a id="opIdtransferMigrateAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/migrate_account \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "account_number": "string",
    "account_type": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "routing_number": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "wire_routing_number": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/migrate_account`

As an alternative to adding Items via Link, you can also use the `/transfer/migrate_account` endpoint to migrate known account and routing numbers to Plaid Items.  Note that Items created in this way are not compatible with endpoints for other products, such as `/accounts/balance/get`, and can only be used with Transfer endpoints.  If you require access to other endpoints, create the Item through Link instead.  Access to `/transfer/migrate_account` is not enabled by default; to obtain access, contact your Plaid Account Manager.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/#transfermigrate_account">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_number": "string",
  "account_type": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "routing_number": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "wire_routing_number": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="migrate-account-into-transfers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferMigrateAccountRequest](#schematransfermigrateaccountrequest)|true|none|
|» account_number|body|string|true|The user's account number.|
|» account_type|body|string|true|The type of the bank account (`checking` or `savings`).|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» routing_number|body|string|true|The user's routing number.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» wire_routing_number|body|string|false|The user's wire transfer routing number. This is the ABA number; for some institutions, this may differ from the ACH number used in `routing_number`.|

## Create a recurring transfer

<a id="opIdtransferRecurringCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/recurring/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "string",
    "account_id": "string",
    "ach_class": "ccd",
    "amount": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "device": {
      "ip_address": "string",
      "user_agent": "string"
    },
    "funding_account_id": "string",
    "idempotency_key": "string",
    "iso_currency_code": "string",
    "network": "ach",
    "schedule": {
      "end_date": "1970-01-01",
      "interval_count": 0,
      "interval_execution_day": 0,
      "interval_unit": "week",
      "start_date": "1970-01-01"
    },
    "secret": "string",
    "test_clock_id": "string",
    "type": "debit",
    "user": {
      "address": {
        "city": "string",
        "country": "string",
        "postal_code": "string",
        "region": "string",
        "street": "string"
      },
      "email_address": "string",
      "legal_name": "string",
      "phone_number": "string"
    },
    "user_present": true
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/recurring/create`

Use the `/transfer/recurring/create` endpoint to initiate a new recurring transfer.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/#transferrecurringcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "account_id": "string",
  "ach_class": "ccd",
  "amount": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "device": {
    "ip_address": "string",
    "user_agent": "string"
  },
  "funding_account_id": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "network": "ach",
  "schedule": {
    "end_date": "1970-01-01",
    "interval_count": 0,
    "interval_execution_day": 0,
    "interval_unit": "week",
    "start_date": "1970-01-01"
  },
  "secret": "string",
  "test_clock_id": "string",
  "type": "debit",
  "user": {
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "street": "string"
    },
    "email_address": "string",
    "legal_name": "string",
    "phone_number": "string"
  },
  "user_present": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-recurring-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferRecurringCreateRequest](#schematransferrecurringcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[TransferAccessToken](#schematransferaccesstoken)|true|The Plaid `access_token` for the account that will be debited or credited. Required if not using `payment_profile_token`.|
|» account_id|body|[TransferAccountID](#schematransferaccountid)|true|The Plaid `account_id` corresponding to the end-user account that will be debited or credited. Returned only if `account_id` was set on intent creation.|
|» ach_class|body|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|» amount|body|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» description|body|string|true|The description of the recurring transfer.|
|» device|body|[TransferDevice](#schematransferdevice)|true|Information about the device being used to initiate the authorization.|
|» funding_account_id|body|[TransferFundingAccountIDRequest](#schematransferfundingaccountidrequest)|false|The id of the funding account to use, available in the Plaid Dashboard. This determines which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited. Defaults to the account configured during onboarding.|
|» idempotency_key|body|[TransferRecurringIdempotencyKey](#schematransferrecurringidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique recurring transfer. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a recurring fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single recurring transfer is created.|
|» iso_currency_code|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** The currency of the transfer amount. The default value is "USD".|
|» network|body|[TransferNetwork](#schematransfernetwork)|true|The network or rails used for the transfer.<br><br>For transfers submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for same-day is 9:30 AM Pacific Time and the cutoff for next-day transfers is 5:30 PM Pacific Time. It is recommended to submit a transfer at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. Note that both legs of the transfer will be downgraded if applicable.|
|» schedule|body|[TransferRecurringSchedule](#schematransferrecurringschedule)|true|The schedule that the recurring transfer will be executed on.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» test_clock_id|body|string \| null|false|Plaid’s unique identifier for a test clock.|
|» type|body|[TransferType](#schematransfertype)|true|The type of transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|
|» user|body|[TransferUserInRequest](#schematransferuserinrequest)|true|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|
|» user_present|body|boolean \| null|true|If the end user is initiating the specific transfer themselves via an interactive UI, this should be `true`; for automatic recurring payments where the end user is not actually initiating each individual transfer, it should be `false`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» ach_class|ccd|
|» ach_class|ppd|
|» ach_class|tel|
|» ach_class|web|
|» network|ach|
|» network|same-day-ach|
|» network|rtp|
|» type|debit|
|» type|credit|

```json
  "decision": "approved",
```

`POST /transfer/recurring/list`

Use the `/transfer/recurring/list` endpoint to see a list of all your recurring transfers and their statuses. Results are paginated; use the `count` and `offset` query parameters to retrieve the desired recurring transfers.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "count": 25,
  "end_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "funding_account_id": "string",
```

<h3 id="list-recurring-transfers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferRecurringListRequest](#schematransferrecurringlistrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» count|body|integer|false|The maximum number of recurring transfers to return.|
|» end_time|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The end datetime of recurring transfers to list. This should be in RFC 3339 format (i.e. `2019-12-06T22:35:49Z`)|

|» start_time|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The start datetime of recurring transfers to list. This should be in RFC 3339 format (i.e. `2019-12-06T22:35:49Z`)|

## Create a refund

<a id="opIdtransferRefundCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/refund/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "idempotency_key": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "transfer_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/refund/create`

Use the `/transfer/refund/create` endpoint to create a refund for a transfer. A transfer can be refunded if the transfer was initiated in the past 180 days.

Processing of the refund will not occur until at least 3 business days following the transfer's settlement date, plus any hold/settlement delays. This 3-day window helps better protect your business from regular ACH returns. Consumer initiated returns (unauthorized returns) could still happen for about 60 days from the settlement date. If the original transfer is canceled, returned or failed, all pending refunds will automatically be canceled. Processed refunds cannot be revoked.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/#transferrefundcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "transfer_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-refund-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferRefundCreateRequest](#schematransferrefundcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» amount|body|[TransferRefundAmount](#schematransferrefundamount)|true|The amount of the refund (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» idempotency_key|body|[TransferRefundIdempotencyKey](#schematransferrefundidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique refund. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a refund fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single refund is created.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» transfer_id|body|[TransferIDForRefund](#schematransferidforrefund)|true|The ID of the transfer to refund.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "refund": {
    "amount": "12.34",
    "created": "2020-08-06T17:27:15Z",
    "id": "667af684-9ee1-4f5f-862a-633ec4c545cc",
    "status": "pending",
    "transfer_id": "460cbe92-2dcc-8eae-5ad6-b37d0ec90fd9"
  },
  "request_id": "saKrIBuEB9qJZno"
}
```

```json
  "status": 0,

}
```

## Create user

<a id="opIduserCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_user_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /user/create`

This endpoint should be called for each of your end users before they begin a Plaid income flow. This provides you a single token to access all income data associated with the user. You should only create one per end user.

If you call the endpoint multiple times with the same `client_user_id`, the first creation call will succeed and the rest will fail with an error message indicating that the user has been created for the given `client_user_id`.

Ensure that you store the `user_token` along with your user's identifier in your database, as it is not possible to retrieve a previously created `user_token`.

<a href="/api/products/income/#usercreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_user_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UserCreateRequest](#schemausercreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_user_id|body|string|true|A unique ID representing the end user. Maximum of 128 characters. Typically this will be a user ID number from your application. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "Aim3b",
  "user_id": "wz666MBjYWTp2PDzzggYhM6oWWmBb",
  "user_token": "user-sandbox-b0e2c4ee-a763-4df5-bfe9-46a46bce993d"
}
```

<h3 id="create-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[UserCreateResponse](#schemausercreateresponse)|

## Execute a transaction using an e-wallet

<a id="opIdwalletTransactionExecute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/wallet/transaction/execute \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": {
      "iso_currency_code": "GBP",
      "value": 1
    },
    "client_id": "string",
    "counterparty": {
      "name": "string",
      "numbers": {
        "bacs": {
          "account": "string",
          "sort_code": "string"
        },
        "international": {
          "iban": "stringstringstr"
        }
      }
    },
    "idempotency_key": "string",
    "reference": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "wallet_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /wallet/transaction/execute`

Execute a transaction using the specified e-wallet.
Specify the e-wallet to debit from, the counterparty to credit to, the idempotency key to prevent duplicate transactions, the amount and reference for the transaction.
Transactions will settle in seconds to several days, depending on the underlying payment rail.

<a href="/api/products/virtual-accounts/#wallettransactionexecute">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": {
    "iso_currency_code": "GBP",
    "value": 1
  },
  "client_id": "string",
  "counterparty": {
    "name": "string",
    "numbers": {
      "bacs": {
        "account": "string",
        "sort_code": "string"
      },
      "international": {
        "iban": "stringstringstr"
      }
    }
  },
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "reference": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "wallet_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="execute-a-transaction-using-an-e-wallet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WalletTransactionExecuteRequest](#schemawallettransactionexecuterequest)|true|none|
|» amount|body|[WalletTransactionAmount](#schemawallettransactionamount)|true|The amount and currency of a transaction|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» counterparty|body|[WalletTransactionCounterparty](#schemawallettransactioncounterparty)|true|An object representing the e-wallet transaction's counterparty|
|» idempotency_key|body|[WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey](#schemawallettransactionidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique wallet transaction. Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a wallet transaction fails due to a network connection error, then after a minimum delay of one minute, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single wallet transaction is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any transaction that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 24 hours of the first request, from being processed.|
|» reference|body|string|true|A reference for the transaction. This must be an alphanumeric string with 6 to 18 characters and must not contain any special characters or spaces.<br>Ensure that the `reference` field is unique for each transaction.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» wallet_id|body|string|true|The ID of the e-wallet to debit from|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "4zlKapIkTm8p5KM",
  "status": "EXECUTED",
  "transaction_id": "wallet-transaction-id-production-53e58b32-fc1c-46fe-bbd6-e584b27a88"
}
```

<h3 id="execute-a-transaction-using-an-e-wallet-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[WalletTransactionExecuteResponse](#schemawallettransactionexecuteresponse)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

`POST /watchlist_screening/individual/review/create`

Create a review for the individual watchlist screening. Reviews are compliance reports created by users in your organization regarding the relevance of potential hits found by Plaid.

```json
  ],

}
```

<h3 id="create-a-review-for-an-individual-watchlist-screening-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WatchlistScreeningIndividualReviewCreateRequest](#schemawatchlistscreeningindividualreviewcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» comment|body|[ReviewComment](#schemareviewcomment)|false|A comment submitted by a team member as part of reviewing a watchlist screening.|
|» confirmed_hits|body|[[WatchlistScreeningHitID](#schemawatchlistscreeninghitid)]|true|Hits to mark as a true positive after thorough manual review. These hits will never recur or be updated once dismissed. In most cases, confirmed hits indicate that the customer should be rejected.|
|» dismissed_hits|body|[[WatchlistScreeningHitID](#schemawatchlistscreeninghitid)]|true|Hits to mark as a false positive after thorough manual review. These hits will never recur or be updated once dismissed.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» watchlist_screening_id|body|[WatchlistScreeningIndividualID](#schemawatchlistscreeningindividualid)|true|ID of the associated screening.|

`POST /watchlist_screening/individual/update`

Update a specific individual watchlist screening. This endpoint can be used to add additional customer information, correct outdated information, add a reference id, assign the individual to a reviewer, and update which program it is associated with. Please note that you may not update `search_terms` and `status` at the same time since editing `search_terms` may trigger an automatic `status` change.

```bash
    "client_id": "string",
    "key_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /webhook_verification_key/get`

Plaid signs all outgoing webhooks and provides JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) so that you can verify the authenticity of any incoming webhooks to your application. A message signature is included in the `Plaid-Verification` header.

The `/webhook_verification_key/get` endpoint provides a JSON Web Key (JWK) that can be used to verify a JWT.

<a href="/api/webhooks/webhook-verification/#get-webhook-verification-key">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "key_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-webhook-verification-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WebhookVerificationKeyGetRequest](#schemawebhookverificationkeygetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» key_id|body|string|true|The key ID ( `kid` ) from the JWT header.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key": {
    "alg": "ES256",
    "created_at": 1560466150,
    "crv": "P-256",
    "expired_at": null,
    "kid": "bfbd5111-8e33-4643-8ced-b2e642a72f3c",
    "kty": "EC",
    "use": "sig",
    "x": "hKXLGIjWvCBv-cP5euCTxl8g9GLG9zHo_3pO5NN1DwQ",
    "y": "shhexqPB7YffGn6fR6h2UhTSuCtPmfzQJ6ENVIoO4Ys"
  },
  "request_id": "RZ6Omi1bzzwDaLo"
}
```

<h3 id="get-webhook-verification-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[WebhookVerificationKeyGetResponse](#schemawebhookverificationkeygetresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & plaidVersion & secret
</aside>

<h2 id="tocS_ACHClass">ACHClass</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaachclass"></a>
<a id="schema_ACHClass"></a>
<a id="tocSachclass"></a>
<a id="tocsachclass"></a>

```json
"ccd"
```

Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.

`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts

`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment

`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry

`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet

Returned for Auth Items only.<br><br>`pending_automatic_verification`: The Item is pending automatic verification<br><br>`pending_manual_verification`: The Item is pending manual micro-deposit verification. <h2 id="tocS_AccountBalance">AccountBalance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccountbalance"></a>
<a id="schema_AccountBalance"></a>
<a id="tocSaccountbalance"></a>
<a id="tocsaccountbalance"></a>

```json
{
  "available": 0,
  "current": 0,
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "last_updated_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "limit": 0,
  "unofficial_currency_code": "string"
}
```

A set of fields describing the balance for an account. Balance information may be cached unless the balance object was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|available|number(double) \| null|true|none|The amount of funds available to be withdrawn from the account, as determined by the financial institution.<br><br>For `credit`-type accounts, the `available` balance typically equals the `limit` less the `current` balance, less any pending outflows plus any pending inflows.<br><br>For `depository`-type accounts, the `available` balance typically equals the `current` balance less any pending outflows plus any pending inflows. For `depository`-type accounts, the `available` balance does not include the overdraft limit.<br><br>For `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier), the `available` balance is the total cash available to withdraw as presented by the institution.<br><br>Note that not all institutions calculate the `available`  balance. In the event that `available` balance is unavailable, Plaid will return an `available` balance value of `null`.<br><br>Available balance may be cached and is not guaranteed to be up-to-date in realtime unless the value was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>If `current` is `null` this field is guaranteed not to be `null`.|
|current|number(double) \| null|true|none|The total amount of funds in or owed by the account.<br><br>For `credit`-type accounts, a positive balance indicates the amount owed; a negative amount indicates the lender owing the account holder.<br><br>For `loan`-type accounts, the current balance is the principal remaining on the loan, except in the case of student loan accounts at Sallie Mae (`ins_116944`). For Sallie Mae student loans, the account's balance includes both principal and any outstanding interest.<br><br>For `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier), the current balance is the total value of assets as presented by the institution.<br><br>Note that balance information may be cached unless the value was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`; if the Item is enabled for Transactions, the balance will be at least as recent as the most recent Transaction update. If you require realtime balance information, use the `available` balance as provided by `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>When returned by `/accounts/balance/get`, this field may be `null`. When this happens, `available` is guaranteed not to be `null`.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the balance. Always null if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-null.|
|last_updated_datetime|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`) indicating the last time that the balance for the given account has been updated<br><br>This is currently only provided when the `min_last_updated_datetime` is passed when calling `/accounts/balance/get` for `ins_128026` (Capital One).|
|limit|number(double) \| null|true|none|For `credit`-type accounts, this represents the credit limit.<br><br>For `depository`-type accounts, this represents the pre-arranged overdraft limit, which is common for current (checking) accounts in Europe.<br><br>In North America, this field is typically only available for `credit`-type accounts.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the balance. Always null if `iso_currency_code` is non-null. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|

Identity information about an account

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|Plaid’s unique identifier for the account. This value will not change unless Plaid can't reconcile the account with the data returned by the financial institution. This may occur, for example, when the name of the account changes. If this happens a new `account_id` will be assigned to the account.<br><br>The `account_id` can also change if the `access_token` is deleted and the same credentials that were used to generate that `access_token` are used to generate a new `access_token` on a later date. In that case, the new `account_id` will be different from the old `account_id`.<br><br>If an account with a specific `account_id` disappears instead of changing, the account is likely closed. Closed accounts are not returned by the Plaid API.<br><br>Like all Plaid identifiers, the `account_id` is case sensitive.|
|balances|[AccountBalance](#schemaaccountbalance)|true|none|A set of fields describing the balance for an account. Balance information may be cached unless the balance object was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`.|
|mask|string \| null|true|none|The last 2-4 alphanumeric characters of an account's official account number. Note that the mask may be non-unique between an Item's accounts, and it may also not match the mask that the bank displays to the user.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the account, either assigned by the user or by the financial institution itself|
|official_name|string \| null|true|none|The official name of the account as given by the financial institution|
|persistent_account_id|string|false|none|A unique and persistent identifier for accounts that can be used to trace multiple instances of the same account across different Items for depository accounts. This is currently an opt-in field and only supported for Chase Items.|
|subtype|[AccountSubtype](#schemaaccountsubtype)|true|none|See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|type|[AccountType](#schemaaccounttype)|true|none|`investment:` Investment account. In API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier, this type is called `brokerage` instead.<br><br>`credit:` Credit card<br><br>`depository:` Depository account<br><br>`loan:` Loan account<br><br>`other:` Non-specified account type<br><br>See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|verification_status|string|false|none|The current verification status of an Auth Item initiated through Automated or Manual micro-deposits.  Returned for Auth Items only.<br><br>`pending_automatic_verification`: The Item is pending automatic verification<br><br>`pending_manual_verification`: The Item is pending manual micro-deposit verification. Items remain in this state until the user successfully verifies the two amounts.<br><br>`automatically_verified`: The Item has successfully been automatically verified	<br><br>`manually_verified`: The Item has successfully been manually verified<br><br>`verification_expired`: Plaid was unable to automatically verify the deposit within 7 calendar days and will no longer attempt to validate the Item. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`verification_failed`: The Item failed manual micro-deposit verification because the user exhausted all 3 verification attempts. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.	<br>	|
|owners|[[Owner](#schemaowner)]|true|none|Data returned by the financial institution about the account owner or owners. Only returned by Identity or Assets endpoints. For business accounts, the name reported may be either the name of the individual or the name of the business, depending on the institution. Multiple owners on a single account will be represented in the same `owner` object, not in multiple owner objects within the array. In API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier, the `owners` object is not returned, and instead identity information is returned in the top level `identity` object. For more details, see [Plaid API versioning](https://plaid.com/docs/api/versioning/#version-2019-05-29)|

```json

```

The application requires that accounts be limited to a specific cardinality.
`MULTI_SELECT`: indicates that the user should be allowed to pick multiple accounts.
`SINGLE_SELECT`: indicates that the user should be allowed to pick only a single account.
`ALL`: indicates that the user must share all of their accounts and should not be given the opportunity to de-select

```json
  "secret": "string"
```

AssetReportCreateRequest defines the request schema for `/asset_report/create`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_tokens|[[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)]|true|none|An array of access tokens corresponding to the Items that will be included in the report. The `assets` product must have been initialized for the Items during link; the Assets product cannot be added after initialization.|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|days_requested|integer|true|none|The maximum integer number of days of history to include in the Asset Report. If using Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty, `days_requested` must be at least 61 for new originations or at least 31 for refinancings.<br><br>An Asset Report requested with "Additional History" (that is, with more than 61 days of transaction history) will incur an Additional History fee.|
|options|[AssetReportCreateRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportcreaterequestoptions)|false|none|An optional object to filter `/asset_report/create` results. If provided, must be non-`null`. The optional `user` object is required for the report to be eligible for Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty program.|
|report_type|[FreddieReportType](#schemafreddiereporttype)|false|none|When set to `VERIFICATION_OF_EMPLOYMENT` and the Asset Report is added to an Audit Copy Token, the Asset Report will be retrieved by Freddie Mac in the Verification Of Employment (VOE) version instead of the default Verification Of Assets (VOA) version.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|report_type|VERIFICATION_OF_EMPLOYMENT|

```json
  },
```

An optional object to filter `/asset_report/create` results. If provided, must be non-`null`. The optional `user` object is required for the report to be eligible for Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty program.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|add_ons|[[AssetReportAddOns](#schemaassetreportaddons)]|false|none|Additional information that can be included in the asset report. Possible values: `"investments"`, `"fast_assets"`|
|client_report_id|string \| null|false|none|Client-generated identifier, which can be used by lenders to track loan applications.|
|include_fast_report|boolean \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** true to return balance and identity earlier as a fast report. Defaults to false if omitted.|
|products|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Additional information that can be included in the asset report. Possible values: `"investments"`|
|user|[AssetReportUser](#schemaassetreportuser)|false|none|The user object allows you to provide additional information about the user to be appended to the Asset Report. All fields are optional. The `first_name`, `last_name`, and `ssn` fields are required if you would like the Report to be eligible for Fannie Mae’s Day 1 Certainty™ program.|
|webhook|string \| null|false|none|URL to which Plaid will send Assets webhooks, for example when the requested Asset Report is ready.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|add_ons|investments|
|add_ons|fast_assets|

A transaction on the asset report

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The ID of the account in which this transaction occurred.|
|account_owner|string \| null|false|none|The name of the account owner. This field is not typically populated and only relevant when dealing with sub-accounts.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The settled value of the transaction, denominated in the transactions's currency, as stated in `iso_currency_code` or `unofficial_currency_code`. Positive values when money moves out of the account; negative values when money moves in. For example, debit card purchases are positive; credit card payments, direct deposits, and refunds are negative.|
|category|[string]|false|none|A hierarchical array of the categories to which this transaction belongs. For a full list of categories, see [`/categories/get`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#categoriesget).<br><br>If the `transactions` object was returned by an Assets endpoint such as `/asset_report/get/` or `/asset_report/pdf/get`, this field will only appear in an Asset Report with Insights.|
|category_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the category to which this transaction belongs. For a full list of categories, see [`/categories/get`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#categoriesget).<br><br>If the `transactions` object was returned by an Assets endpoint such as `/asset_report/get/` or `/asset_report/pdf/get`, this field will only appear in an Asset Report with Insights.|
|check_number|string \| null|false|none|The check number of the transaction. This field is only populated for check transactions.|
|date|string(date)|true|none|For pending transactions, the date that the transaction occurred; for posted transactions, the date that the transaction posted. Both dates are returned in an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format ( `YYYY-MM-DD` ).|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the transaction. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-null.|
|location|[Location](#schemalocation)|false|none|A representation of where a transaction took place|
|logo_url|string \| null|false|none|The logo associated with the merchant, if available. Formatted as a 100x100 pixels PNG file path.|
|merchant_name|string \| null|false|none|The merchant name, as enriched by Plaid from the `name` field. This is typically a more human-readable version of the merchant counterparty in the transaction. For some bank transactions (such as checks or account transfers) where there is no meaningful merchant name, this value will be `null`.|
|name|string|false|none|The merchant name or transaction description.<br><br>If the `transactions` object was returned by a Transactions endpoint such as `/transactions/get`, this field will always appear. If the `transactions` object was returned by an Assets endpoint such as `/asset_report/get/` or `/asset_report/pdf/get`, this field will only appear in an Asset Report with Insights.|
|original_description|string \| null|true|none|The string returned by the financial institution to describe the transaction. For transactions returned by `/transactions/get`, this field is in beta and will be omitted unless the client is both enrolled in the closed beta program and has set `options.include_original_description` to `true`.|
|payment_meta|[PaymentMeta](#schemapaymentmeta)|false|none|Transaction information specific to inter-bank transfers. If the transaction was not an inter-bank transfer, all fields will be `null`.<br><br>If the `transactions` object was returned by a Transactions endpoint such as `/transactions/get`, the `payment_meta` key will always appear, but no data elements are guaranteed. If the `transactions` object was returned by an Assets endpoint such as `/asset_report/get/` or `/asset_report/pdf/get`, this field will only appear in an Asset Report with Insights.|
|pending|boolean|true|none|When `true`, identifies the transaction as pending or unsettled. Pending transaction details (name, type, amount, category ID) may change before they are settled.|
|pending_transaction_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of a posted transaction's associated pending transaction, where applicable.|
|transaction_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the transaction. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `transaction_id` is case sensitive.|
|transaction_type|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Please use the `payment_channel` field, `transaction_type` will be deprecated in the future.<br><br>`digital:` transactions that took place online.<br><br>`place:` transactions that were made at a physical location.<br><br>`special:` transactions that relate to banks, e.g. fees or deposits.<br><br>`unresolved:` transactions that do not fit into the other three types.<br>|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the transaction. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `iso_currency_code`s.|
|website|string \| null|false|none|The website associated with the merchant, if available.|
|credit_category|[CreditCategory](#schemacreditcategory)|false|none|Information describing the intent of the transaction. Most relevant for credit use cases, but not limited to such use cases.|
|date_transacted|string \| null|false|none|The date on which the transaction took place, in IS0 8601 format.|

The user object allows you to provide additional information about the user to be appended to the Asset Report. All fields are optional. The `first_name`, `last_name`, and `ssn` fields are required if you would like the Report to be eligible for Fannie Mae’s Day 1 Certainty™ program.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_user_id|string \| null|false|none|An identifier you determine and submit for the user.|
|email|string \| null|false|none|The user's email address.|
|first_name|string \| null|false|none|The user's first name. Required for the Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty™ program.|
|last_name|string \| null|false|none|The user's last name.  Required for the Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty™ program.|
|middle_name|string \| null|false|none|The user's middle name|
|phone_number|string \| null|false|none|The user's phone number, in E.164 format: +{countrycode}{number}. For example: "+14151234567". Phone numbers provided in other formats will be parsed on a best-effort basis.|
|ssn|string \| null|false|none|The user's Social Security Number. Required for the Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty™ program.<br><br>Format: "ddd-dd-dddd"|

An object containing identifying numbers used for making electronic transfers to and from the `accounts`. The identifying number type (ACH, EFT, IBAN, or BACS) used will depend on the country of the account. An account may have more than one number type. If a particular identifying number type is not used by any `accounts` for which data has been requested, the array for that type will be empty.

|eft|[[NumbersEFT](#schemanumberseft)]|true|none|An array of EFT numbers identifying accounts.|
|international|[[NumbersInternational](#schemanumbersinternational)]|true|none|An array of IBAN numbers identifying accounts.|

AuthGetResponse defines the response schema for `/auth/get`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accounts|[[AccountBase](#schemaaccountbase)]|true|none|The `accounts` for which numbers are being retrieved.|
|item|[Item](#schemaitem)|true|none|Metadata about the Item.|
|numbers|[AuthGetNumbers](#schemaauthgetnumbers)|true|none|An object containing identifying numbers used for making electronic transfers to and from the `accounts`. The identifying number type (ACH, EFT, IBAN, or BACS) used will depend on the country of the account. An account may have more than one number type. <h2 id="tocS_BankInitiatedReturnRisk">BankInitiatedReturnRisk</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabankinitiatedreturnrisk"></a>
<a id="schema_BankInitiatedReturnRisk"></a>
<a id="tocSbankinitiatedreturnrisk"></a>
<a id="tocsbankinitiatedreturnrisk"></a>

```json
{
  "risk_tier": 1,
  "score": 1
}
```

The object contains a risk score and a risk tier that evaluate the transaction return risk because an account is overdrawn or because an ineligible account is used. Common return codes in this category include: "R01", "R02", "R03", "R04", "R06", "R08",  "R09", "R13", "R16", "R17", "R20", "R23". These returns have a turnaround time of 2 banking days.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|risk_tier|[BankInitiatedRiskTier](#schemabankinitiatedrisktier)|true|none|In the `bank_initiated_return_risk` object, there are eight risk tiers corresponding to the scores:<br>  1: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 0.0% - 0.5%<br>  2: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 0.5% - 1.5%<br>  3: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 1.5% - 3%<br>  4: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 3% - 5%<br>  5: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 5% - 10%<br>  6: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 10% - 15%<br>  7: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 15% and 50%<br>  8: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate greater than 50%<br>|
|score|[SignalScore](#schemasignalscore)|true|none|A score from 1-99 that indicates the transaction return risk: a higher risk score suggests a higher return likelihood.|

<h2 id="tocS_BankInitiatedRiskTier">BankInitiatedRiskTier</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabankinitiatedrisktier"></a>
<a id="schema_BankInitiatedRiskTier"></a>
<a id="tocSbankinitiatedrisktier"></a>
<a id="tocsbankinitiatedrisktier"></a>

```json
1
```

In the `bank_initiated_return_risk` object, there are eight risk tiers corresponding to the scores:
  1: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 0.0% - 0.5%
  2: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 0.5% - 1.5%
  3: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 1.5% - 3%
  4: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 3% - 5%
  5: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 5% - 10%
  6: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 10% - 15%
  7: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate between 15% and 50%
  8: Predicted bank-initiated return incidence rate greater than 50%

```json
{

  },

    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },

  }
```
