Represents a bank transfer within the Bank Transfers API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The account ID that should be credited/debited for this bank transfer.|
|ach_class|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|true|none|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|amount|[BankTransferAmount](#schemabanktransferamount)|true|none|The amount of the bank transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|cancellable|boolean|true|none|When `true`, you can still cancel this bank transfer.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|The datetime when this bank transfer was created. This will be of the form `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`|
|custom_tag|string \| null|true|none|A string containing the custom tag provided by the client in the create request. Will be null if not provided.|
|description|string|true|none|The description of the transfer.|
|direction|[BankTransferDirection](#schemabanktransferdirection)|true|none|Indicates the direction of the transfer: `outbound` for API-initiated transfers, or `inbound` for payments received by the FBO account.|
|failure_reason|[BankTransferFailure](#schemabanktransferfailure)|true|none|The failure reason if the type of this transfer is `"failed"` or `"reversed"`. Null value otherwise.|
|id|[BankTransferID](#schemabanktransferid)|true|none|Plaid’s unique identifier for a bank transfer.|
|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The currency of the transfer amount, e.g. "USD"|
|metadata|[BankTransferMetadata](#schemabanktransfermetadata)|true|none|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|network|[BankTransferNetwork](#schemabanktransfernetwork)|true|none|The network or rails used for the transfer. Valid options are `ach`, `same-day-ach`, or `wire`.|
|origination_account_id|string|true|none|Plaid’s unique identifier for the origination account that was used for this transfer.|
|status|[BankTransferStatus](#schemabanktransferstatus)|true|none|The status of the transfer.|
|type|[BankTransferType](#schemabanktransfertype)|true|none|The type of bank transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|
|user|[BankTransferUser](#schemabanktransferuser)|true|none|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ach_class|ccd|
|ach_class|ppd|
|ach_class|tel|
|ach_class|web|
|direction|outbound|
|direction|inbound|
|direction|null|
|network|ach|
|network|same-day-ach|
|network|wire|
|status|pending|
|status|posted|
|status|cancelled|
|status|failed|
|status|reversed|
|type|debit|
|type|credit|

|type|[BankTransferType](#schemabanktransfertype)|true|none|The type of bank transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|


The type of event that this bank transfer represents.

`pending`: A new transfer was created; it is in the pending state.

`cancelled`: The transfer was cancelled by the client.

`failed`: The transfer failed, no funds were moved.

`posted`: The transfer has been successfully submitted to the payment network.

`reversed`: A posted transfer was reversed.

<h2 id="tocS_BankTransferIdempotencyKey">BankTransferIdempotencyKey</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabanktransferidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="schema_BankTransferIdempotencyKey"></a>
<a id="tocSbanktransferidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="tocsbanktransferidempotencykey"></a>

```json
"string"
```

A random key provided by the client, per unique bank transfer. Maximum of 50 characters.

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a bank transfer fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single bank transfer is created.

```json
  "environment": "development",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "webhook_type": "string"
}
```

Fired when new ACH events are available. To begin receiving this webhook, you must first register your webhook listener endpoint via the [webhooks page in the Dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/webhooks). The `BANK_TRANSFERS_EVENTS_UPDATE` webhook can be used to track the progress of ACH transfers used in [micro-deposit verification](/docs/auth/coverage/microdeposit-events/). Receiving this webhook indicates you should fetch the new events from `/bank_transfer/event/sync`. Note that [Transfer](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer) customers should use Transfer webhooks instead of using `BANK_TRANSFERS_EVENTS_UPDATE`; see [micro-deposit events documentation](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/microdeposit-events/) for more details.

|webhook_type|string|true|none|`BANK_TRANSFERS`|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

<h2 id="tocS_ConsentPaymentIdempotencyKey">ConsentPaymentIdempotencyKey</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconsentpaymentidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="schema_ConsentPaymentIdempotencyKey"></a>
<a id="tocSconsentpaymentidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="tocsconsentpaymentidempotencykey"></a>

```json
"string"
```

A random key provided by the client, per unique consent payment. Maximum of 128 characters.

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a consent payment fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single payment is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any payment that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 24 hours of the first request, from being processed.

CreditBankEmploymentGetRequest defines the request schema for `/beta/credit/v1/bank_employment/get`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|user_token|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|true|none|The user token associated with the User data is being requested for.|

The warning associated with the data that was unavailable for the Bank Employment Report.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cause|[CreditBankIncomeCause](#schemacreditbankincomecause)|true|none|An error object and associated `item_id` used to identify a specific Item and error when a batch operation operating on multiple Items has encountered an error in one of the Items.|
|warning_code|[CreditBankIncomeWarningCode](#schemacreditbankincomewarningcode)|true|none|The warning code identifies a specific kind of warning.<br>`IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE`: Unable to extract identity for the Item<br>`TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE`: Unable to extract transactions for the Item<br>`ITEM_UNAPPROVED`: User did not grant permission to share data for the Item<br>`REPORT_DELETED`: Report deleted due to customer or consumer request<br>`DATA_UNAVAILABLE`: No relevant data was found for the Item|
|warning_type|[CreditBankEmploymentWarningType](#schemacreditbankemploymentwarningtype)|true|none|The warning type which will always be `BANK_EMPLOYMENT_WARNING`.|

An error object and associated `item_id` used to identify a specific Item and error when a batch operation operating on multiple Items has encountered an error in one of the Items.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|display_message|string|true|none|A user-friendly representation of the error code. null if the error is not related to user action.<br>This may change over time and is not safe for programmatic use.|
|error_code|string|true|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. Error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred.|
|error_message|string|true|none|A developer-friendly representation of the error code. This may change over time and is not safe for programmatic use.|
|error_type|[CreditBankIncomeErrorType](#schemacreditbankincomeerrortype)|true|none|A broad categorization of the error. Safe for programmatic use.|
|item_id|string|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this warning.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|error_type|INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR|
|error_type|INSUFFICIENT_CREDENTIALS|
|error_type|ITEM_LOCKED|
|error_type|USER_SETUP_REQUIRED|
|error_type|COUNTRY_NOT_SUPPORTED|
|error_type|INSTITUTION_DOWN|
|error_type|INSTITUTION_NO_LONGER_SUPPORTED|
|error_type|INSTITUTION_NOT_RESPONDING|
|error_type|INVALID_CREDENTIALS|
|error_type|INVALID_MFA|
|error_type|INVALID_SEND_METHOD|
|error_type|ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED|
|error_type|MFA_NOT_SUPPORTED|
|error_type|NO_ACCOUNTS|
|error_type|ITEM_NOT_SUPPORTED|
|error_type|ACCESS_NOT_GRANTED|

The end user's monthly summary for the income source(s).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|end_date|string(date)|false|none|The end date of the period included in this monthly summary.<br>This date will be the last day of the month, unless the month being covered is a partial month because it is the last month included in the summary and the date range being requested does not end with the last day of the month.<br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The ISO 4217 currency code of the amount or balance.<br>Please use [`total_amounts`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/income/#credit-bank_income-get-response-bank-income-items-bank-income-sources-historical-summary-total-amounts) instead.|
|start_date|string(date)|false|none|The start date of the period covered in this monthly summary.<br>This date will be the first day of the month, unless the month being covered is a partial month because it is the first month included in the summary and the date range being requested does not begin with the first day of the month.<br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|total_amount|number|false|none|**Deprecated.** Total amount of earnings for the income source(s) of the user for the month in the summary.<br>This may return an incorrect value if the summary includes income sources in multiple currencies.<br>Please use [`total_amounts`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/income/#credit-bank_income-get-response-bank-income-items-bank-income-sources-historical-summary-total-amounts) instead.|
|total_amounts|[[CreditAmountWithCurrency](#schemacreditamountwithcurrency)]|false|none|Total amount of earnings for the income source(s) of the user for the month in the summary.<br>This can contain multiple amounts, with each amount denominated in one unique currency.|
|transactions|[[CreditBankIncomeTransaction](#schemacreditbankincometransaction)]|false|none|none|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The unofficial currency code associated with the amount or balance. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-null.<br>Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br>Please use [`total_amounts`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/income/#credit-bank_income-get-response-bank-income-items-bank-income-sources-historical-summary-total-amounts) instead.|

### Properties

|pay_frequency|[CreditBankIncomePayFrequency](#schemacreditbankincomepayfrequency)|false|none|The income pay frequency.|
|start_date|string(date)|false|none|Minimum of all dates within the specific income sources in the user's bank account for days requested by the client.<br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|total_amount|number|false|none|Total amount of earnings in the user’s bank account for the specific income source for days requested by the client.|
|transaction_count|integer|false|none|Number of transactions for the income source within the start and end date.|

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|end_date|string(date)|false|none|The latest date in which all income sources identified by Plaid appear in the user's account.<br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|historical_summary|[[CreditBankIncomeHistoricalSummary](#schemacreditbankincomehistoricalsummary)]|false|none|none|

|income_sources_count|integer|false|none|Number of income sources per end user.|
|income_transactions_count|integer|false|none|Number of income transactions per end user.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The ISO 4217 currency code of the amount or balance.<br>Please use [`total_amounts`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/income/#credit-bank_income-get-response-bank-income-bank-income-summary-total-amounts) instead.|
|start_date|string(date)|false|none|The earliest date within the days requested in which all income sources identified by Plaid appear in a user's account.<br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|total_amount|number|false|none|**Deprecated.** Total amount of earnings across all the income sources in the end user's Items for the days requested by the client.<br>This may return an incorrect value if the summary includes income sources in multiple currencies.<br>Please use [`total_amounts`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/income/#credit-bank_income-get-response-bank-income-bank-income-summary-total-amounts) instead.|
|total_amounts|[[CreditAmountWithCurrency](#schemacreditamountwithcurrency)]|false|none|Total amount of earnings across all the income sources in the end user's Items for the days requested by the client.<br>This can contain multiple amounts, with each amount denominated in one unique currency.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The unofficial currency code associated with the amount or balance. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-null.<br>Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br>Please use [`total_amounts`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/income/#credit-bank_income-get-response-bank-income-bank-income-summary-total-amounts) instead.|

```json
}
```

The transactions data for the end user's income source(s).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|number|false|none|The settled value of the transaction, denominated in the transactions's currency as stated in `iso_currency_code` or `unofficial_currency_code`.<br>Positive values when money moves out of the account; negative values when money moves in.<br>For example, credit card purchases are positive; credit card payment, direct deposits, and refunds are negative.|
|check_number|string \| null|false|none|The check number of the transaction. This field is only populated for check transactions.|
|date|string(date)|false|none|For pending transactions, the date that the transaction occurred; for posted transactions, the date that the transaction posted.<br>Both dates are returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|iso_currency_code|[CreditIsoCurrencyCode](#schemacreditisocurrencycode)|false|none|The ISO 4217 currency code of the amount or balance.|
|name|string|false|none|The merchant name or transaction description.|
|original_description|string \| null|false|none|The string returned by the financial institution to describe the transaction.|
|pending|boolean|false|none|When true, identifies the transaction as pending or unsettled.<br>Pending transaction details (name, type, amount, category ID) may change before they are settled.|

Does not necessarily correspond to a specific document type.<br><br>`PLAID_GENERATED_PAYSTUB_PDF`: Used to indicate that the PDF for the paystub was generated by Plaid.<br><br>`NONE`: Used to indicate that there is no underlying document for the data.<br><br>`UNKNOWN`: Document type could not be determined.|

<h2 id="tocS_CreditDocumentType">CreditDocumentType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreditdocumenttype"></a>
<a id="schema_CreditDocumentType"></a>
<a id="tocScreditdocumenttype"></a>
<a id="tocscreditdocumenttype"></a>

```json
"string"
```

The type of document.

`PAYSTUB`: A paystub.

`BANK_STATEMENT`: A bank statement.

`US_TAX_W2`: A W-2 wage and tax statement provided by a US employer reflecting wages earned by the employee.

`US_MILITARY_ERAS`: An electronic Retirement Account Statement (eRAS) issued by the US military.

`US_MILITARY_LES`: A Leave and Earnings Statement (LES) issued by the US military.

`US_MILITARY_CLES`: A Civilian Leave and Earnings Statment (CLES) issued by the US military.

`GIG`: Used to indicate that the income is related to gig work. Does not necessarily correspond to a specific document type.

`PLAID_GENERATED_PAYSTUB_PDF`: Used to indicate that the PDF for the paystub was generated by Plaid.

`NONE`: Used to indicate that there is no underlying document for the data.

`UNKNOWN`: Document type could not be determined.

CreditFreddieMacReportsGetRequest defines the request schema for `credit/asset_report/freddie_mac/get`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audit_copy_token|string|true|none|A token that can be shared with a third party auditor to allow them to obtain access to the Asset Report. This token should be stored securely.|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

Defines the response body for `/credit/payroll_income/get`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|items|[[PayrollItem](#schemapayrollitem)]|true|none|Array of payroll items.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomerInitiatedReturnRisk">CustomerInitiatedReturnRisk</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomerinitiatedreturnrisk"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomerInitiatedReturnRisk"></a>
<a id="tocScustomerinitiatedreturnrisk"></a>
<a id="tocscustomerinitiatedreturnrisk"></a>

```json
{
  "risk_tier": 1,
  "score": 1
}
```

The object contains a risk score and a risk tier that evaluate the transaction return risk of an unauthorized debit. Common return codes in this category include: "R05", "R07", "R10", "R11", "R29". These returns typically have a return time frame of up to 60 calendar days. During this period, the customer of financial institutions can dispute a transaction as unauthorized.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|risk_tier|[CustomerInitiatedRiskTier](#schemacustomerinitiatedrisktier)|true|none|A tier corresponding to the projected likelihood that the transaction, if initiated, will be subject to a return.<br><br>In the `customer_initiated_return_risk` object, there are five risk tiers corresponding to the scores:<br>  1: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.00% - 0.02%<br>  2: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.02% - 0.05%<br>  3: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.05% - 0.1%<br>  4: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.1% - 0.5%<br>  5: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate greater than 0.5%<br>|
|score|[SignalScore](#schemasignalscore)|true|none|A score from 1-99 that indicates the transaction return risk: a higher risk score suggests a higher return likelihood.|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomerInitiatedRiskTier">CustomerInitiatedRiskTier</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomerinitiatedrisktier"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomerInitiatedRiskTier"></a>
<a id="tocScustomerinitiatedrisktier"></a>
<a id="tocscustomerinitiatedrisktier"></a>

```json
1
```

A tier corresponding to the projected likelihood that the transaction, if initiated, will be subject to a return.

In the `customer_initiated_return_risk` object, there are five risk tiers corresponding to the scores:
  1: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.00% - 0.02%
  2: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.02% - 0.05%
  3: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.05% - 0.1%
  4: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.1% - 0.5%
  5: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate greater than 0.5%

<h2 id="tocS_DefaultUpdateWebhook">DefaultUpdateWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadefaultupdatewebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_DefaultUpdateWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSdefaultupdatewebhook"></a>
<a id="tocsdefaultupdatewebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "environment": "development",
  "error": {
    "causes": [
      null
    ],
    "display_message": "string",
    "documentation_url": "string",
    "error_code": "string",
    "error_message": "string",
    "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "request_id": "string",
    "status": 0,
    "suggested_action": "string"
  },
  "item_id": "string",
  "new_transactions": 0,
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "webhook_type": "string"
}
```

Fired when new transaction data is available for an Item. Plaid will typically check for new transaction data several times a day.

This webhook is intended for use with `/transactions/get`; if you are using the newer `/transactions/sync` endpoint, this webhook will still be fired to maintain backwards compatibility, but it is recommended to listen for and respond to the `SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE` webhook instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|item_id|string|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item the webhook relates to.|

```json
  "employer_id": "string",
  "employer_name": "string",
  "institution_id": "string",
  "institution_name": "string",
  "is_allocated_remainder": true,
  "percent_allocated": 0,
  "request_id": "string",

  "switch_method": "instant",
  "target_account_id": "string",
  "target_item_id": "string"
}
```

DepositSwitchGetResponse defines the response schema for `/deposit_switch/get`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_has_multiple_allocations|boolean \| null|true|none|When `true`, user’s direct deposit goes to multiple banks. When false, user’s direct deposit only goes to the target account. Always `null` if the deposit switch has not been completed.|
|amount_allocated|number(double) \| null|true|none|The dollar amount of direct deposit allocated to the target account. Always `null` if the target account is not allocated an amount or if the deposit switch has not been completed.|
|date_completed|string(date) \| null|true|none|[ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date the deposit switch was completed. Always `null` if the deposit switch has not been completed.<br>|
|date_created|string(date)|true|none|[ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date the deposit switch was created.<br>|
|deposit_switch_id|string|true|none|The ID of the deposit switch.|
|employer_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the employer selected by the user. If the user did not select an employer, the value returned is `null`.|
|employer_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the employer selected by the user. If the user did not select an employer, the value returned is `null`.|
|institution_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the institution selected by the user. If the user did not select an institution, the value returned is `null`.|
|institution_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the institution selected by the user. If the user did not select an institution, the value returned is `null`.|
|is_allocated_remainder|boolean \| null|true|none|When `true`, the target account is allocated the remainder of direct deposit after all other allocations have been deducted. When `false`, user’s direct deposit is allocated as a percent or amount. Always `null` if the deposit switch has not been completed.|
|percent_allocated|number(double) \| null|true|none|The percentage of direct deposit allocated to the target account. Always `null` if the target account is not allocated a percentage or if the deposit switch has not been completed or if `is_allocated_remainder` is true.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|
|state|string|true|none|<br>The state, or status, of the deposit switch.<br><br>- `initialized` – The deposit switch has been initialized with the user entering the information required to submit the deposit switch request.<br><br>- `processing` – The deposit switch request has been submitted and is being processed.<br><br>- `completed` – The user's employer has fulfilled the deposit switch request.<br><br>- `error` – There was an error processing the deposit switch request.|
|switch_method|string \| null|false|none|The method used to make the deposit switch.<br><br>- `instant` – User instantly switched their direct deposit to a new or existing bank account by connecting their payroll or employer account.<br><br>- `mail` – User requested that Plaid contact their employer by mail to make the direct deposit switch.<br><br>- `pdf` – User generated a PDF or email to be sent to their employer with the information necessary to make the deposit switch.'|
|target_account_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the bank account the direct deposit was switched to.|
|target_item_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the Item the direct deposit was switched to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|initialized|
|state|processing|
|state|completed|
|state|error|
|switch_method|instant|
|switch_method|mail|
|switch_method|pdf|
|switch_method|null|

`DOCUMENT_TYPE_BANK_STATEMENT`: A bank statement.

`DOCUMENT_TYPE_US_TAX_W2`: A W-2 wage and tax statement provided by a US employer reflecting wages earned by the employee.

`DOCUMENT_TYPE_US_MILITARY_ERAS`: An electronic Retirement Account Statement (eRAS) issued by the US military.

`DOCUMENT_TYPE_US_MILITARY_LES`: A Leave and Earnings Statement (LES) issued by the US military.

`DOCUMENT_TYPE_US_MILITARY_CLES`: A Civilian Leave and Earnings Statement (CLES) issued by the US military.

`DOCUMENT_TYPE_GIG`: Used to indicate that the income is related to gig work. Does not necessarily correspond to a specific document type.

`DOCUMENT_TYPE_NONE`: Used to indicate that there is no underlying document for the data.

`DOCUMENT_TYPE_PLAID_GENERATED_PAYSTUB_PDF`: Used to indicate that the PDF for the paystub was generated by Plaid.

`UNKNOWN`: Document type could not be determined.

<h2 id="tocS_DocumentAnalysis">DocumentAnalysis</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "authenticity": "match",
  "extracted_data": {
    "date_of_birth": "match",
    "expiration_date": "not_expired",
    "issuing_country": "match",
    "name": "match"
  },
  "image_quality": "high"
}
```

High level descriptions of how the associated document was processed. If a document fails verification, the details in the `analysis` object should help clarify why the document was rejected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authenticity|[DocumentAuthenticityMatchCode](#schemadocumentauthenticitymatchcode)|true|none|High level summary of whether the document in the provided image matches the formatting rules and security checks for the associated jurisdiction.<br><br>For example, most identity documents have formatting rules like the following:<br><br><br>The image of the person's face must have a certain contrast in order to highlight skin tone<br><br><br>The subject in the document's image must remove eye glasses and pose in a certain way<br><br><br>The informational fields (name, date of birth, ID number, etc.) must be colored and aligned according to specific rules<br><br><br>Security features like watermarks and background patterns must be present<br><br>So a `match` status for this field indicates that the document in the provided image seems to conform to the various formatting and security rules associated with the detected document.|
|extracted_data|[PhysicalDocumentExtractedDataAnalysis](#schemaphysicaldocumentextracteddataanalysis)|true|none|Analysis of the data extracted from the submitted document.|
|image_quality|[ImageQuality](#schemaimagequality)|true|none|A high level description of the quality of the image the user submitted.<br><br>For example, an image that is blurry, distorted by glare from a nearby light source, or improperly framed might be marked as low or medium quality. Poor quality images are more likely to fail OCR and/or template conformity checks.<br><br>Note: By default, Plaid will let a user recapture document images twice before failing the entire session if we attribute the failure to low image quality.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|authenticity|match|
|authenticity|partial_match|
|authenticity|no_match|
|authenticity|no_data|
|image_quality|high|
|image_quality|medium|
|image_quality|low|

<h2 id="tocS_DocumentAuthenticityMatchCode">DocumentAuthenticityMatchCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="schema_DocumentAuthenticityMatchCode"></a>
<a id="tocSdocumentauthenticitymatchcode"></a>
<a id="tocsdocumentauthenticitymatchcode"></a>

```json
"match"
```

High level summary of whether the document in the provided image matches the formatting rules and security checks for the associated jurisdiction.

For example, most identity documents have formatting rules like the following:


The image of the person's face must have a certain contrast in order to highlight skin tone


The subject in the document's image must remove eye glasses and pose in a certain way


The informational fields (name, date of birth, ID number, etc.) must be colored and aligned according to specific rules


Security features like watermarks and background patterns must be present

So a `match` status for this field indicates that the document in the provided image seems to conform to the various formatting and security rules associated with the detected document.

An object representing metadata from the end user's uploaded document.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|doc_id|string|false|none|An identifier of the document that is also present in the paystub response.|
|doc_type|[DocType](#schemadoctype)|false|none|The type of document.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_TYPE_PAYSTUB`: A paystub.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_TYPE_BANK_STATEMENT`: A bank statement.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_TYPE_US_TAX_W2`: A W-2 wage and tax statement provided by a US employer reflecting wages earned by the employee.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_TYPE_US_MILITARY_ERAS`: An electronic Retirement Account Statement (eRAS) issued by the US military.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_TYPE_US_MILITARY_LES`: A Leave and Earnings Statement (LES) issued by the US military.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_TYPE_US_MILITARY_CLES`: A Civilian Leave and Earnings Statement (CLES) issued by the US military.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_TYPE_GIG`: Used to indicate that the income is related to gig work. Does not necessarily correspond to a specific document type.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_TYPE_NONE`: Used to indicate that there is no underlying document for the data.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_TYPE_PLAID_GENERATED_PAYSTUB_PDF`: Used to indicate that the PDF for the paystub was generated by Plaid.<br><br>`UNKNOWN`: Document type could not be determined.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the document.|
|status|string \| null|false|none|The processing status of the document.<br><br>`PROCESSING_COMPLETE`: The document was successfully processed.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_ERROR`: The document could not be processed. Possible causes include: The document was an unacceptable document type such as an offer letter or bank statement, the document image was cropped or blurry, or the document was corrupted.<br><br>`UNKNOWN` or `null`: An internal error occured. If this happens repeatedly, contact support or your Plaid account manager.|

For example, if the first set of document images are blurry or obscured by glare, the user will be asked to capture their documents again, resulting in at least two separate entries within `documents`. If the overall `documentary_verification` is `failed`, the user has exhausted their retry attempts.|
|status|string|true|none|The outcome status for the associated Identity Verification attempt's `documentary_verification` step. This field will always have the same value as `steps.documentary_verification`.|

A program that configures the active lists, search parameters, and other behavior for initial and ongoing screening of entities.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audit_trail|[WatchlistScreeningAuditTrail](#schemawatchlistscreeningaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|id|[EntityWatchlistProgramID](#schemaentitywatchlistprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated entity program.|
|is_archived|[ProgramArchived](#schemaprogramarchived)|true|none|Archived programs are read-only and cannot screen new customers nor participate in ongoing monitoring.|
|is_rescanning_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicator specifying whether the program is enabled and will perform daily rescans.|
|lists_enabled|[[EntityWatchlistCode](#schemaentitywatchlistcode)]|true|none|Watchlists enabled for the associated program|
|name|[EntityWatchlistScreeningProgramName](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeningprogramname)|true|none|A name for the entity program to define its purpose. For example, "High Risk Organizations" or "Applicants".|
|name_sensitivity|[ProgramNameSensitivity](#schemaprogramnamesensitivity)|true|none|The valid name matching sensitivity configurations for a screening program. Note that while certain matching techniques may be more prevalent on less strict settings, all matching algorithms are enabled for every sensitivity.<br><br>`coarse` - See more potential matches. This sensitivity will see more broad phonetic matches across alphabets that make missing a potential hit very unlikely. This setting is noisier and will require more manual review.<br><br>`balanced` - A good default for most companies. This sensitivity is balanced to show high quality hits with reduced noise.<br><br>`strict` - Aggressive false positive reduction. This sensitivity will require names to be more similar than `coarse` and `balanced` settings, relying less on phonetics, while still accounting for character transpositions, missing tokens, and other common permutations.<br><br>`exact` - Matches must be nearly exact. This sensitivity will only show hits with exact or nearly exact name matches with only basic correction such as extraneous symbols and capitalization. This setting is generally not recommended unless you have a very specific use case.|

```json
        },
```

```json
          "weak_alias_determination": "none"
        }
      }
    ],
    "phone_numbers": [
      {

          "summary": "match"
        },

        },

      }

  "historical_since": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z",
  "id": "enthit_52xR9LKo77r1Np",
  "inactive_since": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z",
  "list_code": "EU_CON",
  "plaid_uid": "uid_3NggckTimGSJHS",
  "review_status": "pending_review",
  "source_uid": "26192ABC"
}
```

Data from a government watchlist that has been attached to the screening.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|analysis|[EntityScreeningHitAnalysis](#schemaentityscreeninghitanalysis)|false|none|Analysis information describing why a screening hit matched the provided entity information|
|data|[EntityScreeningHitData](#schemaentityscreeninghitdata)|false|none|Information associated with the entity watchlist hit|
|first_active|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|historical_since|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|id|[EntityWatchlistScreeningHitID](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeninghitid)|true|none|ID of the associated entity screening hit.|
|inactive_since|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|list_code|[EntityWatchlistCode](#schemaentitywatchlistcode)|true|none|Shorthand identifier for a specific screening list for entities.|
|plaid_uid|[InternalUID](#schemainternaluid)|true|none|A universal identifier for a watchlist individual that is stable across searches and updates.|
|review_status|[WatchlistScreeningHitStatus](#schemawatchlistscreeninghitstatus)|true|none|The current state of review. All watchlist screening hits begin in a `pending_review` state but can be changed by creating a review. When a hit is in the `pending_review` state, it will always show the latest version of the watchlist data Plaid has available and be compared against the latest customer information saved in the watchlist screening. Once a hit has been marked as `confirmed` or `dismissed` it will no longer be updated so that the state is as it was when the review was first conducted.|
|source_uid|[SourceUID](#schemasourceuid)|true|none|The identifier provided by the source sanction or watchlist. When one is not provided by the source, this is `null`.|

<h2 id="tocS_ExternalPaymentScheduleBase">ExternalPaymentScheduleBase</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaexternalpaymentschedulebase"></a>
<a id="schema_ExternalPaymentScheduleBase"></a>
<a id="tocSexternalpaymentschedulebase"></a>
<a id="tocsexternalpaymentschedulebase"></a>

```json
{
  "adjusted_start_date": "1970-01-01",
  "end_date": "1970-01-01",
  "interval": "WEEKLY",
  "interval_execution_day": 0,
  "start_date": "1970-01-01"
}
```

The schedule that the payment will be executed on. If a schedule is provided, the payment is automatically set up as a standing order. If no schedule is specified, the payment will be executed only once.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|adjusted_start_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The start date sent to the bank after adjusting for holidays or weekends.  Will be provided in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD). If the start date did not require adjustment, this field will be `null`.|
|end_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|A date in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD). Standing order payments will end on the last `interval_execution_day` on or before the `end_date`.<br>If the only `interval_execution_day` between the start date and the end date (inclusive) is also the same day that `/payment_initiation/payment/create` was called, the bank *may* make a payment on that day, but it is not guaranteed to do so.|
|interval|[PaymentScheduleInterval](#schemapaymentscheduleinterval)|false|none|The frequency interval of the payment.|
|interval_execution_day|integer|false|none|The day of the interval on which to schedule the payment.<br><br>If the payment interval is weekly, `interval_execution_day` should be an integer from 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday).<br><br>If the payment interval is monthly, `interval_execution_day` should be an integer indicating which day of the month to make the payment on. Integers from 1 to 28 can be used to make a payment on that day of the month. Negative integers from -1 to -5 can be used to make a payment relative to the end of the month. To make a payment on the last day of the month, use -1; to make the payment on the second-to-last day, use -2, and so on.|
|start_date|string(date)|false|none|A date in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD). Standing order payments will begin on the first `interval_execution_day` on or after the `start_date`.<br><br>If the first `interval_execution_day` on or after the start date is also the same day that `/payment_initiation/payment/create` was called, the bank *may* make the first payment on that day, but it is not guaranteed to do so.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|interval|WEEKLY|
|interval|MONTHLY|

Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `iso_currency_code`s.|

<h2 id="tocS_HistoricalUpdateWebhook">HistoricalUpdateWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahistoricalupdatewebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_HistoricalUpdateWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocShistoricalupdatewebhook"></a>
<a id="tocshistoricalupdatewebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "environment": "development",
  "error": {
    "causes": [
      null
    ],
    "display_message": "string",
    "documentation_url": "string",
    "error_code": "string",
    "error_message": "string",
    "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "request_id": "string",
    "status": 0,
    "suggested_action": "string"
  },
  "item_id": "string",
  "new_transactions": 0,
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "webhook_type": "string"
}
```

Fired when an Item's historical transaction pull is completed and Plaid has prepared as much historical transaction data as possible for the Item. Once this webhook has been fired, transaction data beyond the most recent 30 days can be fetched for the Item. If [Account Select v2](https://plaid.com/docs/link/customization/#account-select) is enabled, this webhook will also be fired if account selections for the Item are updated, with `new_transactions` set to the number of net new transactions pulled after the account selection update.

This webhook is intended for use with `/transactions/get`; if you are using the newer `/transactions/sync` endpoint, this webhook will still be fired to maintain backwards compatibility, but it is recommended to listen for and respond to the `SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE` webhook instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|new_transactions|number|true|none|The number of new, unfetched transactions available|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`HISTORICAL_UPDATE`|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`TRANSACTIONS`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|development|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

```json
}
```

A securities holding at an institution.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The Plaid `account_id` associated with the holding.|
|cost_basis|number(double) \| null|true|none|The original total value of the holding. This field is calculated by Plaid as the sum of the purchase price of all of the shares in the holding.|
|institution_price|number(double)|true|none|The last price given by the institution for this security.|
|institution_price_as_of|string(date) \| null|false|none|The date at which `institution_price` was current.|
|institution_price_datetime|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Date and time at which `institution_price` was current, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).<br><br>This field is returned for select financial institutions and comes as provided by the institution. It may contain default time values (such as 00:00:00).<br>|
|institution_value|number(double)|true|none|The value of the holding, as reported by the institution.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the holding. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|quantity|number(double)|true|none|The total quantity of the asset held, as reported by the financial institution. If the security is an option, `quantity` will reflect the total number of options (typically the number of contracts multiplied by 100), not the number of contracts.|
|security_id|string|true|none|The Plaid `security_id` associated with the holding. Security data is not specific to a user's account; any user who held the same security at the same financial institution at the same time would have identical security data. The `security_id` for the same security will typically be the same across different institutions, but this is not guaranteed. The `security_id` does not typically change, but may change if inherent details of the security change due to a corporate action, for example, in the event of a ticker symbol change or CUSIP change.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the holding. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `iso_currency_code`s.<br>|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|new_holdings|number|true|none|The number of new holdings reported since the last time this webhook was fired.|
|updated_holdings|number|true|none|The number of updated holdings reported since the last time this webhook was fired.|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`DEFAULT_UPDATE`|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`HOLDINGS`|

An optional flag specifying how you would like Plaid to handle attempts to create an Identity Verification when an Identity Verification already exists for the provided `client_user_id` and `template_id`.
If idempotency is enabled, Plaid will return the existing Identity Verification. If idempotency is disabled, Plaid will reject the request with a `400 Bad Request` status code if an Identity Verification already exists for the supplied `client_user_id` and `template_id`.

A identity verification attempt represents a customer's attempt to verify their identity, reflecting the required steps for completing the session, the results for each step, and information collected in the process.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|An identifier to help you connect this object to your internal systems. For example, your database ID corresponding to this object.|
|completed_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|documentary_verification|[DocumentaryVerification](#schemadocumentaryverification)|true|none|Data, images, analysis, and results from the `documentary_verification` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.documentary_verification` has reached a terminal state of either `success` or `failed`.|
|id|[IdentityVerificationID](#schemaidentityverificationid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification attempt.|
|kyc_check|[KYCCheckDetails](#schemakyccheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `kyc_check` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.kyc_check` has reached a terminal state of either `success` or `failed`.|
|previous_attempt_id|[PreviousIdentityVerificationAttemptID](#schemapreviousidentityverificationattemptid)|true|none|The ID for the Identity Verification preceding this session. This field will only be filled if the current Identity Verification is a retry of a previous attempt.|
|redacted_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|shareable_url|[ShareableURL](#schemashareableurl)|true|none|A shareable URL that can be sent directly to the user to complete verification|
|status|[IdentityVerificationStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstatus)|true|none|The status of this Identity Verification attempt.<br><br><br>`active` - The Identity Verification attempt is incomplete. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed or passed.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed, passing all steps defined to the associated Identity Verification template<br><br>`failed` - The user failed one or more steps in the session and was told to contact support.<br><br>`expired` - The Identity Verification attempt was active for a long period of time without being completed and was automatically marked as expired. Note that sessions currently do not expire. Automatic expiration is expected to be enabled in the future.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled, either via the dashboard by a user, or via API. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed or passed.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.|
|steps|[IdentityVerificationStepSummary](#schemaidentityverificationstepsummary)|true|none|Each step will be one of the following values:<br><br><br>`active` - This step is the user's current step. They are either in the process of completing this step, or they recently closed their Identity Verification attempt while in the middle of this step. Only one step will be marked as `active` at any given point.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed this step.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed this step. This can either call the user to fail the session as a whole, or cause them to fallback to another step depending on how the Identity Verification template is configured. A failed step does not imply a failed session.<br><br>`waiting_for_prerequisite` - The user needs to complete another step first, before they progress to this step. This step may never run, depending on if the user fails an earlier step or if the step is only run as a fallback.<br><br>`not_applicable` - This step will not be run for this session.<br><br>`skipped` - The retry instructions that created this Identity Verification attempt specified that this step should be skipped.<br><br>`expired` - This step had not yet been completed when the Identity Verification attempt as a whole expired.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled before the user completed this step.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.<br><br>`manually_approved` - The step was manually overridden to pass by a team member in the dashboard.<br><br>`manually_rejected` - The step was manually overridden to fail by a team member in the dashboard.|
|template|[IdentityVerificationTemplateReference](#schemaidentityverificationtemplatereference)|true|none|The resource ID and version number of the template configuring the behavior of a given identity verification.|
|user|[IdentityVerificationUserData](#schemaidentityverificationuserdata)|true|none|The identity data that was either collected from the user or provided via API in order to perform an identity verification.|
|watchlist_screening_id|[WatchlistScreeningIndividualIDNullable](#schemawatchlistscreeningindividualidnullable)|true|none|ID of the associated screening.|

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityVerificationConsent">IdentityVerificationConsent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaidentityverificationconsent"></a>
<a id="schema_IdentityVerificationConsent"></a>
<a id="tocSidentityverificationconsent"></a>
<a id="tocsidentityverificationconsent"></a>

```json
true
```

A flag specifying whether the end user has already agreed to a privacy policy specifying that their data will be shared with Plaid for verification purposes.

If `gave_consent` is set to `true`, the `accept_tos` step will be marked as `skipped` and the end user's session will start at the next step requirement.

Request schema for '/identity_verification/create'

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|gave_consent|[IdentityVerificationConsent](#schemaidentityverificationconsent)|true|none|A flag specifying whether the end user has already agreed to a privacy policy specifying that their data will be shared with Plaid for verification purposes.<br><br>If `gave_consent` is set to `true`, the `accept_tos` step will be marked as `skipped` and the end user's session will start at the next step requirement.|
|is_idempotent|[IdempotencyFlag](#schemaidempotencyflag)|false|none|An optional flag specifying how you would like Plaid to handle attempts to create an Identity Verification when an Identity Verification already exists for the provided `client_user_id` and `template_id`.<br>If idempotency is enabled, Plaid will return the existing Identity Verification. If idempotency is disabled, Plaid will reject the request with a `400 Bad Request` status code if an Identity Verification already exists for the supplied `client_user_id` and `template_id`.|
|is_shareable|boolean|true|none|A flag specifying whether you would like Plaid to expose a shareable URL for the verification being created.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|template_id|[IdentityVerificationTemplateID](#schemaidentityverificationtemplateid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification template.|
|user|[IdentityVerificationRequestUser](#schemaidentityverificationrequestuser)|true|none|User information collected outside of Link, most likely via your own onboarding process.<br><br>Each of the following identity fields are optional:<br><br>`email_address`<br><br>`phone_number`<br><br>`date_of_birth`<br><br>`name`<br><br>`address`<br><br>`id_number`<br><br>Specifically, these fields are optional in that they can either be fully provided (satisfying every required field in their subschema) or omitted from the request entirely by not providing the key or value.<br>Providing these fields via the API will result in Link skipping the data collection process for the associated user. All verification steps enabled in the associated Identity Verification Template will still be run. Verification steps will either be run immediately, or once the user completes the `accept_tos` step, depending on the value provided to the `gave_consent` field.|

User information collected outside of Link, most likely via your own onboarding process.

Each of the following identity fields are optional:

`email_address`

`phone_number`

`date_of_birth`

`name`

`address`

`id_number`

Specifically, these fields are optional in that they can either be fully provided (satisfying every required field in their subschema) or omitted from the request entirely by not providing the key or value.
Providing these fields via the API will result in Link skipping the data collection process for the associated user. All verification steps enabled in the associated Identity Verification Template will still be run. Verification steps will either be run immediately, or once the user completes the `accept_tos` step, depending on the value provided to the `gave_consent` field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|[UserAddress](#schemauseraddress)|false|none|Home address for the user.|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|An identifier to help you connect this object to your internal systems. For example, your database ID corresponding to this object.|
|date_of_birth|[ISO8601Date](#schemaiso8601date)|false|none|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD (RFC 3339 Section 5.6).|
|email_address|[EmailAddress](#schemaemailaddress)|false|none|A valid email address.|
|id_number|[UserIDNumber](#schemauseridnumber)|false|none|ID number submitted by the user, currently used only for the Identity Verification product. If the user has not submitted this data yet, this field will be `null`. Otherwise, both fields are guaranteed to be filled.|
|name|[UserName](#schemausername)|false|none|The full name provided by the user. If the user has not submitted their name, this field will be null. Otherwise, both fields are guaranteed to be filled.|
|phone_number|[IdentityVerificationUserPhoneNumber](#schemaidentityverificationuserphonenumber)|false|none|A phone number in E.164 format.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

For example, if your Plaid Template has `verify_sms` disabled, a custom retry with `verify_sms` enabled will still require the step.<br><br>The `selfie_check` step is currently not supported on the sandbox server. Sandbox requests will silently disable the `selfie_check` step when provided.|
|strategy|[Strategy](#schemastrategy)|true|none|An instruction specifying what steps the new Identity Verification attempt should require the user to complete:<br><br><br>`reset` - Restart the user at the beginning of the session, regardless of whether they successfully completed part of their previous session.<br><br>`incomplete` - Start the new session at the step that the user failed in the previous session, skipping steps that have already been successfully completed.<br><br>`infer` - If the most recent Identity Verification attempt associated with the given `client_user_id` has a status of `failed` or `expired`, retry using the `incomplete` strategy. Otherwise, use the `reset` strategy.<br><br>`custom` - Start the new session with a custom configuration, specified by the value of the `steps` field<br><br>Note:<br><br>The `incomplete` strategy cannot be applied if the session's failing step is `screening` or `risk_check`.<br><br>The `infer` strategy cannot be applied if the session's status is still `active`|
|template_id|[IdentityVerificationTemplateID](#schemaidentityverificationtemplateid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification template.|

Instructions for the `custom` retry strategy specifying which steps should be required or skipped.


Note:


This field must be provided when the retry strategy is `custom` and must be omitted otherwise.

Custom retries override settings in your Plaid Template. For example, if your Plaid Template has `verify_sms` disabled, a custom retry with `verify_sms` enabled will still require the step.

The `selfie_check` step is currently not supported on the sandbox server. Sandbox requests will silently disable the `selfie_check` step when provided.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|documentary_verification|boolean|true|none|A boolean field specifying whether the new session should require or skip the `documentary_verification` step.|
|kyc_check|boolean|true|none|A boolean field specifying whether the new session should require or skip the `kyc_check` step.|
|selfie_check|boolean|true|none|A boolean field specifying whether the new session should require or skip the `selfie_check` step.|
|verify_sms|boolean|true|none|A boolean field specifying whether the new session should require or skip the `verify_sms` step.|

A identity verification attempt represents a customer's attempt to verify their identity, reflecting the required steps for completing the session, the results for each step, and information collected in the process.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|An identifier to help you connect this object to your internal systems. For example, your database ID corresponding to this object.|
|completed_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|documentary_verification|[DocumentaryVerification](#schemadocumentaryverification)|true|none|Data, images, analysis, and results from the `documentary_verification` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.documentary_verification` has reached a terminal state of either `success` or `failed`.|
|id|[IdentityVerificationID](#schemaidentityverificationid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification attempt.|
|kyc_check|[KYCCheckDetails](#schemakyccheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `kyc_check` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.kyc_check` has reached a terminal state of either `success` or `failed`.|
|previous_attempt_id|[PreviousIdentityVerificationAttemptID](#schemapreviousidentityverificationattemptid)|true|none|The ID for the Identity Verification preceding this session. This field will only be filled if the current Identity Verification is a retry of a previous attempt.|
|redacted_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|
|shareable_url|[ShareableURL](#schemashareableurl)|true|none|A shareable URL that can be sent directly to the user to complete verification|
|status|[IdentityVerificationStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstatus)|true|none|The status of this Identity Verification attempt.<br><br><br>`active` - The Identity Verification attempt is incomplete. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed or passed.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed, passing all steps defined to the associated Identity Verification template<br><br>`failed` - The user failed one or more steps in the session and was told to contact support.<br><br>`expired` - The Identity Verification attempt was active for a long period of time without being completed and was automatically marked as expired. Note that sessions currently do not expire. Automatic expiration is expected to be enabled in the future.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled, either via the dashboard by a user, or via API. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed or passed.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.|
|steps|[IdentityVerificationStepSummary](#schemaidentityverificationstepsummary)|true|none|Each step will be one of the following values:<br><br><br>`active` - This step is the user's current step. They are either in the process of completing this step, or they recently closed their Identity Verification attempt while in the middle of this step. Only one step will be marked as `active` at any given point.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed this step.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed this step. This can either call the user to fail the session as a whole, or cause them to fallback to another step depending on how the Identity Verification template is configured. A failed step does not imply a failed session.<br><br>`waiting_for_prerequisite` - The user needs to complete another step first, before they progress to this step. This step may never run, depending on if the user fails an earlier step or if the step is only run as a fallback.<br><br>`not_applicable` - This step will not be run for this session.<br><br>`skipped` - The retry instructions that created this Identity Verification attempt specified that this step should be skipped.<br><br>`expired` - This step had not yet been completed when the Identity Verification attempt as a whole expired.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled before the user completed this step.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.<br><br>`manually_approved` - The step was manually overridden to pass by a team member in the dashboard.<br><br>`manually_rejected` - The step was manually overridden to fail by a team member in the dashboard.|
|template|[IdentityVerificationTemplateReference](#schemaidentityverificationtemplatereference)|true|none|The resource ID and version number of the template configuring the behavior of a given identity verification.|
|user|[IdentityVerificationUserData](#schemaidentityverificationuserdata)|true|none|The identity data that was either collected from the user or provided via API in order to perform an identity verification.|
|watchlist_screening_id|[WatchlistScreeningIndividualIDNullable](#schemawatchlistscreeningindividualidnullable)|true|none|ID of the associated screening.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|success|
|status|failed|
|status|expired|
|status|canceled|
|status|pending_review|

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityVerificationStatus">IdentityVerificationStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaidentityverificationstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_IdentityVerificationStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSidentityverificationstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsidentityverificationstatus"></a>

```json
"success"
```

The status of this Identity Verification attempt.


`active` - The Identity Verification attempt is incomplete. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed or passed.

`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed, passing all steps defined to the associated Identity Verification template

`failed` - The user failed one or more steps in the session and was told to contact support.

`expired` - The Identity Verification attempt was active for a long period of time without being completed and was automatically marked as expired. Note that sessions currently do not expire. Automatic expiration is expected to be enabled in the future.

`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled, either via the dashboard by a user, or via API. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed or passed.

`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityVerificationStepSummary">IdentityVerificationStepSummary</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaidentityverificationstepsummary"></a>
<a id="schema_IdentityVerificationStepSummary"></a>
<a id="tocSidentityverificationstepsummary"></a>
<a id="tocsidentityverificationstepsummary"></a>

```json
{
  "accept_tos": "success",
  "documentary_verification": "success",
  "kyc_check": "success",
  "risk_check": "success",
  "selfie_check": "success",
  "verify_sms": "success",
  "watchlist_screening": "success"
}
```

Each step will be one of the following values:


`active` - This step is the user's current step. They are either in the process of completing this step, or they recently closed their Identity Verification attempt while in the middle of this step. Only one step will be marked as `active` at any given point.

`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed this step.

`failed` - The user failed this step. This can either call the user to fail the session as a whole, or cause them to fallback to another step depending on how the Identity Verification template is configured. A failed step does not imply a failed session.

`waiting_for_prerequisite` - The user needs to complete another step first, before they progress to this step. This step may never run, depending on if the user fails an earlier step or if the step is only run as a fallback.

`not_applicable` - This step will not be run for this session.

`skipped` - The retry instructions that created this Identity Verification attempt specified that this step should be skipped.

`expired` - This step had not yet been completed when the Identity Verification attempt as a whole expired.

`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled before the user completed this step.

`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.

`manually_approved` - The step was manually overridden to pass by a team member in the dashboard.

`manually_rejected` - The step was manually overridden to fail by a team member in the dashboard.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accept_tos|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the identity verification process.|
|documentary_verification|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the identity verification process.|
|kyc_check|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the identity verification process.|
|risk_check|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the identity verification process.|
|selfie_check|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the identity verification process.|
|verify_sms|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the identity verification process.|
|watchlist_screening|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the identity verification process.|

A high level description of the quality of the image the user submitted.

For example, an image that is blurry, distorted by glare from a nearby light source, or improperly framed might be marked as low or medium quality. Poor quality images are more likely to fail OCR and/or template conformity checks.

Note: By default, Plaid will let a user recapture document images twice before failing the entire session if we attribute the failure to low image quality.

<h2 id="tocS_IncomeVerificationPrecheckConfidence">IncomeVerificationPrecheckConfidence</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaincomeverificationprecheckconfidence"></a>
<a id="schema_IncomeVerificationPrecheckConfidence"></a>
<a id="tocSincomeverificationprecheckconfidence"></a>
<a id="tocsincomeverificationprecheckconfidence"></a>

```json
"HIGH"
```

The confidence that Plaid can support the user in the digital income verification flow instead of requiring a manual paystub upload. One of the following:

`"HIGH"`: It is very likely that this user can use the digital income verification flow.

"`LOW`": It is unlikely that this user can use the digital income verification flow.

`"UNKNOWN"`: It was not possible to determine if the user is supportable with the information passed.

<h2 id="tocS_IncomeVerificationStatusWebhook">IncomeVerificationStatusWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "environment": "development",
  "item_id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "verification_status": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "webhook_type": "string"
}
```

Fired when the status of an income verification instance has changed. It will typically take several minutes for this webhook to fire after the end user has uploaded their documents in the Document Income flow.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|
|item_id|string|true|none|The Item ID associated with the verification.|
|user_id|[UserId](#schemauserid)|false|none|The Plaid `user_id` of the User associated with this webhook, warning, or error.|
|verification_status|string|true|none|`VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_COMPLETE`: The income verification status processing has completed. If the user uploaded multiple documents, this webhook will fire when all documents have finished processing. Call the `/income/verification/paystubs/get` endpoint and check the document metadata to see which documents were successfully parsed.<br><br>`VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_FAILED`: A failure occurred when attempting to process the verification documentation.<br><br>`VERIFICATION_STATUS_PENDING_APPROVAL`: (deprecated) The income verification has been sent to the user for review.|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`INCOME_VERIFICATION`|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`"INCOME"`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|development|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

A program that configures the active lists, search parameters, and other behavior for initial and ongoing screening of individuals.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audit_trail|[WatchlistScreeningAuditTrail](#schemawatchlistscreeningaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|id|[WatchlistProgramID](#schemawatchlistprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated program.|
|is_archived|[ProgramArchived](#schemaprogramarchived)|true|none|Archived programs are read-only and cannot screen new customers nor participate in ongoing monitoring.|
|is_rescanning_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicator specifying whether the program is enabled and will perform daily rescans.|
|lists_enabled|[[IndividualWatchlistCode](#schemaindividualwatchlistcode)]|true|none|Watchlists enabled for the associated program|
|name|[IndividualWatchlistScreeningProgramName](#schemaindividualwatchlistscreeningprogramname)|true|none|A name for the program to define its purpose. For example, "High Risk Individuals", "US Cardholders", or "Applicants".|
|name_sensitivity|[ProgramNameSensitivity](#schemaprogramnamesensitivity)|true|none|The valid name matching sensitivity configurations for a screening program. Note that while certain matching techniques may be more prevalent on less strict settings, all matching algorithms are enabled for every sensitivity.<br><br>`coarse` - See more potential matches. This sensitivity will see more broad phonetic matches across alphabets that make missing a potential hit very unlikely. This setting is noisier and will require more manual review.<br><br>`balanced` - A good default for most companies. This sensitivity is balanced to show high quality hits with reduced noise.<br><br>`strict` - Aggressive false positive reduction. This sensitivity will require names to be more similar than `coarse` and `balanced` settings, relying less on phonetics, while still accounting for character transpositions, missing tokens, and other common permutations.<br><br>`exact` - Matches must be nearly exact. This sensitivity will only show hits with exact or nearly exact name matches with only basic correction such as extraneous symbols and capitalization. This setting is generally not recommended unless you have a very specific use case.|
