<h2 id="tocS_InflowModel">InflowModel</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainflowmodel"></a>
<a id="schema_InflowModel"></a>
<a id="tocSinflowmodel"></a>
<a id="tocsinflowmodel"></a>

```json
{
  "income_amount": 0,
  "payment_day_of_month": 0,
  "statement_day_of_month": "string",
  "transaction_name": "string",
  "type": "string"
}
```

The `inflow_model` allows you to model a test account that receives regular income or make regular payments on a loan. Any transactions generated by the `inflow_model` will appear in addition to randomly generated test data or transactions specified by `override_accounts`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|income_amount|number(double)|true|none|Amount of income per month. This value is required if `type` is `monthly-income`.|
|payment_day_of_month|number|true|none|Number between 1 and 28, or `last` meaning the last day of the month. The day of the month on which the income transaction will appear. The name of the income transaction. This field is required if `type` is `monthly-income`, `monthly-balance-payment` or `monthly-interest-only-payment`.|
|statement_day_of_month|string|true|none|Number between 1 and 28, or `last` meaning the last day of the month. The day of the month on which the balance is calculated for the next payment. The name of the income transaction. This field is required if `type` is `monthly-balance-payment` or `monthly-interest-only-payment`.|
|transaction_name|string|true|none|The name of the income transaction. This field is required if `type` is `monthly-income`, `monthly-balance-payment` or `monthly-interest-only-payment`.|
|type|string|true|none|Inflow model. One of the following:<br><br>`none`: No income<br><br>`monthly-income`: Income occurs once per month `monthly-balance-payment`: Pays off the balance on a liability account at the given statement day of month.<br><br>`monthly-interest-only-payment`: Makes an interest-only payment on a liability account at the given statement day of month.<br><br>Note that account types supported by Liabilities will accrue interest in the Sandbox. The types impacted are account type `credit` with subtype `credit` or `paypal`, and account type `loan` with subtype `student` or `mortgage`.|

<h2 id="tocS_InitialUpdateWebhook">InitialUpdateWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainitialupdatewebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_InitialUpdateWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSinitialupdatewebhook"></a>
<a id="tocsinitialupdatewebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "environment": "development",
  "error": "string",
  "item_id": "string",
  "new_transactions": 0,
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "webhook_type": "string"
}
```

Fired when an Item's initial transaction pull is completed. Once this webhook has been fired, transaction data for the most recent 30 days can be fetched for the Item. If [Account Select v2](https://plaid.com/docs/link/customization/#account-select) is enabled, this webhook will also be fired if account selections for the Item are updated, with `new_transactions` set to the number of net new transactions pulled after the account selection update.

This webhook is intended for use with `/transactions/get`; if you are using the newer `/transactions/sync` endpoint, this webhook will still be fired to maintain backwards compatibility, but it is recommended to listen for and respond to the `SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE` webhook instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|
|error|string \| null|false|none|The error code associated with the webhook.|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|new_transactions|number|true|none|The number of new, unfetched transactions available.|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`INITIAL_UPDATE`|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`TRANSACTIONS`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|development|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

To identify institutions that support those methods, use the `auth_metadata` object. For more details, see [Full Auth coverage](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/).|

The status of an institution is determined by the health of its Item logins, Transactions updates, Investments updates, Liabilities updates, Auth requests, Balance requests, Identity requests, Investments requests, and Liabilities requests. A login attempt is conducted during the initial Item add in Link. If there is not enough traffic to accurately calculate an institution's status, Plaid will return null rather than potentially inaccurate data.

Institution status is accessible in the Dashboard and via the API using the `/institutions/get_by_id` endpoint with the `include_status` option set to true. Note that institution status is not available in the Sandbox environment.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth|[ProductStatus](#schemaproductstatus)|false|none|A representation of the status health of a request type. Auth requests, Balance requests, Identity requests, Investments requests, Liabilities requests, Transactions updates, Investments updates, Liabilities updates, and Item logins each have their own status object.|
|health_incidents|[[HealthIncident](#schemahealthincident)]|false|none|Details of recent health incidents associated with the institution.|
|identity|[ProductStatus](#schemaproductstatus)|false|none|A representation of the status health of a request type. Auth requests, Balance requests, Identity requests, Investments requests, Liabilities requests, Transactions updates, Investments updates, Liabilities updates, and Item logins each have their own status object.|

Auth requests, Balance requests, Identity requests, Investments requests, Liabilities requests, Transactions updates, Investments updates, Liabilities updates, and Item logins each have their own status object.|
|item_logins|[ProductStatus](#schemaproductstatus)|false|none|A representation of the status health of a request type. Auth requests, Balance requests, Identity requests, Investments requests, Liabilities requests, Transactions updates, Investments updates, Liabilities updates, and Item logins each have their own status object.|

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "country_codes": [
    "US"
  ],
  "options": {
    "include_auth_metadata": false,
    "include_optional_metadata": true,
    "include_payment_initiation_metadata": false,
    "oauth": true,
    "payment_initiation": {
      "consent_id": "string",
      "payment_id": "string"
    }
  },
  "products": [
    "assets"
  ],
  "query": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

InstitutionsSearchRequest defines the request schema for `/institutions/search`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|country_codes|[[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)]|true|none|Specify an array of Plaid-supported country codes this institution supports, using the ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country code standard. In API versions 2019-05-29 and earlier, the `country_codes` parameter is an optional parameter within the `options` object and will default to `[US]` if it is not supplied.<br>|
|options|[InstitutionsSearchRequestOptions](#schemainstitutionssearchrequestoptions)|false|none|An optional object to filter `/institutions/search` results.|
|products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|true|none|Filter the Institutions based on whether they support all products listed in `products`. Provide `null` to get institutions regardless of supported products. Note that when `auth` is specified as a product, if you are enabled for Instant Match or Automated Micro-deposits, institutions that support those products will be returned even if `auth` is not present in their product array.|
|query|string|true|none|The search query. Institutions with names matching the query are returned|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

<h2 id="tocS_InstitutionsSearchRequestOptions">InstitutionsSearchRequestOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainstitutionssearchrequestoptions"></a>
<a id="schema_InstitutionsSearchRequestOptions"></a>
<a id="tocSinstitutionssearchrequestoptions"></a>
<a id="tocsinstitutionssearchrequestoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "include_auth_metadata": false,
  "include_optional_metadata": true,
  "include_payment_initiation_metadata": false,
  "oauth": true,
  "payment_initiation": {
    "consent_id": "string",
    "payment_id": "string"
  }
}
```

An optional object to filter `/institutions/search` results.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_auth_metadata|boolean \| null|false|none|When `true`, returns metadata related to the Auth product indicating which auth methods are supported.|
|include_optional_metadata|boolean|false|none|When true, return the institution's homepage URL, logo and primary brand color.|
|include_payment_initiation_metadata|boolean \| null|false|none|When `true`, returns metadata related to the Payment Initiation product indicating which payment configurations are supported.|
|oauth|boolean \| null|false|none|Limit results to institutions with or without mandatory OAuth login flows. Note that institutions will only have `oauth` set to `true` if *all* Items associated with that institution are required to use OAuth flows; institutions in a state of migration to OAuth may have the `oauth` attribute set to `false` even if they support OAuth.|
|payment_initiation|[InstitutionsSearchPaymentInitiationOptions](#schemainstitutionssearchpaymentinitiationoptions)|false|none|Additional options that will be used to filter institutions by various Payment Initiation configurations.|

<h2 id="tocS_InvestmentTransaction">InvestmentTransaction</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainvestmenttransaction"></a>
<a id="schema_InvestmentTransaction"></a>
<a id="tocSinvestmenttransaction"></a>
<a id="tocsinvestmenttransaction"></a>

```json
{
  "account_id": "string",
  "amount": 0,
  "cancel_transaction_id": "string",
  "date": "1970-01-01",
  "fees": 0,
  "investment_transaction_id": "string",
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "price": 0,
  "quantity": 0,
  "security_id": "string",
  "subtype": "account fee",
  "type": "buy",
  "unofficial_currency_code": "string"
}
```

A transaction within an investment account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The `account_id` of the account against which this transaction posted.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The complete value of the transaction. Positive values when cash is debited, e.g. purchases of stock; negative values when cash is credited, e.g. sales of stock. Treatment remains the same for cash-only movements unassociated with securities.|
|cancel_transaction_id|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** A legacy field formerly used internally by Plaid to identify certain canceled transactions.|
|date|string(date)|true|none|The [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) posting date for the transaction.|
|fees|number(double) \| null|true|none|The combined value of all fees applied to this transaction|
|investment_transaction_id|string|true|none|The ID of the Investment transaction, unique across all Plaid transactions. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `investment_transaction_id` is case sensitive.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the transaction. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|name|string|true|none|The institution’s description of the transaction.|
|price|number(double)|true|none|The price of the security at which this transaction occurred.|
|quantity|number(double)|true|none|The number of units of the security involved in this transaction. Positive for buy transactions; negative for sell transactions.|
|security_id|string \| null|true|none|The `security_id` to which this transaction is related.|
|subtype|[InvestmentTransactionSubtype](#schemainvestmenttransactionsubtype)|true|none|For descriptions of possible transaction types and subtypes, see the [Investment transaction types schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#investment-transaction-types-schema).|
|type|[InvestmentTransactionType](#schemainvestmenttransactiontype)|true|none|Value is one of the following:<br>`buy`: Buying an investment<br>`sell`: Selling an investment<br>`cancel`: A cancellation of a pending transaction<br>`cash`: Activity that modifies a cash position<br>`fee`: A fee on the account<br>`transfer`: Activity which modifies a position, but not through buy/sell activity e.g. options exercise, portfolio transfer<br><br>For descriptions of possible transaction types and subtypes, see the [Investment transaction types schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#investment-transaction-types-schema).|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the holding. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `iso_currency_code`s.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|subtype|account fee|
|subtype|adjustment|
|subtype|assignment|
|subtype|buy|
|subtype|buy to cover|
|subtype|contribution|
|subtype|deposit|
|subtype|distribution|
|subtype|dividend|
|subtype|dividend reinvestment|
|subtype|exercise|
|subtype|expire|
|subtype|fund fee|
|subtype|interest|
|subtype|interest receivable|

<h2 id="tocS_InvestmentTransactionType">InvestmentTransactionType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainvestmenttransactiontype"></a>
<a id="schema_InvestmentTransactionType"></a>
<a id="tocSinvestmenttransactiontype"></a>
<a id="tocsinvestmenttransactiontype"></a>

```json
"buy"
```

Value is one of the following:
`buy`: Buying an investment
`sell`: Selling an investment
`cancel`: A cancellation of a pending transaction
`cash`: Activity that modifies a cash position
`fee`: A fee on the account
`transfer`: Activity which modifies a position, but not through buy/sell activity e.g. options exercise, portfolio transfer

For descriptions of possible transaction types and subtypes, see the [Investment transaction types schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#investment-transaction-types-schema).

|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|new_investments_transactions|number|true|none|The number of new transactions reported since the last time this webhook was fired.|

|webhook_type|string|true|none|`INVESTMENTS_TRANSACTIONS`|

```json
  },
```


Specify the list of investments transactions on the account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|currency|string|true|none|Either a valid `iso_currency_code` or `unofficial_currency_code`|
|date|string(date)|true|none|Posting date for the transaction. Must be formatted as an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date.|
|fees|number(double)|false|none|The combined value of all fees applied to this transaction.|
|name|string|true|none|The institution's description of the transaction.|
|price|number(double)|true|none|The price of the security at which this transaction occurred.|
|quantity|number(double)|true|none|The number of units of the security involved in this transaction. Must be positive if the type is a buy and negative if the type is a sell.|
|security|[SecurityOverride](#schemasecurityoverride)|false|none|Specify the security associated with the holding or investment transaction. When inputting custom security data to the Sandbox, Plaid will perform post-data-retrieval normalization and enrichment. These processes may cause the data returned by the Sandbox to be slightly different from the data you input. An ISO-4217 currency code and a security identifier (`ticker_symbol`, `cusip`, `isin`, or `sedol`) are required.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the investment transaction. Possible values are:<br>`buy`: Buying an investment<br>`sell`: Selling an investment<br>`cash`: Activity that modifies a cash position<br>`fee`: A fee on the account<br>`transfer`: Activity that modifies a position, but not through buy/sell activity e.g. options exercise, portfolio transfer|

Metadata about the Item.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|available_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|true|none|A list of products available for the Item that have not yet been accessed. The contents of this array will be mutually exclusive with `billed_products`.|
|billed_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|true|none|A list of products that have been billed for the Item. The contents of this array will be mutually exclusive with `available_products`. Note - `billed_products` is populated in all environments but only requests in Production are billed. Also note that products that are billed on a pay-per-call basis rather than a pay-per-Item basis, such as `balance`, will not appear here.<br>|
|consent_expiration_time|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|The RFC 3339 timestamp after which the consent provided by the end user will expire. Upon consent expiration, the item will enter the `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` error state. To circumvent the `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` error and maintain continuous consent, the end user can reauthenticate via Link’s update mode in advance of the consent expiration time.<br><br>Note - This is only relevant for certain OAuth-based institutions. For all other institutions, this field will be null.<br>|
|consented_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|Beta: A list of products that have gone through consent collection for the Item. Only present for those enabled in the beta.<br>|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|true|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|institution_id|string \| null|false|none|The Plaid Institution ID associated with the Item. Field is `null` for Items created via Same Day Micro-deposits.|
|item_id|string|true|none|The Plaid Item ID. The `item_id` is always unique; linking the same account at the same institution twice will result in two Items with different `item_id` values. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `item_id` is case-sensitive.|
|products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|A list of authorized products for the Item.<br>|
|update_type|string|true|none|Indicates whether an Item requires user interaction to be updated, which can be the case for Items with some forms of two-factor authentication.<br><br>`background` - Item can be updated in the background<br><br>`user_present_required` - Item requires user interaction to be updated|
|webhook|string \| null|true|none|The URL registered to receive webhooks for the Item.|

<a id="tocsjwkpublickey"></a>

```json
{
  "alg": "string",
  "created_at": 0,
  "crv": "string",
  "expired_at": 0,
  "kid": "string",
  "kty": "string",
  "use": "string",
  "x": "string",
  "y": "string"
}
```

A JSON Web Key (JWK) that can be used in conjunction with [JWT libraries](https://jwt.io/#libraries-io) to verify Plaid webhooks

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alg|string|true|none|The alg member identifies the cryptographic algorithm family used with the key.|
|created_at|integer|true|none|The timestamp when the key was created, in Unix time.|
|crv|string|true|none|The crv member identifies the cryptographic curve used with the key.|
|expired_at|integer \| null|true|none|The timestamp when the key expired, in Unix time.|
|kid|string|true|none|The kid (Key ID) member can be used to match a specific key. This can be used, for instance, to choose among a set of keys within the JWK during key rollover.|
|kty|string|true|none|The kty (key type) parameter identifies the cryptographic algorithm family used with the key, such as RSA or EC.|
|use|string|true|none|The use (public key use) parameter identifies the intended use of the public key.|
|x|string|true|none|The x member contains the x coordinate for the elliptic curve point, provided as a base64url-encoded string of the coordinate's big endian representation.|
|y|string|true|none|The y member contains the y coordinate for the elliptic curve point, provided as a base64url-encoded string of the coordinate's big endian representation.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|po_box|[POBoxStatus](#schemapoboxstatus)|true|none|Field describing whether the associated address is a post office box. Will be `yes` when a P.O. box is detected, `no` when Plaid confirmed the address is not a P.O. box, and `no_data` when Plaid was not able to determine if the address is a P.O. box.|
|summary|[MatchSummaryCode](#schemamatchsummarycode)|true|none|An enum indicating the match type between data provided by user and data checked against an external data source.<br><br><br>`match` indicates that the provided input data was a strong match against external data.<br><br>`partial_match` indicates the data approximately matched against external data. For example, "Knope" vs. "Knope-Wyatt" for last name.<br><br>`no_match` indicates that Plaid was able to perform a check against an external data source and it did not match the provided input data.<br><br>`no_data` indicates that Plaid was unable to find external data to compare against the provided input data.<br><br>`no_input` indicates that Plaid was unable to perform a check because no information was provided for this field by the end user.|
|type|[AddressPurposeLabel](#schemaaddresspurposelabel)|true|none|Field describing whether the associated address is being used for commercial or residential purposes.<br><br>Note: This value will be `no_data` when Plaid does not have sufficient data to determine the address's use.|

|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|true|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`DEFAULT_UPDATE`|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`LIABILITIES`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|development|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

Used to configure Sandbox test data for the Liabilities product

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|balance_transfer_apr|number(double)|true|none|The balance transfer APR percentage value. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`.|
|cash_apr|number(double)|true|none|The cash APR percentage value. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`.|
|expected_payoff_date|string(date)|true|none|Override the `expected_payoff_date` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|guarantor|string|true|none|Override the `guarantor` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|interest_capitalization_grace_period_months|number|true|none|If set, interest capitalization begins at the given number of months after loan origination. By default interest is never capitalized. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|is_federal|boolean|true|none|Override the `is_federal` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|is_overdue|boolean|true|none|Override the `is_overdue` field|
|last_payment_amount|number(double)|true|none|Override the `last_payment_amount` field. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`.|
|loan_name|string|true|none|Override the `loan_name` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|loan_status|[StudentLoanStatus](#schemastudentloanstatus)|true|none|An object representing the status of the student loan|
|minimum_payment_amount|number(double)|true|none|Override the `minimum_payment_amount` field. Can only be set if `type` is `credit` or `student`.|
|nominal_apr|number(double)|true|none|The interest rate on the loan as a percentage. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|origination_date|string(date)|true|none|The date on which the loan was initially lent, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) (YYYY-MM-DD) format. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|payment_reference_number|string|true|none|Override the `payment_reference_number` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|principal|number(double)|true|none|The original loan principal. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|pslf_status|[PSLFStatus](#schemapslfstatus)|true|none|Information about the student's eligibility in the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program. This is only returned if the institution is FedLoan (`ins_116527`). |
|purchase_apr|number(double)|true|none|The purchase APR percentage value. For simplicity, this is the only interest rate used to calculate interest charges. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`.|
|repayment_model|[StudentLoanRepaymentModel](#schemastudentloanrepaymentmodel)|true|none|Student loan repayment information used to configure Sandbox test data for the Liabilities product|
|repayment_plan_description|string|true|none|Override the `repayment_plan.description` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|repayment_plan_type|string|true|none|Override the `repayment_plan.type` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`. Possible values are: `"extended graduated"`, `"extended standard"`, `"graduated"`, `"income-contingent repayment"`, `"income-based repayment"`, `"interest only"`, `"other"`, `"pay as you earn"`, `"revised pay as you earn"`, or `"standard"`.|
|sequence_number|string|true|none|Override the `sequence_number` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|servicer_address|[Address](#schemaaddress)|true|none|A physical mailing address.|
|special_apr|number(double)|true|none|The special APR percentage value. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the liability object, either `credit` or `student`. Mortgages are not currently supported in the custom Sandbox.|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenAccountFilters">LinkTokenAccountFilters</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinktokenaccountfilters"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkTokenAccountFilters"></a>
<a id="tocSlinktokenaccountfilters"></a>
<a id="tocslinktokenaccountfilters"></a>

```json
{
  "credit": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "credit card"
    ]
  },
  "depository": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "checking"
    ]
  },
  "investment": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "529"
    ]
  },
  "loan": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "auto"
    ]
  }
}
```

By default, Link will provide limited account filtering: it will only display Institutions that are compatible with all products supplied in the `products` parameter of `/link/token/create`, and, if `auth` is specified in the `products` array, will also filter out accounts other than `checking` and `savings` accounts on the Account Select pane. You can further limit the accounts shown in Link by using `account_filters` to specify the account subtypes to be shown in Link. Only the specified subtypes will be shown. This filtering applies to both the Account Select view (if enabled) and the Institution Select view. Institutions that do not support the selected subtypes will be omitted from Link. To indicate that all subtypes should be shown, use the value `"all"`. If the `account_filters` filter is used, any account type for which a filter is not specified will be entirely omitted from Link. For a full list of valid types and subtypes, see the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema).

For institutions using OAuth, the filter will not affect the list of accounts shown by the bank in the OAuth window.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|credit|[CreditFilter](#schemacreditfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `credit`-type accounts|
|depository|[DepositoryFilter](#schemadepositoryfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `depository`-type accounts|
|investment|[InvestmentFilter](#schemainvestmentfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier).|
|loan|[LoanFilter](#schemaloanfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `loan`-type accounts|

This filtering applies to both the Account Select view (if enabled) and the Institution Select view. Institutions that do not support the selected subtypes will be omitted from Link. To indicate that all subtypes should be shown, use the value `"all"`. If the `account_filters` filter is used, any account type for which a filter is not specified will be entirely omitted from Link. For a full list of valid types and subtypes, see the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema).<br><br>For institutions using OAuth, the filter will not affect the list of accounts shown by the bank in the OAuth window.<br>|
|additional_consented_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|(Beta) This field has no effect unless you are participating in the Product Scope Transparency beta program.<br>List of additional Plaid product(s) you wish to collect consent for. These products will not be billed until you start using them by calling the relevant endpoints.<br><br>`balance` is *not* a valid value, the Balance product does not require explicit initialization and will automatically have consent collected.<br><br>Institutions that do not support these products will still be shown in Link|
|android_package_name|string|false|none|The name of your app's Android package. Required if using the `link_token` to initialize Link on Android. When creating a `link_token` for initializing Link on other platforms, this field must be left blank. Any package name specified here must also be added to the Allowed Android package names setting on the [developer dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api). |
|auth|[LinkTokenCreateRequestAuth](#schemalinktokencreaterequestauth)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Auth product. This field can be used to enable or disable extended Auth flows for the resulting Link session. Omitting any field will result in a default that can be configured by your account manager.|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|client_name|string|true|none|The name of your application, as it should be displayed in Link. Maximum length of 30 characters. If a value longer than 30 characters is provided, Link will display "This Application" instead.|
|country_codes|[[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)]|true|none|Specify an array of Plaid-supported country codes using the ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country code standard. Institutions from all listed countries will be shown. For a complete mapping of supported products by country, see https://plaid.com/global/.<br><br>If Link is launched with multiple country codes, only products that you are enabled for in all countries will be used by Link. Note that while all countries are enabled by default in Sandbox and Development, in Production only US and Canada are enabled by default. To gain access to European institutions in the Production environment, [file a product access Support ticket](https://dashboard.plaid.com/support/new/product-and-development/product-troubleshooting/request-product-access) via the Plaid dashboard. If you initialize with a European country code, your users will see the European consent panel during the Link flow.<br><br>If using a Link customization, make sure the country codes in the customization match those specified in `country_codes`. If both `country_codes` and a Link customization are used, the value in `country_codes` may override the value in the customization.<br><br>If using the Auth features Instant Match, Same-day Micro-deposits, or Automated Micro-deposits, `country_codes` must be set to `['US']`.|
|deposit_switch|[LinkTokenCreateRequestDepositSwitch](#schemalinktokencreaterequestdepositswitch)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Deposit Switch (beta) product. This field is required if `deposit_switch` is included in the `products` array.|
|employment|[LinkTokenCreateRequestEmployment](#schemalinktokencreaterequestemployment)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Employment product. This field is required if `employment` is included in the `products` array.|
|eu_config|[LinkTokenEUConfig](#schemalinktokeneuconfig)|false|none|Configuration parameters for EU flows|
|identity_verification|[LinkTokenCreateRequestIdentityVerification](#schemalinktokencreaterequestidentityverification)|false|none|Specifies option for initializing Link for use with the Identity Verification product.|
|income_verification|[LinkTokenCreateRequestIncomeVerification](#schemalinktokencreaterequestincomeverification)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Income product. This field is required if `income_verification` is included in the `products` array.|
|institution_data|[LinkTokenCreateInstitutionData](#schemalinktokencreateinstitutiondata)|false|none|A map containing data used to highlight institutions in Link.|
|institution_id|string|false|none|Used for certain Europe-only configurations, as well as certain legacy use cases in other regions.|
|investments|[LinkTokenInvestments](#schemalinktokeninvestments)|false|none|Configuration parameters for the Investments product|
|language|string|true|none|The language that Link should be displayed in.<br><br>Supported languages are:<br>- Danish (`'da'`)<br>- Dutch (`'nl'`)<br>- English (`'en'`)<br>- Estonian (`'et'`)<br>- French (`'fr'`)<br>- German (`'de'`)<br>- Italian (`'it'`)<br>- Latvian (`'lv'`)<br>- Lithuanian (`'lt'`)<br>- Norwegian (`'no'`)<br>- Polish (`'po'`)<br>- Romanian (`'ro'`)<br>- Spanish (`'es'`)<br>- Swedish (`'se'`)<br><br>When using a Link customization, the language configured here must match the setting in the customization, or the customization will not be applied.|
|link_customization_name|string|false|none|The name of the Link customization from the Plaid Dashboard to be applied to Link. If not specified, the `default` customization will be used. When using a Link customization, the language in the customization must match the language selected via the `language` parameter, and the countries in the customization should match the country codes selected via `country_codes`.|
|payment_initiation|[LinkTokenCreateRequestPaymentInitiation](#schemalinktokencreaterequestpaymentinitiation)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Payment Initiation (Europe) product. This field is required if `payment_initiation` is included in the `products` array. Either `payment_id` or `consent_id` must be provided.|
|products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|List of Plaid product(s) you wish to use. If launching Link in update mode, should be omitted; required otherwise.<br><br>`balance` is *not* a valid value, the Balance product does not require explicit initialization and will automatically be initialized when any other product is initialized.<br><br>The products specified here will determine which institutions will be available to your users in Link. Only institutions that support *all* requested products can be selected; a if a user attempts to select an institution that does not support a listed product, a "Connectivity not supported" error message will appear in Link. To maximize the number of institutions available, initialize Link with the minimal product set required for your use case. Additional products can be added after Link initialization by calling the relevant endpoints. For details and exceptions, see [Choosing when to initialize products](https://plaid.com/docs/link/initializing-products/).<br><br>Note that, unless you have opted to disable Instant Match support, institutions that support Instant Match will also be shown in Link if `auth` is specified as a product, even though these institutions do not contain `auth` in their product array.<br><br>In Production, you will be billed for each product that you specify when initializing Link. Note that a product cannot be removed from an Item once the Item has been initialized with that product. To stop billing on an Item for subscription-based products, such as Liabilities, Investments, and Transactions, remove the Item via `/item/remove`.|
|redirect_uri|string|false|none|A URI indicating the destination where a user should be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or via a webview. The `redirect_uri` should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production or Development, must be an https URI. To specify any subdomain, use `*` as a wildcard character, e.g. `https://*.example.com/oauth.html`. If `android_package_name` is specified, this field should be left blank.  Note that any redirect URI must also be added to the Allowed redirect URIs list in the [developer dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api).|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|transfer|[LinkTokenCreateRequestTransfer](#schemalinktokencreaterequesttransfer)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Transfer product.|
|update|[LinkTokenCreateRequestUpdate](#schemalinktokencreaterequestupdate)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode).|
|user|[LinkTokenCreateRequestUser](#schemalinktokencreaterequestuser)|true|none|An object specifying information about the end user who will be linking their account.|
|user_token|string|false|none|A user token generated using `/user/create`. Any Item created during the Link session will be associated with the user.|
|webhook|string|false|none|The destination URL to which any webhooks should be sent.|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenCreateRequestAccountSubtypes">LinkTokenCreateRequestAccountSubtypes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinktokencreaterequestaccountsubtypes"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkTokenCreateRequestAccountSubtypes"></a>
<a id="tocSlinktokencreaterequestaccountsubtypes"></a>
<a id="tocslinktokencreaterequestaccountsubtypes"></a>

```json
{
  "credit": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "credit card"
    ]
  },
  "depository": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "checking"
    ]
  },
  "investment": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "529"
    ]
  },
  "loan": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "auto"
    ]
  }
}
```

By default, Link will only display account types that are compatible with all products supplied in the `products` parameter of `/link/token/create`. You can further limit the accounts shown in Link by using `account_filters` to specify the account subtypes to be shown in Link. Only the specified subtypes will be shown. This filtering applies to both the Account Select view (if enabled) and the Institution Select view. Institutions that do not support the selected subtypes will be omitted from Link. To indicate that all subtypes should be shown, use the value `"all"`. If the `account_filters` filter is used, any account type for which a filter is not specified will be entirely omitted from Link.

For a full list of valid types and subtypes, see the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema).

For institutions using OAuth, the filter will not affect the list of institutions or accounts shown by the bank in the OAuth window.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|credit|[LinkTokenCreateCreditFilter](#schemalinktokencreatecreditfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `credit`-type accounts|
|depository|[LinkTokenCreateDepositoryFilter](#schemalinktokencreatedepositoryfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `depository`-type accounts|
|investment|[LinkTokenCreateInvestmentFilter](#schemalinktokencreateinvestmentfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier).|
|loan|[LinkTokenCreateLoanFilter](#schemalinktokencreateloanfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `loan`-type accounts|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenCreateRequestAuth">LinkTokenCreateRequestAuth</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinktokencreaterequestauth"></a>

<a id="tocslinktokencreaterequestauth"></a>

```json
{
  "auth_type_select_enabled": false,
  "automated_microdeposits_enabled": true,
  "flow_type": "FLEXIBLE_AUTH",
  "instant_match_enabled": true,
  "same_day_microdeposits_enabled": true
}
```

Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Auth product. This field can be used to enable or disable extended Auth flows for the resulting Link session. Omitting any field will result in a default that can be configured by your account manager.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth_type_select_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether Auth Type Select is enabled for the Link session, allowing the end user to choose between linking instantly or manually prior to selecting their financial institution. Note that this can only be true if `same_day_microdeposits_enabled` is set to true.|
|automated_microdeposits_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the Link session is enabled for the Automated Micro-deposits flow.|
|flow_type|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** This field has been deprecated in favor of `auth_type_select_enabled`.|
|instant_match_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the Link session is enabled for the Instant Match flow. As of November 2022, Instant Match will be enabled by default. Instant Match can be disabled by setting this field to `false`.|
|same_day_microdeposits_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the Link session is enabled for the Same Day Micro-deposits flow.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|flow_type|FLEXIBLE_AUTH|

This field is required if `income_verification` is included in the `products` array and `bank` is specified in `income_source_types`.|

|payroll_income|[LinkTokenCreateRequestIncomeVerificationPayrollIncome](#schemalinktokencreaterequestincomeverificationpayrollincome)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with Payroll Income.|
|precheck_id|string|false|none|The ID of a precheck created with `/income/verification/precheck`. Will be used to improve conversion of the income verification flow by streamlining the Link interface presented to the end user.|
|stated_income_sources|[[LinkTokenCreateRequestUserStatedIncomeSource](#schemalinktokencreaterequestuserstatedincomesource)]|false|none|A list of user stated income sources|

```json
    "family_name": "Knope",
    "given_name": "Leslie"
  },
  "phone_number": "string",
  "phone_number_verified_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "ssn": "string"

```

An object specifying information about the end user who will be linking their account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|[UserAddress](#schemauseraddress)|false|none|Home address for the user.|
|client_user_id|string|true|none|A unique ID representing the end user. Typically this will be a user ID number from your application. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`. It is currently used as a means of searching logs for the given user in the Plaid Dashboard.|
|date_of_birth|string(date) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** To be provided in the format "yyyy-mm-dd". Not currently used.|
|email_address|string|false|none|The user's email address. This field is optional, but required to enable the [pre-authenticated returning user flow](https://plaid.com/docs/link/returning-user/#pre-authenticated-rux).|
|email_address_verified_time|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The date and time the email address was verified in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`). This was previously an optional field used in the [returning user experience](https://plaid.com/docs/link/returning-user). This field is no longer required to enable the returning user experience.<br><br> Only pass a verification time for an email address that you have verified. If you have performed verification but don’t have the time, you may supply a signal value of the start of the UNIX epoch.<br><br> Example: `2020-01-01T00:00:00Z`|
|id_number|[UserIDNumber](#schemauseridnumber)|false|none|ID number submitted by the user, currently used only for the Identity Verification product. If the user has not submitted this data yet, this field will be `null`. Otherwise, both fields are guaranteed to be filled.|
|legal_name|string|false|none|The user's full legal name, used for [micro-deposit based verification flows](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/). For a small number of customers on legacy flows, providing this field is required to enable micro-deposit-based flows. For all other customers, this field is optional, but providing the user's name in this field when using micro-deposit-based verification will enable certain risk checks and can reduce micro-deposit fraud.|
|name|object|false|none|none|
|phone_number|string|false|none|The user's phone number in [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format. This field is optional, but required to enable the [returning user experience](https://plaid.com/docs/link/returning-user).|
|phone_number_verified_time|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The date and time the phone number was verified in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`). This was previously an optional field used in the [returning user experience](https://plaid.com/docs/link/returning-user). This field is no longer required to enable the returning user experience.<br><br> Only pass a verification time for a phone number that you have verified. If you have performed verification but don’t have the time, you may supply a signal value of the start of the UNIX epoch.<br><br> Example: `2020-01-01T00:00:00Z`<br>|
|ssn|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** To be provided in the format "ddd-dd-dddd". Not currently used.|

<h2 id="tocS_MatchSummaryCode">MatchSummaryCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamatchsummarycode"></a>
<a id="schema_MatchSummaryCode"></a>
<a id="tocSmatchsummarycode"></a>
<a id="tocsmatchsummarycode"></a>

```json
"match"
```

An enum indicating the match type between data provided by user and data checked against an external data source.


`match` indicates that the provided input data was a strong match against external data.

`partial_match` indicates the data approximately matched against external data. For example, "Knope" vs. "Knope-Wyatt" for last name.

`no_match` indicates that Plaid was able to perform a check against an external data source and it did not match the provided input data.

`no_data` indicates that Plaid was unable to find external data to compare against the provided input data.

`no_input` indicates that Plaid was unable to perform a check because no information was provided for this field by the end user.

|mask|string|true|none|The account's mask. Should be a string of 2-4 alphanumeric characters. This allows you to model a mask which does not match the account number (such as with a virtual account number).|
|name|string|true|none|The account's name|
|official_name|string|true|none|The account's official name|

<h2 id="tocS_MinLastUpdatedDatetime">MinLastUpdatedDatetime</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaminlastupdateddatetime"></a>
<a id="schema_MinLastUpdatedDatetime"></a>
<a id="tocSminlastupdateddatetime"></a>
<a id="tocsminlastupdateddatetime"></a>

```json
"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
```

Timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`) indicating the oldest acceptable balance when making a request to `/accounts/balance/get`.

If the balance that is pulled for `ins_128026` (Capital One) is older than the given timestamp, an `INVALID_REQUEST` error with the code of `LAST_UPDATED_DATETIME_OUT_OF_RANGE` will be returned with the most recent timestamp for the requested account contained in the response.

This field is only used when the institution is `ins_128026` (Capital One), in which case a value must be provided or an `INVALID_REQUEST` error with the code of `INVALID_FIELD` will be returned. For all other institutions, this field is ignored.

Contains details about a mortgage account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The ID of the account that this liability belongs to.|
|account_number|string|true|none|The account number of the loan.|
|current_late_fee|number(double) \| null|true|none|The current outstanding amount charged for late payment.|
|escrow_balance|number(double) \| null|true|none|Total amount held in escrow to pay taxes and insurance on behalf of the borrower.|
|has_pmi|boolean \| null|true|none|Indicates whether the borrower has private mortgage insurance in effect.|
|has_prepayment_penalty|boolean \| null|true|none|Indicates whether the borrower will pay a penalty for early payoff of mortgage.|
|interest_rate|[MortgageInterestRate](#schemamortgageinterestrate)|true|none|Object containing metadata about the interest rate for the mortgage.|
|last_payment_amount|number(double) \| null|true|none|The amount of the last payment.|
|last_payment_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|The date of the last payment. Dates are returned in an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|loan_term|string \| null|true|none|Full duration of mortgage as at origination (e.g. `10 year`).|
|loan_type_description|string \| null|true|none|Description of the type of loan, for example `conventional`, `fixed`, or `variable`. This field is provided directly from the loan servicer and does not have an enumerated set of possible values.|
|maturity_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|Original date on which mortgage is due in full. Dates are returned in an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|next_monthly_payment|number(double) \| null|true|none|The amount of the next payment.|
|next_payment_due_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|The due date for the next payment. Dates are returned in an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|origination_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|The date on which the loan was initially lent. Dates are returned in an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|origination_principal_amount|number(double) \| null|true|none|The original principal balance of the mortgage.|
|past_due_amount|number(double) \| null|true|none|Amount of loan (principal + interest) past due for payment.|
|property_address|[MortgagePropertyAddress](#schemamortgagepropertyaddress)|true|none|Object containing fields describing property address.|
|ytd_interest_paid|number(double) \| null|true|none|The year to date (YTD) interest paid.|
|ytd_principal_paid|number(double) \| null|true|none|The YTD principal paid.|

<h2 id="tocS_NameMatchScore">NameMatchScore</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanamematchscore"></a>
<a id="schema_NameMatchScore"></a>
<a id="tocSnamematchscore"></a>
<a id="tocsnamematchscore"></a>

```json
{
  "is_business_name_detected": true,
  "is_first_name_or_last_name_match": true,
  "is_nickname_match": true,
  "score": 0
}
```

Score found by matching name provided by the API with the name on the account at the financial institution. If the account contains multiple owners, the maximum match score is filled.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|is_business_name_detected|boolean \| null|false|none|If the name on either of the names that was matched for the score was a business name, with corp, llc, ltd etc in the name. While this being true confirms business name, false means it was either not a business name or Plaid could not detect it as such, since a lot of business names match owner names and are hard to detect.|
|is_first_name_or_last_name_match|boolean \| null|false|none|first or last name completely matched|
|is_nickname_match|boolean \| null|false|none|nickname matched, example Jennifer and Jenn.|
|score|integer \| null|false|none|Represents the match score for name. 100 is a perfect score, 85-99 means a strong match, 50-84 is a partial match, less than 50 is a weak match and 0 is a complete mismatch. If the name is missing from either the API or financial institution, this is empty.|

<h2 id="tocS_NewAccountsAvailableWebhook">NewAccountsAvailableWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanewaccountsavailablewebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_NewAccountsAvailableWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSnewaccountsavailablewebhook"></a>
<a id="tocsnewaccountsavailablewebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "environment": "development",
  "error": {
    "causes": [
      null
    ],
    "display_message": "string",
    "documentation_url": "string",
    "error_code": "string",
    "error_message": "string",
    "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "request_id": "string",
    "status": 0,
    "suggested_action": "string"
  },
  "item_id": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "webhook_type": "string"
}
```

Fired when Plaid detects a new account for Items created or updated with [Account Select v2](https://plaid.com/docs/link/customization/#account-select). Upon receiving this webhook, you can prompt your users to share new accounts with you through [Account Select v2 update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode/#using-update-mode-to-request-new-accounts).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|false|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|false|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|webhook_code|string|false|none|`NEW_ACCOUNTS_AVAILABLE`|
|webhook_type|string|false|none|`ITEM`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|development|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

<h2 id="tocS_NumbersACH">NumbersACH</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanumbersach"></a>
<a id="schema_NumbersACH"></a>
<a id="tocSnumbersach"></a>
<a id="tocsnumbersach"></a>

```json
{
  "account": "string",
  "account_id": "string",
  "can_transfer_in": true,
  "can_transfer_out": true,
  "routing": "string",
  "wire_routing": "string"
}
```

Identifying information for transferring money to or from a US account via ACH or wire transfer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|string|true|none|The ACH account number for the account.<br><br>Note that when using OAuth with Chase Bank (`ins_56`), Chase will issue "tokenized" routing and account numbers, which are not the user's actual account and routing numbers. These tokenized numbers should work identically to normal account and routing numbers. The digits returned in the `mask` field will continue to reflect the actual account number, rather than the tokenized account number; for this reason, when displaying account numbers to the user to help them identify their account in your UI, always use the `mask` rather than truncating the `account` number. If a user revokes their permissions to your app, the tokenized numbers will continue to work for ACH deposits, but not withdrawals.|
|account_id|string|true|none|The Plaid account ID associated with the account numbers|
|can_transfer_in|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the account supports ACH transfers into the account|
|can_transfer_out|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the account supports ACH transfers out of the account|
|routing|string|true|none|The ACH routing number for the account. If the institution is `ins_56`, this may be a tokenized routing number. For more information, see the description of the `account` field.|
|wire_routing|string \| null|true|none|The wire transfer routing number for the account, if available|

Data to use to set values of test accounts. Some values cannot be specified in the schema and will instead will be calculated from other test data in order to achieve more consistent, realistic test data.

### Properties

|force_available_balance|number(double)|true|none|If provided, the account will always have this amount as its  available balance, regardless of current balance or changes in transactions over time.|
|holdings|[HoldingsOverride](#schemaholdingsoverride)|false|none|Specify the holdings on the account.|
|identity|[OwnerOverride](#schemaowneroverride)|true|none|Data about the owner or owners of an account. Any fields not specified will be filled in with default Sandbox information.|
|income|[IncomeOverride](#schemaincomeoverride)|false|none|Specify payroll data on the account.|
|inflow_model|[InflowModel](#schemainflowmodel)|true|none|The `inflow_model` allows you to model a test account that receives regular income or make regular payments on a loan. Any transactions generated by the `inflow_model` will appear in addition to randomly generated test data or transactions specified by `override_accounts`.|
|investment_transactions|[Investments_TransactionsOverride](#schemainvestments_transactionsoverride)|false|none|Specify the list of investments transactions on the account.|
|liability|[LiabilityOverride](#schemaliabilityoverride)|true|none|Used to configure Sandbox test data for the Liabilities product|
|meta|[Meta](#schemameta)|true|none|Allows specifying the metadata of the test account|
|numbers|[Numbers](#schemanumbers)|true|none|Account and bank identifier number data used to configure the test account. All values are optional.|
|starting_balance|number(double)|true|none|If provided, the account will start with this amount as the current balance.<br>|
|subtype|[AccountSubtype](#schemaaccountsubtype)|true|none|See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|transactions|[[TransactionOverride](#schematransactionoverride)]|true|none|Specify the list of transactions on the account.|
|type|[OverrideAccountType](#schemaoverrideaccounttype)|true|none|`investment:` Investment account.<br><br>`credit:` Credit card<br><br>`depository:` Depository account<br><br>`loan:` Loan account<br><br>`payroll:` Payroll account<br><br>`other:` Non-specified account type<br><br>See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|

Request schema for `/partner/customer/create`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|[PartnerEndCustomerAddress](#schemapartnerendcustomeraddress)|true|none|The end customer's address.|
|application_name|string|true|none|The name of the end customer's application. This will be shown to end users when they go through the Plaid Link flow.|
|assets_under_management|[PartnerEndCustomerAssetsUnderManagement](#schemapartnerendcustomerassetsundermanagement)|false|none|Assets under management for the given end customer. Required for end customers with monthly service commitments.|
|billing_contact|[PartnerEndCustomerBillingContact](#schemapartnerendcustomerbillingcontact)|false|none|The billing contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's technical contact if omitted.|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|company_name|string|true|none|The company name of the end customer being created. This will be used to display the end customer in the Plaid Dashboard. It will not be shown to end users.|
|create_link_customization|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the end customer's default Link customization will be set to match the partner's. You can always change the end customer's Link customization in the Plaid Dashboard. See the [Link Customization docs](https://plaid.com/docs/link/customization/) for more information.|
|customer_support_info|[PartnerEndCustomerCustomerSupportInfo](#schemapartnerendcustomercustomersupportinfo)|false|none|This information is public. Users of your app will see this information when managing connections between your app and their bank accounts in Plaid Portal. Defaults to partner's customer support info if omitted.|
|is_bank_addendum_completed|boolean|true|none|Denotes whether the partner has forwarded the Plaid bank addendum to the end customer.|
|is_diligence_attested|boolean|true|none|Denotes whether or not the partner has completed attestation of diligence for the end customer to be created.|
|legal_entity_name|string|true|none|The end customer's legal name. This will be shared with financial institutions as part of the OAuth registration process. It will not be shown to end users.|
|logo|string|false|none|Base64-encoded representation of the end customer's logo. Must be a PNG of size 1024x1024 under 4MB. The logo will be shared with financial institutions and shown to the end user during Link flows. A logo is required if `create_link_customization` is `true`. If `create_link_customization` is `false` and the logo is omitted, a stock logo will be used.|
|products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|true|none|The products to be enabled for the end customer.|
|redirect_uris|[string]|false|none|A list of URIs indicating the destination(s) where a user can be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or via a webview. URIs should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production or Development, URIs must use https. To specify any subdomain, use `*` as a wildcard character, e.g. `https://*.example.com/oauth.html`. To modify redirect URIs for an end customer after creating them, go to the end customer's [API page](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api) in the Dashboard.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|technical_contact|[PartnerEndCustomerTechnicalContact](#schemapartnerendcustomertechnicalcontact)|false|none|The technical contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's technical contact if omitted.|
|website|string|true|none|The end customer's website.|

<h2 id="tocS_PartnerEndCustomerStatus">PartnerEndCustomerStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapartnerendcustomerstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_PartnerEndCustomerStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSpartnerendcustomerstatus"></a>
<a id="tocspartnerendcustomerstatus"></a>

```json
"UNDER_REVIEW"
```

The status of the given end customer.

`UNDER_REVIEW`: The end customer has been created and enabled in the non-Production environments. The end customer must be manually reviewed by the Plaid team before it can be enabled in production, at which point its status will automatically transition to `PENDING_ENABLEMENT` or `DENIED`.

`PENDING_ENABLEMENT`: The end customer is ready to be enabled in the Production environment. Call the `/partner/customer/enable` endpoint to enable the end customer in Production.

`ACTIVE`: The end customer has been enabled in all environments.

`DENIED`: The end customer has been created and enabled in the non-Production environments, but it did not pass review by the Plaid team and therefore cannot be enabled in the Production environment. Talk to your Account Manager for more information.

### Properties

Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a consent payment fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single payment is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any payment that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 24 hours of the first request, from being processed.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

PaymentInitiationConsentPaymentExecuteResponse defines the response schema for `/payment_initiation/consent/payment/execute`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_id|string|true|none|A unique ID identifying the payment|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|
|status|[PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentstatus)|true|none|The status of the payment.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED`: This is the initial state of all payments. It indicates that the payment is waiting on user input to continue processing. A payment may re-enter this state later on if further input is needed.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED`: The payment has been successfully authorised and accepted by the financial institution but has not been executed.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: The payment has failed due to insufficient funds.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: The payment has failed to be initiated. This error is retryable once the root cause is resolved.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: The payment has been blocked. This is a retryable error.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`: The payment is currently being processed. The payment will automatically exit this state when the financial institution has authorised the transaction.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED`: The payment was cancelled during authorisation.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: The payment has been successfully executed and is considered complete.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: The payment has settled and funds are available for use. Payment settlement can only be guaranteed by using Plaid virtual accounts. A payment will typically settle within seconds to several days, depending on which payment rail is used.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established. This state is only used for standing orders.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: The payment was rejected by the financial institution.<br><br>Deprecated:<br>These statuses will be removed in a future release.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: The payment status is unknown.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`: The payment is currently being processed. The payment will automatically exit this state when processing is complete.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established. This state is only used for standing orders.|


Payment consent scope. Defines possible directions for payments made with the given consent.

`ME_TO_ME`: Allows moving money between accounts owned by the same user.

`EXTERNAL`: Allows initiating payments from the user's account to third parties.

The status of the payment consent.

`UNAUTHORISED`: Consent created, but requires user authorisation.

`REJECTED`: Consent authorisation was rejected by the user and/or the bank.

`AUTHORISED`: Consent is active and ready to be used.

`REVOKED`: Consent has been revoked and can no longer be used.

`EXPIRED`: Consent is no longer valid.

This is a retryable error.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`: The payment is currently being processed. This state is only used for standing orders.|

PaymentInitiationPaymentReverseRequest defines the request schema for `/payment_initiation/payment/reverse`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|[PaymentAmountToRefund](#schemapaymentamounttorefund)|false|none|The amount and currency of a payment|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|idempotency_key|[WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey](#schemawallettransactionidempotencykey)|true|none|A random key provided by the client, per unique wallet transaction. Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a wallet transaction fails due to a network connection error, then after a minimum delay of one minute, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single wallet transaction is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any transaction that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 24 hours of the first request, from being processed.|
|payment_id|string|true|none|The ID of the payment to reverse|
|reference|string|true|none|A reference for the refund. This must be an alphanumeric string with 6 to 18 characters and must not contain any special characters or spaces.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

|status|[WalletTransactionStatus](#schemawallettransactionstatus)|true|none|The status of the transaction.<br><br>`AUTHORISING`: The transaction is being processed for validation and compliance.<br><br>`INITIATED`: The transaction has been initiated and is currently being processed.<br><br>`EXECUTED`: The transaction has been successfully executed and is considered complete. This is only applicable for debit transactions.<br><br>`SETTLED`: The transaction has settled and funds are available for use. This is only applicable for credit transactions. A transaction will typically settle within seconds to several days, depending on which payment rail is used.<br><br>`FAILED`: The transaction failed to process successfully. This is a terminal status.<br><br>`BLOCKED`: The transaction has been blocked for violating compliance rules. This is a terminal status.|

<h2 id="tocS_PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus">PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentinitiationpaymentstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSpaymentinitiationpaymentstatus"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentinitiationpaymentstatus"></a>

```json
"PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED"
```

The status of the payment.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED`: This is the initial state of all payments. It indicates that the payment is waiting on user input to continue processing. A payment may re-enter this state later on if further input is needed.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED`: The payment has been successfully authorised and accepted by the financial institution but has not been executed.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: The payment has failed due to insufficient funds.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: The payment has failed to be initiated. This error is retryable once the root cause is resolved.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: The payment has been blocked. This is a retryable error.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`: The payment is currently being processed. The payment will automatically exit this state when the financial institution has authorised the transaction.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED`: The payment was cancelled during authorisation.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: The payment has been successfully executed and is considered complete.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: The payment has settled and funds are available for use. Payment settlement can only be guaranteed by using Plaid virtual accounts. A payment will typically settle within seconds to several days, depending on which payment rail is used.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established. This state is only used for standing orders.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: The payment was rejected by the financial institution.

Deprecated:
These statuses will be removed in a future release.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: The payment status is unknown.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`: The payment is currently being processed. The payment will automatically exit this state when processing is complete.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established. This state is only used for standing orders.

<h2 id="tocS_PaymentMeta">PaymentMeta</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentmeta"></a>
<a id="schema_PaymentMeta"></a>
<a id="tocSpaymentmeta"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentmeta"></a>

```json
{
  "by_order_of": "string",
  "payee": "string",
  "payer": "string",
  "payment_method": "string",
  "payment_processor": "string",
  "ppd_id": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "reference_number": "string"
}
```

Transaction information specific to inter-bank transfers. If the transaction was not an inter-bank transfer, all fields will be `null`.

If the `transactions` object was returned by a Transactions endpoint such as `/transactions/get`, the `payment_meta` key will always appear, but no data elements are guaranteed. If the `transactions` object was returned by an Assets endpoint such as `/asset_report/get/` or `/asset_report/pdf/get`, this field will only appear in an Asset Report with Insights.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|by_order_of|string \| null|true|none|The party initiating a wire transfer. Will be `null` if the transaction is not a wire transfer.|
|payee|string \| null|true|none|For transfers, the party that is receiving the transaction.|
|payer|string \| null|true|none|For transfers, the party that is paying the transaction.|
|payment_method|string \| null|true|none|The type of transfer, e.g. 'ACH'|
|payment_processor|string \| null|true|none|The name of the payment processor|
|ppd_id|string \| null|true|none|The ACH PPD ID for the payer.|
|reason|string \| null|true|none|The payer-supplied description of the transfer.|
|reference_number|string \| null|true|none|The transaction reference number supplied by the financial institution.|

```json
"PENDING"
```

The status of the given Payment Profile.

`READY`: This Payment Profile is ready to be used to create transfers using `/transfer/authorization/create` and `/transfer/create`.

`PENDING`: This Payment Profile is not ready to be used. You’ll need to call `/link/token/create` and provide the `payment_profile_token` in the `transfer.payment_profile_token` field to initiate the account linking experience.

`REMOVED`: This Payment Profile has been removed.

<h2 id="tocS_PaymentScheme">PaymentScheme</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentscheme"></a>
<a id="schema_PaymentScheme"></a>
<a id="tocSpaymentscheme"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentscheme"></a>

```json
null
```

Payment scheme. If not specified - the default in the region will be used (e.g. `SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER` for EU). Using unsupported values will result in a failed payment.

`LOCAL_DEFAULT`: The default payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used.

`LOCAL_INSTANT`: The instant payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used (if applicable). Fees may be applied by the institution. If the market does not support an Instant Scheme (e.g. Denmark), the default in the region will be used.

`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER`: The standard payment to a beneficiary within the SEPA area.

`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER_INSTANT`: Instant payment within the SEPA area. May involve additional fees and may not be available at some banks.

```json
  "webhook_type": "string"
```
