Represents a transfer within the Transfers API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|false|none|The Plaid `account_id` corresponding to the end-user account that will be debited or credited.|
|ach_class|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|none|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|amount|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|none|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|cancellable|boolean|true|none|When `true`, you can still cancel this transfer.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|The datetime when this transfer was created. This will be of the form `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`|
|description|string|true|none|The description of the transfer.|
|expected_settlement_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|An estimation of the settlement date which can be useful when the transfer is `pending`. Only set for ACH transfers and is `null` for non-ACH transfers. This will be of the form YYYY-MM-DD.|
|failure_reason|[TransferFailure](#schematransferfailure)|true|none|The failure reason if the event type for a transfer is `"failed"` or `"returned"`. Null value otherwise.|
|funding_account_id|[TransferFundingAccountIDResponse](#schematransferfundingaccountidresponse)|true|none|The id of the funding account to use, available in the Plaid Dashboard. This determines which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited.|
|guarantee_decision|[TransferAuthorizationGuaranteeDecision](#schematransferauthorizationguaranteedecision)|true|none|Indicates whether the transfer is guaranteed by Plaid (Guarantee customers only). This field will contain either `GUARANTEED` or `NOT_GUARANTEED` indicating whether Plaid will guarantee the transfer. If the transfer is not guaranteed, additional information will be provided in the `guarantee_decision_rationale` field. Refer to the `code` field in `guarantee_decision_rationale` for details.|
|guarantee_decision_rationale|[TransferAuthorizationGuaranteeDecisionRationale](#schematransferauthorizationguaranteedecisionrationale)|true|none|The rationale for Plaid's decision to not guarantee a transfer. Will be `null` unless `guarantee_decision` is `NOT_GUARANTEED`.|
|id|[TransferID](#schematransferid)|true|none|Plaid’s unique identifier for a transfer.|
|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The currency of the transfer amount, e.g. "USD"|
|metadata|[TransferMetadata](#schematransfermetadata)|true|none|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|network|[TransferNetwork](#schematransfernetwork)|true|none|The network or rails used for the transfer.<br><br>For transfers submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for same-day is 9:30 AM Pacific Time and the cutoff for next-day transfers is 5:30 PM Pacific Time. It is recommended to submit a transfer at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. Note that both legs of the transfer will be downgraded if applicable.|
|origination_account_id|string|true|none|**Deprecated.** Plaid’s unique identifier for the origination account that was used for this transfer.|
|originator_client_id|string \| null|true|none|The Plaid client ID that is the originator of this transfer. Only present if created on behalf of another client as a third-party sender (TPS).|
|recurring_transfer_id|string \| null|true|none|The id of the recurring transfer if this transfer belongs to a recurring transfer.|
|refunds|[[TransferRefund](#schematransferrefund)]|true|none|A list of refunds associated with this transfer.|
|standard_return_window|string(date) \| null|true|none|The date 3 business days from settlement date indicating the following ACH returns can no longer happen: R01, R02, R03, R29. This will be of the form YYYY-MM-DD.|
|status|[TransferStatus](#schematransferstatus)|true|none|The status of the transfer.<br><br>`pending`: A new transfer was created; it is in the pending state.<br>`posted`: The transfer has been successfully submitted to the payment network.<br>`settled`: Credits are available to be withdrawn or debits have been deducted from the Plaid linked account.<br>`cancelled`: The transfer was cancelled by the client.<br>`failed`: The transfer failed, no funds were moved.<br>`returned`: A posted transfer was returned.|
|sweep_status|[TransferSweepStatus](#schematransfersweepstatus)|false|none|The status of the sweep for the transfer.<br><br>`unswept`: The transfer hasn't been swept yet.<br>`swept`: The transfer was swept to the sweep account.<br>`swept_settled`: Credits are available to be withdrawn or debits have been deducted from the customer’s business checking account.<br>`return_swept`: The transfer was returned, funds were pulled back or pushed back to the sweep account.<br>`null`: The transfer will never be swept (e.g. if the transfer is cancelled or returned before being swept)|
|type|[TransferType](#schematransfertype)|true|none|The type of transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|
|unauthorized_return_window|string(date) \| null|true|none|The date 61 business days from settlement date indicating the following ACH returns can no longer happen: R05, R07, R10, R11, R51, R33, R37, R38, R51, R52, R53. This will be of the form YYYY-MM-DD.|

For example, if a request to create an authorization fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single authorization is created.<br><br>Failure to provide this key may result in duplicate charges.<br><br>Required for guaranteed ACH customers.|

Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. ```


A decision regarding the proposed transfer.

`approved` – The proposed transfer has received the end user's consent and has been approved for processing by Plaid. The `decision_rationale` field is set if Plaid was unable to fetch the account information. You may proceed with the transfer, but further review is recommended (i.e., use Link in update to re-authenticate your user when `decision_rationale.code` is `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED`). Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.

`declined` – Plaid reviewed the proposed transfer and declined processing. Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.

Possible values are:<br><br>`MANUALLY_VERIFIED_ITEM` – Item created via same-day micro deposits, limited information available. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.<br><br>`ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` – Unable to collect the account information due to Item staleness. Can be rectified using Link in update mode. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.<br><br>`PAYMENT_PROFILE_LOGIN_REQUIRED` - Unable to collect the account information due to invalid login when using Payment Profiles. Can be rectified using update mode for Payment Profile. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.<br><br>`ERROR` – Unable to collect the account information due to an error. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.<br><br>`NSF` – Transaction likely to result in a return due to insufficient funds. Plaid will offer `declined` as a transaction decision.<br><br>`RISK` - Transaction is high-risk. Plaid will offer `declined` as a transaction decision.<br><br>`TRANSFER_LIMIT_REACHED` - One or several transfer limits are reached, e.g. monthly transfer limit. Plaid will offer `declined` as a transaction decision.<br><br>`MIGRATED_ACCOUNT_ITEM` - Item created via `/transfer/account_migration` endpoint, limited information available. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.|
|description|string|true|none|A human-readable description of the code associated with a transfer approval or transfer decline.|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferAuthorizationDecisionRationaleCode">TransferAuthorizationDecisionRationaleCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferauthorizationdecisionrationalecode"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferAuthorizationDecisionRationaleCode"></a>
<a id="tocStransferauthorizationdecisionrationalecode"></a>
<a id="tocstransferauthorizationdecisionrationalecode"></a>

```json
"NSF"
```

A code representing the rationale for approving or declining the proposed transfer. Possible values are:

`MANUALLY_VERIFIED_ITEM` – Item created via same-day micro deposits, limited information available. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.

`ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` – Unable to collect the account information due to Item staleness. Can be rectified using Link in update mode. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.

`PAYMENT_PROFILE_LOGIN_REQUIRED` - Unable to collect the account information due to invalid login when using Payment Profiles. Can be rectified using update mode for Payment Profile. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.

`ERROR` – Unable to collect the account information due to an error. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.

`NSF` – Transaction likely to result in a return due to insufficient funds. Plaid will offer `declined` as a transaction decision.

`RISK` - Transaction is high-risk. Plaid will offer `declined` as a transaction decision.

`TRANSFER_LIMIT_REACHED` - One or several transfer limits are reached, e.g. monthly transfer limit. Plaid will offer `declined` as a transaction decision.

`MIGRATED_ACCOUNT_ITEM` - Item created via `/transfer/account_migration` endpoint, limited information available. Plaid will offer `approved` as a transaction decision.

A code representing the reason Plaid declined to guarantee this transfer:

`RETURN_BANK`: The risk of a bank-initiated return (for example, an R01/NSF) is too high to guarantee this transfer.

`RETURN_CUSTOMER`: The risk of a customer-initiated return (for example, a R10/Unauthorized) is too high to guarantee this transfer.

`GUARANTEE_LIMIT_REACHED`: This transfer is low-risk, but Guarantee has exhausted an internal limit on the number or rate of guarantees that applies to this transfer.

`RISK_ESTIMATE_UNAVAILABLE`: A risk estimate is unavailable for this Item.

`REQUIRED_PARAM_MISSING`: Required fields are missing.

Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|

|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The currency of the transfer amount. The default value is "USD".|
|network|string|true|none|The network or rails used for the transfer.|
|origination_account_id|string|true|none|**Deprecated.** Plaid's unique identifier for the origination account that was used for this transfer.|
|originator_client_id|string \| null|true|none|The Plaid client ID that is the originator of this transfer. Only present if created on behalf of another client as a third-party sender (TPS).|
|type|[TransferType](#schematransfertype)|true|none|The type of transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferCreateIdempotencyKey">TransferCreateIdempotencyKey</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransfercreateidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferCreateIdempotencyKey"></a>
<a id="tocStransfercreateidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="tocstransfercreateidempotencykey"></a>

```json
"string"
```

Deprecated. `authorization_id` is now used as idempotency instead.

A random key provided by the client, per unique transfer. Maximum of 50 characters.

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a transfer fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single transfer is created.

Represents an event in the Transfers API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The account ID associated with the transfer.|
|event_id|integer|true|none|Plaid’s unique identifier for this event. IDs are sequential unsigned 64-bit integers.|
|event_type|[TransferEventType](#schematransfereventtype)|true|none|The type of event that this transfer represents.<br><br>`pending`: A new transfer was created; it is in the pending state.<br><br>`cancelled`: The transfer was cancelled by the client.<br><br>`failed`: The transfer failed, no funds were moved.<br><br>`posted`: The transfer has been successfully submitted to the payment network.<br><br>`settled`: Credits are available to be withdrawn or debits have been deducted from the Plaid linked account.<br><br>`returned`: A posted transfer was returned.<br><br>`swept`: The transfer was swept to / from the sweep account.<br><br>`swept_settled`: Credits are available to be withdrawn or debits have been deducted from the customer’s business checking account.<br><br>`return_swept`: Due to the transfer being returned, funds were pulled from or pushed back to the sweep account.|
|failure_reason|[TransferFailure](#schematransferfailure)|true|none|The failure reason if the event type for a transfer is `"failed"` or `"returned"`. Null value otherwise.|
|funding_account_id|[TransferFundingAccountIDResponse](#schematransferfundingaccountidresponse)|true|none|The id of the funding account to use, available in the Plaid Dashboard. This determines which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited.|
|origination_account_id|string \| null|true|none|**Deprecated.** The ID of the origination account that this balance belongs to.|
|originator_client_id|string \| null|true|none|The Plaid client ID that is the originator of the transfer that this event applies to. Only present if the transfer was created on behalf of another client as a third-party sender (TPS).|
|refund_id|string \| null|true|none|Plaid’s unique identifier for a refund. A non-null value indicates the event is for the associated refund of the transfer.|
|sweep_amount|[TransferSweepAmount](#schematransfersweepamount)|true|none|A signed amount of how much was `swept` or `return_swept` (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "-5.50").|
|sweep_id|[TransferSweepID](#schematransfersweepid)|true|none|Plaid’s unique identifier for a sweep.|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|true|none|The datetime when this event occurred. This will be of the form `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.|
|transfer_amount|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|none|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|transfer_id|[TransferID](#schematransferid)|true|none|Plaid’s unique identifier for a transfer.|
|transfer_type|[TransferType](#schematransfertype)|true|none|The type of transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|

|event_type|swept|

|event_type|return_swept|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferEventType">TransferEventType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransfereventtype"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferEventType"></a>
<a id="tocStransfereventtype"></a>
<a id="tocstransfereventtype"></a>

```json
"pending"
```

The type of event that this transfer represents.

`pending`: A new transfer was created; it is in the pending state.

`cancelled`: The transfer was cancelled by the client.

`failed`: The transfer failed, no funds were moved.

`posted`: The transfer has been successfully submitted to the payment network.

`settled`: Credits are available to be withdrawn or debits have been deducted from the Plaid linked account.

`returned`: A posted transfer was returned.

`swept`: The transfer was swept to / from the sweep account.

`swept_settled`: Credits are available to be withdrawn or debits have been deducted from the customer’s business checking account.

`return_swept`: Due to the transfer being returned, funds were pulled from or pushed back to the sweep account.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferIntentAuthorizationDecision">TransferIntentAuthorizationDecision</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferintentauthorizationdecision"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferIntentAuthorizationDecision"></a>
<a id="tocStransferintentauthorizationdecision"></a>
<a id="tocstransferintentauthorizationdecision"></a>

```json
"APPROVED"
```


A decision regarding the proposed transfer.

`APPROVED` – The proposed transfer has received the end user's consent and has been approved for processing by Plaid. The `decision_rationale` field is set if Plaid was unable to fetch the account information. You may proceed with the transfer, but further review is recommended (i.e., use Link in update to re-authenticate your user when `decision_rationale.code` is `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED`). Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.

`DECLINED` – Plaid reviewed the proposed transfer and declined processing. Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.

Represents a transfer intent within Transfer UI.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string \| null|false|none|The Plaid `account_id` corresponding to the end-user account that will be debited or credited. Returned only if `account_id` was set on intent creation.|
|ach_class|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|none|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|amount|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|none|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|The datetime the transfer was created. This will be of the form `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.|
|description|string|true|none|A description for the underlying transfer. Maximum of 8 characters.|
|funding_account_id|[TransferFundingAccountIDResponse](#schematransferfundingaccountidresponse)|true|none|The id of the funding account to use, available in the Plaid Dashboard. This determines which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited.|
|id|string|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for the transfer intent object.|
|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The currency of the transfer amount, e.g. "USD"|
|metadata|[TransferMetadata](#schematransfermetadata)|false|none|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|mode|[TransferIntentCreateMode](#schematransferintentcreatemode)|true|none|The direction of the flow of transfer funds.<br><br>`PAYMENT`: Transfers funds from an end user's account to your business account.<br><br>`DISBURSEMENT`: Transfers funds from your business account to an end user's account.|
|network|[TransferIntentCreateNetwork](#schematransferintentcreatenetwork)|false|none|The network or rails used for the transfer. Defaults to `same-day-ach`.<br><br>For transfers submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for same-day is 9:30 AM Pacific Time and the cutoff for next-day transfers is 5:30 PM Pacific Time. It is recommended to submit a transfer at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. Note that both legs of the transfer will be downgraded if applicable.|
|origination_account_id|string|true|none|**Deprecated.** Plaid’s unique identifier for the origination account for the intent. If not provided, the default account will be used.|
|require_guarantee|boolean \| null|false|none|When `true`, the transfer requires a `GUARANTEED` decision by Plaid to proceed (Guarantee customers only).|
|status|[TransferIntentStatus](#schematransferintentstatus)|true|none|The status of the transfer intent.<br><br>`PENDING`: The transfer intent is pending.<br>`SUCCEEDED`: The transfer intent was successfully created.<br>`FAILED`: The transfer intent was unable to be created.|
|user|[TransferUserInResponse](#schematransferuserinresponse)|true|none|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|

|mode|DISBURSEMENT|

```json
"PAYMENT"
```

The direction of the flow of transfer funds.

`PAYMENT`: Transfers funds from an end user's account to your business account.

`DISBURSEMENT`: Transfers funds from your business account to an end user's account.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferIntentCreateNetwork">TransferIntentCreateNetwork</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferintentcreatenetwork"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferIntentCreateNetwork"></a>
<a id="tocStransferintentcreatenetwork"></a>
<a id="tocstransferintentcreatenetwork"></a>

```json
"same-day-ach"
```

The network or rails used for the transfer. Defaults to `same-day-ach`.

For transfers submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for same-day is 9:30 AM Pacific Time and the cutoff for next-day transfers is 5:30 PM Pacific Time. It is recommended to submit a transfer at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. Note that both legs of the transfer will be downgraded if applicable.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string \| null|false|none|The Plaid `account_id` for the account that will be debited or credited. Returned only if `account_id` was set on intent creation.|
|ach_class|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|none|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|amount|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|none|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|authorization_decision|[TransferIntentAuthorizationDecision](#schematransferintentauthorizationdecision)|true|none|<br>A decision regarding the proposed transfer.<br><br>`APPROVED` – The proposed transfer has received the end user's consent and has been approved for processing by Plaid. The `decision_rationale` field is set if Plaid was unable to fetch the account information. You may proceed with the transfer, but further review is recommended (i.e., use Link in update to re-authenticate your user when `decision_rationale.code` is `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED`). Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.<br><br>`DECLINED` – Plaid reviewed the proposed transfer and declined processing. Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.|
|authorization_decision_rationale|[TransferAuthorizationDecisionRationale](#schematransferauthorizationdecisionrationale)|true|none|The rationale for Plaid's decision regarding a proposed transfer. It is always set for `declined` decisions, and may or may not be null for `approved` decisions.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|The datetime the transfer was created. This will be of the form `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.|
|description|string|true|none|A description for the underlying transfer. Maximum of 8 characters.|
|failure_reason|[TransferIntentGetFailureReason](#schematransferintentgetfailurereason)|true|none|The reason for a failed transfer intent. Returned only if the transfer intent status is `failed`. Null otherwise.|
|funding_account_id|[TransferFundingAccountIDResponse](#schematransferfundingaccountidresponse)|true|none|The id of the funding account to use, available in the Plaid Dashboard. This determines which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited.|
|guarantee_decision|[TransferAuthorizationGuaranteeDecision](#schematransferauthorizationguaranteedecision)|true|none|Indicates whether the transfer is guaranteed by Plaid (Guarantee customers only). This field will contain either `GUARANTEED` or `NOT_GUARANTEED` indicating whether Plaid will guarantee the transfer. If the transfer is not guaranteed, additional information will be provided in the `guarantee_decision_rationale` field. Refer to the `code` field in `guarantee_decision_rationale` for details.|
|guarantee_decision_rationale|[TransferAuthorizationGuaranteeDecisionRationale](#schematransferauthorizationguaranteedecisionrationale)|true|none|The rationale for Plaid's decision to not guarantee a transfer. Will be `null` unless `guarantee_decision` is `NOT_GUARANTEED`.|
|id|string|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for a transfer intent object.|
|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The currency of the transfer amount, e.g. "USD"|
|metadata|[TransferMetadata](#schematransfermetadata)|false|none|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|mode|[TransferIntentCreateMode](#schematransferintentcreatemode)|true|none|The direction of the flow of transfer funds.<br><br>`PAYMENT`: Transfers funds from an end user's account to your business account.<br><br>`DISBURSEMENT`: Transfers funds from your business account to an end user's account.|
|network|[TransferIntentCreateNetwork](#schematransferintentcreatenetwork)|false|none|The network or rails used for the transfer. Defaults to `same-day-ach`.<br><br>For transfers submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for same-day is 9:30 AM Pacific Time and the cutoff for next-day transfers is 5:30 PM Pacific Time. It is recommended to submit a transfer at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. Note that both legs of the transfer will be downgraded if applicable.|
|origination_account_id|string|true|none|**Deprecated.** Plaid’s unique identifier for the origination account used for the transfer.|
|require_guarantee|boolean \| null|false|none|When `true`, the transfer requires a `GUARANTEED` decision by Plaid to proceed (Guarantee customers only).|
|status|[TransferIntentStatus](#schematransferintentstatus)|true|none|The status of the transfer intent.<br><br>`PENDING`: The transfer intent is pending.<br>`SUCCEEDED`: The transfer intent was successfully created.<br>`FAILED`: The transfer intent was unable to be created.|
|transfer_id|string \| null|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for the transfer created through the UI. Returned only if the transfer was successfully created. Null value otherwise.|
|user|[TransferUserInResponse](#schematransferuserinresponse)|true|none|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferNetwork">TransferNetwork</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransfernetwork"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferNetwork"></a>
<a id="tocStransfernetwork"></a>
<a id="tocstransfernetwork"></a>

```json
"ach"
```

The network or rails used for the transfer.

For transfers submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for same-day is 9:30 AM Pacific Time and the cutoff for next-day transfers is 5:30 PM Pacific Time. It is recommended to submit a transfer at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. Note that both legs of the transfer will be downgraded if applicable.

Defines the request schema for `/transfer/recurring/create`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_token|[TransferAccessToken](#schematransferaccesstoken)|true|none|The Plaid `access_token` for the account that will be debited or credited. Required if not using `payment_profile_token`.|
|account_id|[TransferAccountID](#schematransferaccountid)|true|none|The Plaid `account_id` corresponding to the end-user account that will be debited or credited. Returned only if `account_id` was set on intent creation.|
|ach_class|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|none|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network.<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - the transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer, eg. bill payment<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry - debits from a consumer’s account where their authorization is obtained over the Internet|
|amount|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|none|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|description|string|true|none|The description of the recurring transfer.|
|device|[TransferDevice](#schematransferdevice)|true|none|Information about the device being used to initiate the authorization.|
|funding_account_id|[TransferFundingAccountIDRequest](#schematransferfundingaccountidrequest)|false|none|The id of the funding account to use, available in the Plaid Dashboard. This determines which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited. Defaults to the account configured during onboarding.|
|idempotency_key|[TransferRecurringIdempotencyKey](#schematransferrecurringidempotencykey)|true|none|A random key provided by the client, per unique recurring transfer. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a recurring fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single recurring transfer is created.|
|iso_currency_code|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** The currency of the transfer amount. The default value is "USD".|
|network|[TransferNetwork](#schematransfernetwork)|true|none|The network or rails used for the transfer.<br><br>For transfers submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for same-day is 9:30 AM Pacific Time and the cutoff for next-day transfers is 5:30 PM Pacific Time. It is recommended to submit a transfer at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any transfer that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the same-day cutoff, but is submitted in time for the next-day cutoff, will be sent over next-day rails and will not incur same-day charges. Note that both legs of the transfer will be downgraded if applicable.|
|schedule|[TransferRecurringSchedule](#schematransferrecurringschedule)|true|none|The schedule that the recurring transfer will be executed on.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|test_clock_id|string \| null|false|none|Plaid’s unique identifier for a test clock.|
|type|[TransferType](#schematransfertype)|true|none|The type of transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|
|user|[TransferUserInRequest](#schematransferuserinrequest)|true|none|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|
|user_present|boolean \| null|true|none|If the end user is initiating the specific transfer themselves via an interactive UI, this should be `true`; for automatic recurring payments where the end user is not actually initiating each individual transfer, it should be `false`.|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferRecurringSchedule">TransferRecurringSchedule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferrecurringschedule"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferRecurringSchedule"></a>
<a id="tocStransferrecurringschedule"></a>
<a id="tocstransferrecurringschedule"></a>

```json
{
  "end_date": "1970-01-01",
  "interval_count": 0,
  "interval_execution_day": 0,
  "interval_unit": "week",
  "start_date": "1970-01-01"
}
```

The schedule that the recurring transfer will be executed on.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|end_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|A date in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD). The recurring transfer will end on the last `interval_execution_day` on or before the `end_date`.<br>If the `interval_execution_day` between the start date and the end date (inclusive) is also the same day that `/transfer/recurring/create` was called, the bank *may* make a payment on that day, but it is not guaranteed to do so.|
|interval_count|[TransferScheduleIntervalCount](#schematransferscheduleintervalcount)|true|none|The number of recurring `interval_units` between originations. The recurring interval(before holiday adjustment) is calculated by multiplying `interval_unit` and `interval_count`.<br>For instance, to schedule a recurring transfer which originates once every two weeks, set `interval_unit` = `week` and `interval_count` = 2.|
|interval_execution_day|integer|true|none|The day of the interval on which to schedule the transfer.<br><br>If the `interval_unit` is `week`, `interval_execution_day` should be an integer from 1 (Monday) to 5 (Friday).<br><br>If the `interval_unit` is `month`, `interval_execution_day` should be an integer indicating which day of the month to make the transfer on. Integers from 1 to 28 can be used to make a transfer on that day of the month. Negative integers from -1 to -5 can be used to make a transfer relative to the end of the month. To make a transfer on the last day of the month, use -1; to make the transfer on the second-to-last day, use -2, and so on.<br><br>The transfer will be originated on next available banking day if the designated day is a non banking day.|
|interval_unit|[TransferScheduleIntervalUnit](#schematransferscheduleintervalunit)|true|none|The unit of the recurring interval.|
|start_date|string(date)|true|none|A date in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD). The recurring transfer will begin on the first `interval_execution_day` on or after the `start_date`.<br><br>If the first `interval_execution_day` on or after the start date is also the same day that `/transfer/recurring/create` was called, the bank *may* make the first payment on that day, but it is not guaranteed to do so.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|interval_unit|week|
|interval_unit|month|

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. A repayment is created automatically after one or more guaranteed transactions receive a return. If there are multiple eligible returns in a day, they are batched together into a single repayment.

Repayments are sent over ACH, with funds typically available on the next banking day.

|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The currency of the repayment, e.g. "USD".|
|repayment_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the repayment.|

The status of the transfer.

`pending`: A new transfer was created; it is in the pending state.
`posted`: The transfer has been successfully submitted to the payment network.
`settled`: Credits are available to be withdrawn or debits have been deducted from the Plaid linked account.
`cancelled`: The transfer was cancelled by the client.
`failed`: The transfer failed, no funds were moved.
`returned`: A posted transfer was returned.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferSweep">TransferSweep</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransfersweep"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferSweep"></a>
<a id="tocStransfersweep"></a>
<a id="tocstransfersweep"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": "string",
  "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "funding_account_id": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "settled": "1970-01-01"
}
```

Describes a sweep of funds to / from the sweep account.

A sweep is associated with many sweep events (events of type `swept` or `return_swept`) which can be retrieved by invoking the `/transfer/event/list` endpoint with the corresponding `sweep_id`.

`swept` events occur when the transfer amount is credited or debited from your sweep account, depending on the `type` of the transfer. `return_swept` events occur when a transfer is returned and Plaid undoes the credit or debit.

The total sum of the `swept` and `return_swept` events is equal to the `amount` of the sweep Plaid creates and matches the amount of the entry on your sweep account ledger.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|string|true|none|Signed decimal amount of the sweep as it appears on your sweep account ledger (e.g. "-10.00")<br><br>If amount is not present, the sweep was net-settled to zero and outstanding debits and credits between the sweep account and Plaid are balanced.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|The datetime when the sweep occurred, in RFC 3339 format.|
|funding_account_id|[TransferFundingAccountIDResponse](#schematransferfundingaccountidresponse)|true|none|The id of the funding account to use, available in the Plaid Dashboard. This determines which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited.|
|id|string|true|none|Identifier of the sweep.|
|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The currency of the sweep, e.g. "USD".|
|settled|string(date) \| null|true|none|The date when the sweep settled, in the YYYY-MM-DD format.|

<a id="tocStransfersweepamount"></a>
<a id="tocstransfersweepamount"></a>

```json
"string"
```

A signed amount of how much was `swept` or `return_swept` (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "-5.50").

Custom test accounts are configured with a JSON configuration object formulated according to the schema below. All top level fields are optional. Sending an empty object as a configuration will result in an account configured with random balances and transaction history.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|force_error|string|true|none|An error code to force on Item creation. Possible values are:<br><br>`"INSTITUTION_NOT_RESPONDING"`<br>`"INSTITUTION_NO_LONGER_SUPPORTED"`<br>`"INVALID_CREDENTIALS"`<br>`"INVALID_MFA"`<br>`"ITEM_LOCKED"`<br>`"ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED"`<br>`"ITEM_NOT_SUPPORTED"`<br>`"INVALID_LINK_TOKEN"`<br>`"MFA_NOT_SUPPORTED"`<br>`"NO_ACCOUNTS"`<br>`"PLAID_ERROR"`<br>`"USER_INPUT_TIMEOUT"`<br>`"USER_SETUP_REQUIRED"`|
|mfa|[MFA](#schemamfa)|true|none|Specifies the multi-factor authentication settings to use with this test account|
|override_accounts|[[OverrideAccounts](#schemaoverrideaccounts)]|true|none|An array of account overrides to configure the accounts for the Item. By default, if no override is specified, transactions and account data will be randomly generated based on the account type and subtype, and other products will have fixed or empty data.|
|recaptcha|string|true|none|You may trigger a reCAPTCHA in Plaid Link in the Sandbox environment by using the recaptcha field. Possible values are `good` or `bad`. A value of `good` will result in successful Item creation and `bad` will result in a `RECAPTCHA_BAD` error to simulate a failed reCAPTCHA. Both values require the reCAPTCHA to be manually solved within Plaid Link.|
|seed|string|true|none|A seed, in the form of a string, that will be used to randomly generate account and transaction data, if this data is not specified using the `override_accounts` argument. If no seed is specified, the randomly generated data will be different each time.<br><br>Note that transactions data is generated relative to the Item's creation date. Different Items created on different dates with the same seed for transactions data will have different dates for the transactions. The number of days between each transaction and the Item creation will remain constant. For example, an Item created on December 15 might show a transaction on December 14. An Item created on December 20, using the same seed, would show that same transaction occurring on December 19.|
|version|string \| null|false|none|The version of the password schema to use, possible values are 1 or 2. The default value is 2. You should only specify 1 if you know it is necessary for your test suite.|

<h2 id="tocS_UserPermissionRevokedWebhook">UserPermissionRevokedWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemauserpermissionrevokedwebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_UserPermissionRevokedWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSuserpermissionrevokedwebhook"></a>
<a id="tocsuserpermissionrevokedwebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "environment": "development",
  "error": {
    "causes": [
      null
    ],
    "display_message": "string",
    "documentation_url": "string",
    "error_code": "string",
    "error_message": "string",
    "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "request_id": "string",
    "status": 0,
    "suggested_action": "string"
  },
  "item_id": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "webhook_type": "string"
}
```

The `USER_PERMISSION_REVOKED` webhook is fired when an end user has used either the [my.plaid.com portal](https://my.plaid.com) or the financial institution’s consent portal to revoke the permission that they previously granted to access an Item. Once access to an Item has been revoked, it cannot be restored. If the user subsequently returns to your application, a new Item must be created for the user.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`USER_PERMISSION_REVOKED`|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`ITEM`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|development|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

<a id="tocsverificationrefreshstatus"></a>

```json
"VERIFICATION_REFRESH_STATUS_USER_PRESENCE_REQUIRED"
```

The verification refresh status. One of the following:

`"VERIFICATION_REFRESH_STATUS_USER_PRESENCE_REQUIRED"` User presence is required to refresh an income verification.
`"VERIFICATION_REFRESH_SUCCESSFUL"` The income verification refresh was successful.
`"VERIFICATION_REFRESH_NOT_FOUND"` No new data was found after the income verification refresh.

<h2 id="tocS_VerificationStatus">VerificationStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaverificationstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_VerificationStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSverificationstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsverificationstatus"></a>

```json
"VERIFIED"
```

The verification status. One of the following:

`"VERIFIED"`: The information was successfully verified.

`"UNVERIFIED"`: The verification has not yet been performed.

`"NEEDS_INFO"`: The verification was attempted but could not be completed due to missing information.

"`UNABLE_TO_VERIFY`": The verification was performed and the information could not be verified.

`"UNKNOWN"`: The verification status is unknown.

The transaction details

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|[WalletTransactionAmount](#schemawallettransactionamount)|true|none|The amount and currency of a transaction|
|counterparty|[WalletTransactionCounterparty](#schemawallettransactioncounterparty)|true|none|An object representing the e-wallet transaction's counterparty|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the transaction was created, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|last_status_update|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time of the last time the `status` was updated, in IS0 8601 format|
|payment_id|string \| null|false|none|The payment id that this transaction is associated with, if any. This is present only for transaction types `PIS_PAY_IN` and `REFUND`.|
|reference|string|true|none|A reference for the transaction|
|status|[WalletTransactionStatus](#schemawallettransactionstatus)|true|none|The status of the transaction.<br><br>`AUTHORISING`: The transaction is being processed for validation and compliance.<br><br>`INITIATED`: The transaction has been initiated and is currently being processed.<br><br>`EXECUTED`: The transaction has been successfully executed and is considered complete. This is only applicable for debit transactions.<br><br>`SETTLED`: The transaction has settled and funds are available for use. This is only applicable for credit transactions. A transaction will typically settle within seconds to several days, depending on which payment rail is used.<br><br>`FAILED`: The transaction failed to process successfully. This is a terminal status.<br><br>`BLOCKED`: The transaction has been blocked for violating compliance rules. This is a terminal status.|
|transaction_id|string|true|none|A unique ID identifying the transaction|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the transaction. The supported transaction types that are returned are:<br>`BANK_TRANSFER:` a transaction which credits an e-wallet through an external bank transfer.<br><br>`PAYOUT:` a transaction which debits an e-wallet by disbursing funds to a counterparty.<br><br>`PIS_PAY_IN:` a payment which credits an e-wallet through Plaid's Payment Initiation Services (PIS) APIs. For more information see the [Payment Initiation endpoints](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/payment-initiation/).<br><br>`REFUND:` a transaction which debits an e-wallet by refunding a previously initiated payment made through Plaid's [PIS APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/payment-initiation/).<br><br>`FUNDS_SWEEP`: an automated transaction which debits funds from an e-wallet to a designated client-owned account.|
|wallet_id|string|true|none|The EMI (E-Money Institution) wallet that this payment is associated with, if any. This wallet is used as an intermediary account to enable Plaid to reconcile the settlement of funds for Payment Initiation requests.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|AUTHORISING|
|status|INITIATED|
|status|EXECUTED|
|status|SETTLED|
|status|BLOCKED|
|status|FAILED|
|type|BANK_TRANSFER|
|type|PAYOUT|
|type|PIS_PAY_IN|
|type|REFUND|
|type|FUNDS_SWEEP|

WalletTransactionExecuteRequest defines the request schema for `/wallet/transaction/execute`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|[WalletTransactionAmount](#schemawallettransactionamount)|true|none|The amount and currency of a transaction|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|counterparty|[WalletTransactionCounterparty](#schemawallettransactioncounterparty)|true|none|An object representing the e-wallet transaction's counterparty|
|idempotency_key|[WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey](#schemawallettransactionidempotencykey)|true|none|A random key provided by the client, per unique wallet transaction. Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a wallet transaction fails due to a network connection error, then after a minimum delay of one minute, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single wallet transaction is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any transaction that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 24 hours of the first request, from being processed.|
|reference|string|true|none|A reference for the transaction. This must be an alphanumeric string with 6 to 18 characters and must not contain any special characters or spaces.<br>Ensure that the `reference` field is unique for each transaction.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|wallet_id|string|true|none|The ID of the e-wallet to debit from|

<h2 id="tocS_WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey">WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawallettransactionidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="schema_WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey"></a>
<a id="tocSwallettransactionidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="tocswallettransactionidempotencykey"></a>

```json
"string"
```

A random key provided by the client, per unique wallet transaction. Maximum of 128 characters.

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a wallet transaction fails due to a network connection error, then after a minimum delay of one minute, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single wallet transaction is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any transaction that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 24 hours of the first request, from being processed.

<h2 id="tocS_WalletTransactionStatus">WalletTransactionStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawallettransactionstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_WalletTransactionStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSwallettransactionstatus"></a>
<a id="tocswallettransactionstatus"></a>

```json
"AUTHORISING"
```

The status of the transaction.

`AUTHORISING`: The transaction is being processed for validation and compliance.

`INITIATED`: The transaction has been initiated and is currently being processed.

`EXECUTED`: The transaction has been successfully executed and is considered complete. This is only applicable for debit transactions.

`SETTLED`: The transaction has settled and funds are available for use. This is only applicable for credit transactions. A transaction will typically settle within seconds to several days, depending on which payment rail is used.

`FAILED`: The transaction failed to process successfully. This is a terminal status.

`BLOCKED`: The transaction has been blocked for violating compliance rules. This is a terminal status.

A program that configures the active lists, search parameters, and other behavior for initial and ongoing screening of entities.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audit_trail|[WatchlistScreeningAuditTrail](#schemawatchlistscreeningaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|id|[EntityWatchlistProgramID](#schemaentitywatchlistprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated entity program.|
|is_archived|[ProgramArchived](#schemaprogramarchived)|true|none|Archived programs are read-only and cannot screen new customers nor participate in ongoing monitoring.|
|is_rescanning_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicator specifying whether the program is enabled and will perform daily rescans.|
|lists_enabled|[[EntityWatchlistCode](#schemaentitywatchlistcode)]|true|none|Watchlists enabled for the associated program|
|name|[EntityWatchlistScreeningProgramName](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeningprogramname)|true|none|A name for the entity program to define its purpose. For example, "High Risk Organizations" or "Applicants".|
|name_sensitivity|[ProgramNameSensitivity](#schemaprogramnamesensitivity)|true|none|The valid name matching sensitivity configurations for a screening program. Note that while certain matching techniques may be more prevalent on less strict settings, all matching algorithms are enabled for every sensitivity.<br><br>`coarse` - See more potential matches. This sensitivity will see more broad phonetic matches across alphabets that make missing a potential hit very unlikely. This setting is noisier and will require more manual review.<br><br>`balanced` - A good default for most companies. This sensitivity is balanced to show high quality hits with reduced noise.<br><br>`strict` - Aggressive false positive reduction. This sensitivity will require names to be more similar than `coarse` and `balanced` settings, relying less on phonetics, while still accounting for character transpositions, missing tokens, and other common permutations.<br><br>`exact` - Matches must be nearly exact. This sensitivity will only show hits with exact or nearly exact name matches with only basic correction such as extraneous symbols and capitalization. This setting is generally not recommended unless you have a very specific use case.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

|lists_enabled|EU_CON|

|lists_enabled|IZ_UNC|
|lists_enabled|IZ_WBK|
|lists_enabled|US_CAP|
|lists_enabled|US_FSE|
|lists_enabled|US_MBS|
|lists_enabled|US_SDN|
|lists_enabled|US_SSI|
|lists_enabled|US_CMC|

|lists_enabled|AU_CON|
|lists_enabled|UK_HMC|
|name_sensitivity|coarse|
|name_sensitivity|balanced|
|name_sensitivity|strict|
|name_sensitivity|exact|

### Properties

All watchlist screening hits begin in a `pending_review` state but can be changed by creating a review. When a hit is in the `pending_review` state, it will always show the latest version of the watchlist data Plaid has available and be compared against the latest customer information saved in the watchlist screening. Once a hit has been marked as `confirmed` or `dismissed` it will no longer be updated so that the state is as it was when the review was first conducted.|
|source_uid|[SourceUID](#schemasourceuid)|true|none|The identifier provided by the source sanction or watchlist. When one is not provided by the source, this is `null`.|

The current state of review. All watchlist screening hits begin in a `pending_review` state but can be changed by creating a review. When a hit is in the `pending_review` state, it will always show the latest version of the watchlist data Plaid has available and be compared against the latest customer information saved in the watchlist screening. Once a hit has been marked as `confirmed` or `dismissed` it will no longer be updated so that the state is as it was when the review was first conducted.

A program that configures the active lists, search parameters, and other behavior for initial and ongoing screening of individuals.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audit_trail|[WatchlistScreeningAuditTrail](#schemawatchlistscreeningaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|id|[WatchlistProgramID](#schemawatchlistprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated program.|
|is_archived|[ProgramArchived](#schemaprogramarchived)|true|none|Archived programs are read-only and cannot screen new customers nor participate in ongoing monitoring.|
|is_rescanning_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicator specifying whether the program is enabled and will perform daily rescans.|
|lists_enabled|[[IndividualWatchlistCode](#schemaindividualwatchlistcode)]|true|none|Watchlists enabled for the associated program|
|name|[IndividualWatchlistScreeningProgramName](#schemaindividualwatchlistscreeningprogramname)|true|none|A name for the program to define its purpose. For example, "High Risk Individuals", "US Cardholders", or "Applicants".|
|name_sensitivity|[ProgramNameSensitivity](#schemaprogramnamesensitivity)|true|none|The valid name matching sensitivity configurations for a screening program. Note that while certain matching techniques may be more prevalent on less strict settings, all matching algorithms are enabled for every sensitivity.<br><br>`coarse` - See more potential matches. This sensitivity will see more broad phonetic matches across alphabets that make missing a potential hit very unlikely. This setting is noisier and will require more manual review.<br><br>`balanced` - A good default for most companies. This sensitivity is balanced to show high quality hits with reduced noise.<br><br>`strict` - Aggressive false positive reduction. This sensitivity will require names to be more similar than `coarse` and `balanced` settings, relying less on phonetics, while still accounting for character transpositions, missing tokens, and other common permutations.<br><br>`exact` - Matches must be nearly exact. This sensitivity will only show hits with exact or nearly exact name matches with only basic correction such as extraneous symbols and capitalization. This setting is generally not recommended unless you have a very specific use case.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

A review submitted by a team member for an individual watchlist screening. A review can be either a comment on the current screening state, actions taken
against hits attached to the watchlist screening, or both.

|confirmed_hits|[[WatchlistScreeningHitID](#schemawatchlistscreeninghitid)]|true|none|Hits marked as a true positive after thorough manual review. These hits will never recur or be updated once dismissed. In most cases, confirmed hits indicate that the customer should be rejected.|
|dismissed_hits|[[WatchlistScreeningHitID](#schemawatchlistscreeninghitid)]|true|none|Hits marked as a false positive after thorough manual review. These hits will never recur or be updated once dismissed.|
|id|[WatchlistScreeningReviewID](#schemawatchlistscreeningreviewid)|true|none|ID of the associated review.|

An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
